The SNA Coordinator will be involved in all aspects of supporting and leading humanitarian coordination activities for the Syrian NGO Alliance based in Syria Damascus.

**TASKS and RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Internal**

The SNA secretariat Coordinator is responsible for facilitating coordination between the SNA members to serve the SNA mandate, including the sharing of information between members and external stakeholders according to guidelines set out by the SNA.

The SNA secretariat Coordinator is also responsible for the general management of the SNA secretariat and the support services that are provided through this structure, including the day-to-day management of the SNA staff (If any)

Day-to-day management of grants, and budget, ensuring timely reporting

Facilitate and draft strategic planning and Operational planning under the supervision of the steering committee

Implement all operational plans approved by the General assembly

Coordinate and facilitate all periodical meetings for the steering committee and the General assembly

Engage in the identification of new potential SNGO members

Draft advocacy messages under the supervision of the steering committee

Organize and coordinate press conferences and other events related to the SNA work.

To act as the spoken person for the SNA on all media platforms

Follow up with all consultants and advisors assigned to work with the SNA.

Supervise the drafting and finalizing of the Annual report and other communication materials for the SNA

Respect and apply all the PSEAH principles and highly commit to reporting any SEA action.

**External**

Represent and participate effectively in all national forums, committees, and Groups that the SNA has a seat on, such as (ICCG, SSG, SIRF, NFO forum, Donors…etc.) this includes reporting back to the SNA

Represent and participate effectively in all National and international events and workshops concerning the SNA mandate such as the Brussels conference

· Work to ensure effective collaboration among UN, international, and Syrian NGOs

**Note:** the above-mentioned vital responsibilities/accountabilities are illustrative ones. Other future responsibilities/accountability may be assigned to the job depending on the department’s organizational

**COMPETENCIES REQUIRED**
**Technical competencies**: Stakeholder Relationship Management, Surveys Tools, Team Coordination, Microsoft Office Suite Proficiency (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook), Presentation Skills, Effective Meeting Skills, Conflict Management, Emotional Intelligence, Flexibility, Negotiation

**Core competencies**: Professionalism, Respect for Diversity, Planning and Organizing, Stakeholders Orientation

**Managerial competencies:** Building trust, empowering others, Managing performance

**Additional Requirements**

Minimum 7 years of related experience in NGOs or INGOs.

Fluency in English and Arabic.

Ability to travel abroad.

University degree in a relevant field.

jobs.title: Oficial de Recuperación Económica (Medios de Vida) - Guasdualito
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Recuperación Económica (Medios de Vida)** altamente calificado con sede en **Guasdualito, Edo. Apure.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, Zulia y La Guaira. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo del cargo**

Bajo la supervisión del/la Team Leader de Recuperación Económica o del Gerente de Recuperación Económica, el/la Oficial de Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades del componente de medios de vida de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela. Esto incluye el acompañamiento técnico en terreno para el fortalecimiento de emprendedores y micronegocios en comunidades vulnerables, expuestas a riesgos de protección y desastres, así como el desarrollo de habilidades blandas para emprender, la integración del enfoque verde en sus modelos de negocio y su articulación con oportunidades de mercado. Asimismo, el/la Oficial facilitará la transferencia de metodologías de formación a socios locales a través de metodologías desarrolladas por DRC, y garantizará la correcta recopilación de los medios de verificación necesarios para el seguimiento y la rendición de cuentas.

El/la Oficial promoverá una programación integrada y articulada con los equipos de Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres, asegurando intervenciones intersectoriales y de calidad en todas las etapas del proyecto. Además, será responsable de coordinar efectivamente con el equipo de Recuperación Económica y socios locales, y de asegurar el cumplimiento del plan de acción establecido.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Identificación de actividades propias del sector de Medios de Vida**

- Liderar diagnósticos socioeconómicos y de mercado para identificar cadenas productivas, ecosistemas de actores claves del sector público y privado, y oportunidades de inclusión financiera (instituciones, banca, sector privado) que fomenten la autosuficiencia y resiliencia de las Personas de Interés (PDI).
- Evaluar la viabilidad técnica, social, ambiental y económica de propuestas productivas, asegurando que los proyectos de medios de vida sean sostenibles, pertinentes culturalmente y sensibles a los riesgos de protección y desastres.
- Contribuir con datos del contexto local para el ajuste y formulación de propuestas, garantizando la integración del enfoque de Recuperación Económica con otros sectores (Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres).
- Con el apoyo y la orientación de su supervisor y coordinación técnica, sugerir ideas innovadoras y técnicas adecuadas para las intervenciones de Recuperación Económica en función del contexto.

**Implementación técnica y logística**

- Responsable de implementar la planificación, ejecución, seguimiento y cierre técnico de las actividades de medios de vida (focalización, diagnósticos, selección, formación, entregas, encuestas PDM, líneas base/salida y gestión de bases de datos), en coordinación con el Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación económica, y con los equipos de Logística y finanzas para asegurar el cumplimiento del plan de acción y el reporte oportuno de los indicadores propuestos.
- Diseñar e implementar procesos de formación en planes de negocios, medios de vida verdes, orientación vocacional, habilidades blandas, planes de marketing, estructuras de costos, gestión y educación financiera, mediante metodologías híbridas que incluyen plataformas digitales (Moodle). Entre las actividades se contempla la facilitación directa, la Formación a Formadores (ToT) para socios y la gestión logística/financiera necesaria para su ejecución.
- Con la orientación técnica de la coordinación de Recuperación Económica, en conjunto con la supervisión del Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación Económica, ser el punto focal de alianzas estratégicas con actores del sector privado, público o institucional para actividades propias de medios de vida, como lo pueden ser alianzas estratégicas para emprendedores.
- Realizar planes de seguimiento a las PdI relacionados al incremento de su productividad y de medición de indicadores establecidos en el programa de Recuperación Económica.
- Identificar, coordinar y entregar apoyos en especie (como insumos productivos, herramientas, equipos, etc.) de acuerdo con las necesidades socioeconómicas y productivas identificadas, así como con los lineamientos técnicos de la coordinación y el enfoque de protección.
- Participar en la preparación de informes mensuales/trimestrales/anuales aportando análisis técnicos sobre el componente y las actividades realizadas, así como en la orientación técnica para elaborar presupuestos de este componente en formulaciones de proyectos.
- Transferir conocimientos, acompañar, hacer seguimiento sobre la implementación de programas de Recuperación Económica implementadas por organizaciones locales, utilizando metodologías desarrolladas por DRC. La transferencia de conocimientos y de acompañamiento incluyen las fases de focalización, formación, evaluaciones de planes de negocio, y seguimiento de la evolución de los participantes.

**Participación comunitaria**

- Facilitar procesos de información, convocatoria y participación de la comunidad que permitan el acceso y la aceptación comunitaria.
- Monitorear la participación de grupos vulnerables (mujeres, personas mayores, personas con discapacidad) y necesidades específicas para su participación
- Garantizar la calidad, participación comunitaria y mecanismos de rendición de cuentas en la ejecución de actividades.

**Monitoreo y reporte**

- Garantizar la compilación de los medios de verificación requeridos y datos cualitativos de las actividades del proyecto.
- Aplicar encuestas para el registro, línea base, PDMs, línea de salida y otras encuestas necesarias para la implementación del proyecto.
- Reportar a los supervisores, incidentes, retrasos o cualquier otro desafío o reto para la implementación de las actividades a nivel programático, logístico y/o financiero.
- Monitorear el avance de las personas beneficiarias, documentar resultados y generar lecciones aprendidas.
- Aportar a la documentación de buenas prácticas, historias de vida o casos de éxito.
- Contribuir a la elaboración de informes técnicos y narrativos según los requerimientos del proyecto.

**Experiencias y competencias técnicas:**

- 2 años de experiencia relevante en trabajo relacionado con medios de vida, especialmente con el desarrollo y fortalecimiento de emprendimientos, y modelos de negocio de economía circular. Experiencia desarrollando estructuras de costos para pequeños negocios, planes de marketing y/o fortaleciendo habilidades blandas para emprender es valorado.
- Experiencia en trabajo articulado con proyectos de protección, preparación para desastres, WASH, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades en zonas urbanas de difícil acceso y rurales, personas desplazadas, y/o migrantes y refugiadas.
- Experiencia en la facilitación de modelos de aprendizaje híbridos y uso de herramientas digitales (como Moodle) para la capacitación de poblaciones vulnerables es valorada.
- Experiencia y capacidad para relacionarse con las personas, interactuar con equipos multidisciplinarios, resolver conflictos y gestionar dinámicas de grupos.
- Habilidades y experiencia en capacitación y desarrollo de capacidades de personal de organizaciones sin fines de lucro con conocimiento básico o intermedio en medios de vida.
- Habilidades de redacción de informes y otros documentos de comunicación interna.
- Excelente habilidad en MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Experiencia en manejar bases de datos.

**Educación**

- Título universitario pertinente relacionado a administración de empresas, contabilidad, economía, desarrollo humano, trabajo social, psicología, mercadeo, docencia o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Idiomas**

- Español
- Inglés nivel A2 (deseable)

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

jobs.title: EU Policy and Advocacy Manager (Temporary)
jobs.description:
**Job Title**: EU Policy and Advocacy Manager (Temporary)

**Department**: Advocacy and Communications

**Duty Station**: Brussels, Belgium

**Line Manager**: Global Head of Policy and Communications

**Position Type:** Temporary employment, initially 9 months, with possibility for extension to 12 months; Full-time.

**Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP)** is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**OVERVIEW**

NP is seeking an experienced EU Policy and Advocacy Manager to provide temporary coverage during a period of staff absence.

Based in Brussels, the position will ensure continuity in NP’s strategic engagement with European Union (EU) institutions, member states, and relevant civil society networks.

The EU Policy and Advocacy Manager will lead and coordinate the implementation of NP’s EU advocacy strategy, maintain and strengthen strategic relationships, and advance policy discussions on unarmed civilian protection, violence prevention and peacebuilding.

The position will also support NP country programmes in their engagement with EU stakeholders and contribute to broader global advocacy initiatives as required.

**JOB PURPOSE**

The overall objective of this temporary position is to maintain and strengthen NP’s engagement and policy influencing in EU and related policy and advocacy spaces.

The postholder will be responsible for coordinating NP’s EU advocacy processes and relationships. including bilateral engagement with EU member states, related organisations, and with core EU institutions.

The role will also involve participation in policy networks and thematic discussions related to peace and civilian protection, alongside providing strategic guidance and coordination to NP country programmes engaging with EU institutions in Brussels and other European capitals.

The position does not carry direct staff management responsibilities but requires a high degree of independence, strategic judgement and coordination across NP’s global teams.

**COMMITMENT TO NP PRINCIPLES**

All staff are expected to embody and actively work towards NP’s core principles in all aspects of their work:

1. **Nonviolence** in our approach, language, and actions.
2. **Direct Action** when engaging meaningfully with mandate goals.
3. **Radical Connection** through fostering safe, respectful, and inclusive relationships with communities, partners, and colleagues.
4. \*\*Process-\*\*oriented by abiding by NP's values, policies, and the Global Employee Handbook.
5. **Independence** by maintaining integrity in judgment and conduct.
6. **Non-partisanship** by acting without bias or partisan influence.
7. **Redemption and Healing** by contributing to environments where accountability and growth are possible.
8. **Pluriversality** by embracing and protecting the diversity of all people NP works with and for.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategy, representation and policy influencing**

- Lead and coordinate the Implementation of NP’s EU advocacy strategy, with a focus on raising the visibility of nonviolent approaches to civilian protection, violence prevention, and the experiences of civilians affected by violent contexts.
- Represent NP in engagements with EU institutions, member states, and relevant policy and advocacy platforms.
- Monitor developments in EU policies and priorities, identify opportunities for NP’s engagement and recommend strategic responses.
- Coordinate and facilitate engagement between NP Staff, partners and EU stakeholders in Brussels.
- Provide strategic advice and guidance to NP country programmes engaging with EU institutions and representations outside Brussels.
- Ensure continuity and coherence in NP’s EU advocacy priorities and engagement during the temporary assignment.

**Networking and partnerships**

- Maintain and strengthen NP’s relationships and EU-related networks, including with EU staff, member states, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Identify opportunities for strategic collaboration and joint advocacy with like-minded organisations.
- Work closely with NP staff to ensure that the EU policy and advocacy work is well integrated into the relevant team and organisational strategies and plans.
- Facilitate information sharing and coordination across NP teams on EU policy development, opportunities and engagement.

**Learning and impact**

- Contribute to the learning and development of NP by sharing insights from interactions with EU stakeholders to inform practice and programmes.
- Contribute to the broader learning agenda of NP through participation in relevant learning and reflection events.
- Support the documentation of key advocacy developments, engagements and outcomes.

**Other**

- Develop and maintain a strong understanding of NP’s mission, values, country programmes and thematic policy priorities to represent NP effectively.
- Identify potential resource mobilization and partnership opportunities emerging through EU engagement and share relevant information with the programme development colleagues.
- Contribute to other global policy and advocacy initiatives as required and agreed with the line manager.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

**Experience**

- At least 8-10 years of relevant experience working on protection and/or peacebuilding policy and practice, preferably with existing experience advocating toward the European Union.
- Demonstrated experience engaging with EU institutions, member states or European policy and advocacy networks, preferably on peacebuilding, civilian protection or related issues.
- Experience working with or supporting local partners and country programs in conflict-affected contexts.
- Experience developing or coordinating policy advocacy initiatives and maintaining strategic stakeholder relationships.

**Education**

Minimum master’s degree in political science, international relations, peacebuilding, humanitarian studies or a related field is required.

**Language**

Fluency in spoken English and French.

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES**

- Strong understanding of policy influencing processes and relevant EU institutions.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex policy issues to diverse audiences.
- Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to respond to policy developments and advocacy opportunities.
- Excellent organizational, coordination and time management skills.
- Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgement and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
- Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively across diverse, multicultural and geographically dispersed teams.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer committed to a fair, transparent and accessible recruitment process. All qualified applicants are considered solely on merit, regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Nonviolent Peaceforce is committed to safeguarding the welfare of our employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, partner communities, and all stakeholders. All staff and volunteers are expected to uphold this commitment through our Code of Conduct, complete the appropriate safeguarding training, and work in accordance with our safeguarding policies. Employment offers are subject to satisfactory references and screening checks, which may include criminal records and terrorism-finance checks. NP participates in the[ Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/) and may request information from previous employers regarding findings of, or ongoing investigations into, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment. By applying, candidates acknowledge and accept these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE WAIVER**

**We never request payment at any stage of the recruitment process and only communicate through official corporate accounts and platforms. Any request for payment is likely fraudulent. Please verify vacancies through our** [**official website.**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/)

jobs.title: Colombia - Consultoría para el diseño de una estrategia de comunicación y sensibilización
jobs.description:
**1. COOPI**
COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una organización humanitaria laica e independiente italiana que lucha
contra todas las formas de pobreza para mejorar el mundo. Fundada en 1965, hoy COOPI está presente en
33 países de África, América Latina y el Caribe y Oriente Medio, con proyectos tanto de emergencia como de
desarrollo. Los principales financiadores institucionales son la Unión Europea - ECHO e INTPA -, agencias
de la ONU, Agencia Italiana de Cooperación para el Desarrollo AICS, autoridades locales y otros gobiernos
europeos.
Desde 1999, COOPI ha estado presente en Colombia, apoyando a comunidades afectadas por el conflicto
armado y desastres.

**2. Sobre el Proyecto**
En el marco de su acción, COOPI, en consorcio con las organizaciones internacionales FADV, HIAS y HI,
está ejecutando el proyecto: “URABÁ-PAIS: Protección, asistencia humanitaria e integración socioeconómica
para migrantes, refugiados y víctimas del conflicto en el Departamento de Antioquia, Colombia” financiado por
la Agencia Italiana de Cooperación para el Desarrollo - AICS. El proyecto se implementa en el territorio del
Urabá Antioqueño, específicamente en los municipios de Necoclí, Turbo y Apartadó. El proyecto busca
contribuir al mejoramiento de las condiciones de vida de la población en tránsito, las comunidades locales
víctimas del conflicto armado interno y los migrantes venezolanos con vocación de permanencia, fortaleciendo
la cohesión social y la convivencia pacífica en los territorios fronterizos del Golfo de Urabá, Colombia. Los

principales resultados se enmarcan en: R1. La distribución de Asistencia Humanitaria, R2. La provisión de
servicios básicos de salud y R3. El fortalecimiento de la integración socioeconómica y la cohesión social entre
refugiados, migrantes, víctimas del conflicto armado y comunidades locales, mediante la mediación de
mujeres y jóvenes, la formación profesional, la inserción en el mundo laboral y acciones destinadas a
promover la convivencia pacífica.
Como parte del R3, el Proyecto se ha comprometido a elaborar una estrategia de comunicación con un
enfoque comunitario que desarrollará distintas líneas de trabajo, con el fin de promover mensajes y acciones
clave que reduzcan la discriminación, la xenofobia y la violencia de género, promoviendo al mismo tiempo
la integración social y la cohesión comunitaria. En tal sentido, el proyecto propone realizar una campaña
dirigida a la población meta de la siguiente manera:
1\. Sensibilización de la población en general: La campaña difundirá mensajes clave a través de las redes
sociales como Instagram, Facebook, TikTok y canales comunitarios en el marco de la estrategia
“ponte en mis zapatos”, que buscará sensibilizar a la población en general sobre los problemas de
las personas marginadas y desarrollar mecanismos de ayuda mutua. La difusión de la campaña se
realizará también en espacios de formación para niños, adolescentes y jóvenes adultos y para la
población en fase de formación (escuelas de emprendimiento del proyecto).
2\. Promoción de la inclusión y de la diversidad: en el marco de las ferias, de los encuentros y de las
actividades masivas que se desarrollarán durante el proyecto, HI liderará los procesos orientados a
la difusión de mensajes clave para la población migrante, las personas con discapacidad y las
minorías marginadas.
3\. Promoción de la participación juvenil, mediante el desarrollo de material audiovisual como podcast o
testimonios narrativos asociados a las temáticas de la campaña y en el marco de otras actividades
transversales del proyecto, incluido el semillero “la decisión es mía”.
Al término del proyecto, se habrá alcanzado a más de 2500 personas con perfiles diversos, que permitirán la
réplica de los mensajes y de las buenas prácticas derivadas del proyecto.

**3. Objeto de la Contratación**
Contratar a una consultoría especializada en comunicación estratégica, narrativa institucional digital y
producción de contenidos, para el diseño de una campaña de comunicación y sensibilización orientada a la
prevención de la discriminación, la xenofobia y la violencia basada en género, y para la producción de sus
contenidos y piezas finales (digitales, audiovisuales y para espacios físicos). Las piezas serán difundidas por
COOPI, HI y los socios del consorcio Urabá País en redes sociales, espacios educativos y comunitarios y
eventos del proyecto.
La campaña busca contribuir a cambios en percepciones, actitudes y prácticas frente a la discriminación, la
xenofobia y la VBG, promoviendo narrativas de empatía, inclusión y cohesión social.

**Perfil del Consultor/a**
**Requisitos Esenciales (hasta 27 puntos)**
• Profesional, técnico, tecnólogo o estudiante de últimos semestres en Comunicación Social,
Periodismo, Diseño Gráfico, Diseño Visual, Ciencias Sociales o afines. Hasta 10 puntos.
• 2 años de experiencia en producción de contenidos institucionales, con un portafolio que demuestre
habilidades en narrativa audiovisual y fotografía documental. Hasta 7 puntos.
• Experiencia demostrable en la elaboración de estrategias de comunicación y campañas para medios
masivos y digitales, incluyendo la creación de estudios de caso, historias de vida o storytelling
humanitario. Hasta 5 puntos.
• Conocimiento y experiencia en la aplicación de lineamientos de protección de datos, consentimiento
informado y enfoque diferencial (género, discapacidad, interculturalidad). Hasta 3 puntos.
• Dominio de herramientas de edición de video (Premiere Pro, Final Cut o similares) y fotografía
(Lightroom, Photoshop). Hasta 2 puntos.

**Requisitos Deseables (hasta 3 puntos)**
• Estudios de posgrado en áreas relacionadas con comunicación para el desarrollo, acción
humanitaria o cooperación internacional. Hasta 2 puntos.
• Experiencia en trabajo con población migrante, refugiada, víctima del conflicto u otros grupos en
condición de vulnerabilidad. Hasta 1 punto.

**Competencias técnicas:**
● Redacción narrativa con enfoque humano y estratégico.
● Edición de textos con criterios editoriales institucionales.
● Capacidad de síntesis y jerarquización de información.
● Aplicación de lineamientos de marca y visibilidad.
● Gestión ética de información sensible.
● Capacidad de entrevista en campo.
● Enfoque diferencial (género, discapacidad, interculturalidad).

**Equipo mínimo sugerido**
• Equipo propio de alta gama (Cámaras, Iluminación, Sonido directo).

jobs.title: Middle East Humanitarian Appeal Evaluation
jobs.description:
## **About The Role**

**Middle East Humanitarian Appeal Evaluation Consultant**

**Location: Gaza** (across accessible governorates and via remote reach where physical access is prohibited) and **Lebanon** (national-level analysis, with reference to operational areas of South Lebanon, Nabatieh, Baalbek-Hermel and Mount Lebanon as relevant)

**Rate: £60,000 total budget (inclusive of expenses) - maximum of £500 per individual per day.**

**Duration: Approximately 16 weeks (starting ideally from December 2026 until March 2027)**

**Contract: Self-employed Consultant / Contractor / Sole Trader / Limited Liability Companies**

**Please note:** We welcome applications from both **UK-based and overseas contractors**.

*Can you help shape the future of humanitarian response in the Middle East?*

We're seeking an experienced and insightful Humanitarian Evaluation Consultant to lead an independent evaluation of the British Red Cross Middle East Humanitarian Appeal response in Gaza and Lebanon.

This consultancy presents a unique opportunity to assess the effectiveness, relevance, coherence and impact of humanitarian interventions delivered in response to one of the most significant humanitarian crises in recent years. The successful consultant will be responsible for proposing and applying an appropriate evaluation methodology and delivering independent, evidence-based findings and recommendations. Working closely with key stakeholders, you will help improve future humanitarian programming and support better outcomes for affected communities.

We're looking for an experienced evaluator who can work independently, navigate complex operating environments and deliver robust, high-quality analysis that informs strategic decision-making.

Please refer to the Terms of Reference (ToR) for full details of the assignment, including proposal submission requirements, evaluation scope and deliverables.

**What will a day in the life of a MEHA Evaluation Consultant involve?**

- Leading the design and delivery of an independent evaluation of humanitarian programmes across Gaza and Lebanon.
- Developing evaluation methodologies, data collection tools and analytical approaches aligned with recognised humanitarian evaluation standards.
- Conducting document reviews, stakeholder consultations, interviews, focus groups and data analysis to generate evidence-based findings.
- Producing high-quality reports, facilitating validation workshops and presenting recommendations to a range of humanitarian stakeholders.

**To be a successful MEHA Evaluation Consultant, what will you need?**

- Significant experience leading complex evaluations within humanitarian, international development, emergency response or recovery programmes.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian principles, evaluation methodologies, MEAL frameworks and internationally recognised evaluation standards.
- Demonstrable experience evaluating health, cash assistance, humanitarian response, resilience or related programmes in complex contexts.
- Excellent research, analysis, report-writing and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to turn complex findings into clear and actionable recommendations.

**It would also be advantageous if you met the following desirable criteria:**

- Previous experience working in or evaluating programmes in the Middle East.
- Familiarity with Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement.
- Experience managing remote or hybrid evaluation approaches in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
- Proficiency in Arabic, or access to appropriately qualified language support.

**Interested?** The **closing** **date** for applications is 23.59 on **Wednesday 4th November**.

This is a short-term consultancy, **not** a salaried staff role. We’re looking for an experienced contractor with a proven track record in humanitarian evaluation, research and learning. You **must** be self-employed and operating as an independent contractor or consultancy; Self-employed workers are not paid through PAYE, and they do not have the rights and responsibilities of an employee.

**Together, we are the world's emergency responders**

jobs.title: National Professional Officer (Health Financing)
jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:
1\. **International knowledge hub for health** – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.
2\. **Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health** – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.
3\. **Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats** – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.
4\. **Driver of health system transformation** – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.
5\. **Voice for health equity** – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

With the overall aim of advancing progress towards Universal Health Coverage, promoting good practices in health financing and reducing financial hardship, the incumbent leads WHO's health financing work in Ukraine and provides technical advice to national counterparts on health financing policy and reform.

Key duties:
1\. Coordinate and provide technical leadership for the design, implementation and monitoring of WHO's health financing workstream, as programmed in the Country Cooperation Strategy (CCS) Biennial Collaborative Agreement (BCA), including WHO's contribution to health sector coordination and national policy dialogue.
2\. Provide technical advice to the Ministry of Health, the National Health Service of Ukraine (NHSU) and other national partners on the development, implementation and evaluation of health financing policies and reforms at national and subnational levels, including strategic purchasing, the design of the Programme of Medical Guarantees, public financial management, to improve health system performance, including financial protection and progress towards universal health coverage.
3\. Identify and guide priority areas for collaboration, capacity development and technical assistance in health financing, and translate these priorities into deliverable and costed workplans under the CCS BCA and donor-financed projects.
4\. Lead and oversee the generation and use of evidence to support health financing policy and reform. This includes overseeing the analysis of health financing data and the planning, commissioning and quality assurance of studies, policy briefs, situation analyses, reports and other technical products on health financing, health system performance, service coverage and aid effectiveness. Work closely with WHO technical programmes to ensure that evidence generated is used to inform policy advice and dialogue, as well as the monitoring and evaluation of health financing reforms.
5\. Lead and oversee the effective and high-quality implementation of health financing activities under donor-financed initiatives and agreed partnerships at country level. Provide technical direction for technical assistance, policy dialogue and capacity development, ensuring that activities are aligned with agreed objectives, priorities and deliverables. Monitor implementation and results and ensure timely and appropriate reporting to relevant stakeholders and donors.
6\. Represent WHO, as appropriate, in discussions with national authorities, development partners and other stakeholders on health financing. Lead and contribute to technical discussions, coordination mechanisms and policy dialogue, and strengthen collaboration among partners to support coherent implementation of health financing reforms.
7\. Supervise and provide technical direction to the staff working on health financing. Assign and prioritize work, clarify responsibilities, review the quality and timeliness of technical outputs, provide feedback and guidance, and support their performance and professional development. Ensure effective coordination between their respective areas of work and coherence across the health financing portfolio.
8\. Contribute to strengthening national capacity in health financing through technical guidance, knowledge sharing and capacity development activities, in collaboration with national institutions and relevant partners.
9\. Organize and substantively support WHO missions, visits and high-level engagements on health financing, and follow up on agreed recommendations and actions to ensure appropriate implementation.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** A university degree (Bachelor's level) in business administration, management, economics or health economics, health policy, public health, social and political sciences, with concentration in health financing.
**Desirable:** Master's degree or postgraduate degree in any of the above fields.

### Experience

**Essential**: At least five years of professional experience in health systems strengthening, including substantial experience in health financing. Experience working with national health authorities, purchasing agencies, academic institutions, international organizations and/or non-governmental organizations. Demonstrated experience contributing to or providing technical input to national health financing policy processes and policy dialogue.
**Desirable**: Experience in WHO/UN and international agencies; Experience providing policy advice on health systems strengthening, health financing and health sector reform, particularly in transition, reform or post-crisis settings.

### Functional Skills

- Demonstrated knowledge of health systems and health financing policy in the countries of the WHO European Region, including purchasing, benefit package design, public financial management and financial protection monitoring.
- Proven ability to translate technical analysis into policy advice for senior decision-makers and to formulate technical positions independently.
- Ability to interact appropriately and with credibility with high-level stakeholders, including senior officials and ministers.
- Ability to lead high performing teams. Ability to work within significant uncertainties in a rapidly changing environment and to set priorities with limited supervision.
- Data management and data analysis skills.
- Good computer skills (word processing, spreadsheet, PowerPoint presentations).
- Strong written and oral communication skills, including drafting for policy audiences.
- Emotional intelligence: ability to identify and manage one's own emotions, as well as helping others to do the same.

### WHO Competencies

1\. Teamwork
2\. Respecting & promoting individual and cultural differences
3\. Communication
4\. Moving forward in a changing environment
5\. Building and promoting partnerships across the Organization and beyond

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - National Professional Officer (Health Financing) (2604631)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2604631&tz=GMT%2B03%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: Documentary Film Production Consultant
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference (ToR):** Documentary Film Production Consultant, STRIVE Program – Indonesia

**Location:** Indonesia

**Assignment Date:** Until May 2027

**Contract Type:** Consultant (6 months)

**A. BACKGROUND**

Nurani Perdamaian Indonesia (NPID), through the GCERF, is implementing the Strengthening Rehabilitation and Reintegration and Improve Social Cohesion against Violent Extremism (STRIVE) Program from January 2025 to December 2027.

Implemented in partnership with national and local civil society organizations and in close collaboration with relevant government institutions, the STRIVE Program seeks to strengthen Indonesia's efforts in preventing violent extremism by supporting the reintegration and rehabilitation of returnees, former violent extremist offenders, and individuals at risk, while fostering resilient and inclusive communities. The program is implemented across three primary intervention areas:

- Jakarta
- Bima, West Nusa Tenggara
- Poso, Central Sulawesi

Throughout its implementation, STRIVE has promoted multi-stakeholder collaboration involving government agencies, civil society organizations, community leaders, religious leaders, youth, women, and beneficiaries to strengthen social cohesion and sustainable reintegration.

As the program approaches its completion, NP Indonesia intends to produce a high-quality documentary film that captures its journey, achievements, lessons learned, and the human stories behind the intervention. The documentary is expected to serve as a legacy product, an advocacy tool, and a knowledge resource that highlights the importance of sustained investment in community resilience and reintegration beyond the program period.

**B. PURPOSE**

The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a compelling documentary film that captures the overall implementation and impact of the STRIVE Program while communicating the continued importance of community-based reintegration and resilience-building efforts.

The documentary should present authentic stories, demonstrate evidence of program achievements, and inspire continued collaboration among governments, communities, civil society, and development partners.

**C. OBJECTIVES**

The documentary shall aim to:

1. Document the implementation of the STRIVE Program across Jakarta, Bima, and Poso.
2. Capture stories of transformation among beneficiaries, families, communities, and institutional stakeholders.
3. Showcase collaborative efforts between government institutions, civil society organizations, and local communities.
4. Demonstrate the program's contribution to strengthening community resilience, social cohesion, and sustainable reintegration.
5. Produce a high-quality legacy documentary suitable for advocacy, public communication, knowledge sharing, and future resource mobilization.

**D. SCOPE OF WORK**

The selected consultant shall be responsible for the complete production process, including pre-production, production, and post-production.

**1. Pre-Production**

The consultant shall:

1. Participate in inception meetings with NP Indonesia.
2. Review program documents and communication materials.
3. Develop a creative concept and documentary treatment.
4. Prepare storyline, interview framework, and production schedule.
5. Identify key interviewees together with the program team.
6. Prepare filming plans and logistics.

**2. Production**

The consultant shall conduct field production in:

1. Jakarta
2. Bima, West Nusa Tenggara
3. Poso, Central Sulawesi

The filming should include, but not be limited to:

1. Program implementation activities
2. Beneficiary interviews
3. Family member interviews
4. Community leaders
5. Religious leaders
6. Government representatives
7. Consortium partners
8. Community interactions
9. Environmental and supporting footage
10. Drone footage (where permitted)

The consultant is expected to adopt a cinematic documentary approach that emphasizes authentic storytelling and high-quality visual production.

**3. Post-Production**

The consultant shall:

1. Develop the documentary narrative.
2. Edit all footage.
3. Produce motion graphics and animated statistics where appropriate.
4. Add background music and sound mixing.
5. Prepare English and Bahasa Indonesia subtitles.
6. Incorporate revisions based on feedback from NP Indonesia.
7. Deliver final mastered versions.

**E. DOCUMENTARY APPROACH**

Rather than producing a chronological record of program activities, the documentary should adopt a story-driven, human-centered approach.

The documentary should:

1. Highlight authentic experiences.
2. Balance emotional storytelling with evidence-based program achievements.
3. Showcase collaboration among communities, government institutions, and civil society.
4. Present transformation at individual, community, and institutional levels.
5. Maintain a professional cinematic quality suitable for international audiences.

The documentary should conclude with a forward-looking message that emphasizes the importance of sustaining the gains achieved through the STRIVE Program and continuing collective efforts toward resilient communities.

**F. DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE**

The consultant shall deliver:

**Deliverables**

- One documentary film.
- One shortened version of the documentary film.
- One promotional trailer.
- Five short social media video clips.
- Subtitles in English and Bahasa Indonesia.
- High-resolution photographs from field production.
- All raw video footage.
- Editable project files, upon request.

**Timeline**

- **December:** Procurement process, inception meeting, desk review, development of the creative concept and storyline, preparation of the interview list, shooting plan, and logistics.
- **January to March:** Field production in Jakarta, Bima, and Poso.
- **April:** Editing, script writing, motion graphics development, subtitling, music scoring, and preparation of the first cut.
- **May:** Review and revision process, final cut, mastering, and submission of all final deliverables.

**G. CONSULTANT QUALIFICATION**

The consultant or production company should possess:

- Minimum five (5) years of professional experience in documentary film production.
- Demonstrated experience producing documentaries for international development programs, humanitarian organizations, or donor-funded projects.
- Strong storytelling and cinematic production capabilities.
- Proven experience conducting field production in diverse cultural contexts.
- Ability to produce bilingual documentary outputs.
- Availability to travel to all program locations.
- Experience working with government institutions and civil society organizations is considered an asset.

**H. PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS**

Interested consultants shall submit:
**1. Technical Proposal**

1. Understanding of the assignment.
2. Proposed documentary concept.
3. Creative treatment.
4. Storytelling approach.
5. Production methodology.
6. Workplan and timeline.
7. Team composition and roles.
8. Relevant portfolio.
9. Risk management approach.

**2. Financial Proposal**

1. Professional fees.
2. Travel costs.
3. Accommodation.
4. Equipment.
5. Editing.
6. Production expenses.
7. Applicable taxes.

**I. BUDGET**

The estimated total production film is **IDR 250,000,000**, from budget lines: CWW.076 Produce a film adaptation based on one Human Interest stories from Poso ( B11.1 )

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector.NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [InterAgency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here**](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/) **on our website.**

jobs.title: Safety & Security Officer (Ukrainian Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Safety & Security Officer (Ukrainian nationals)

**Department:** Safety & Security

**Division:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Mykolaiv, Ukraine

**Line Manager:** Safety & Security Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

**Overview:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**Job Summary:**

The Safety and Security Officer works directly with the Head of Operations and Security to contribute to the safety and security of NP staff in Ukraine. The position will support with analysis and security inputs and will engage directly with programmes teams for security monitoring and guidance. The position contributes to making sure effective safety and security arrangements are in place for NP staff.

The ideal candidate will bring security expertise developed through experience working in the security and/or humanitarian sector. They are focused and driven by a keen interest and personal commitment to civilian protection – the core of NP’s work.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Security Management**

- Implement and uphold NP safety and security policies, procedures, SOPs, and contingency plans at field and office level.
- Conduct regular security and risk assessments to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigation measures.
- Support the operationalisation of security plans including travel management, incident response, emergency communications, evacuation, relocation, and hibernation procedures.
- Ensure offices, guesthouses, and programme sites meet minimum physical security standards through regular infrastructure and security audits.
- Immediately report and document all security incidents, breaches, threats, or near-misses affecting staff, assets, or operations.

**Operational Support & Staff Movement**

- Provide real-time tracking, monitoring, and oversight of staff and vehicle movements in line with established procedures.
- Ensure vehicles, communications equipment, and personal protective equipment are available, functional, and compliant with minimum standards.
- Work closely with Logistics to identify, procure, and maintain safety and security equipment and resources.

**Information Management & Analysis**

- Collect, verify, analyze, and disseminate security-related information from formal and informal sources.
- Maintain up-to-date records of security incidents, trends, and contextual developments.
- Provide timely security briefings, updates, and advisories to staff and management in response to changes in context.
- Contribute to weekly and monthly security reports relevant to NP areas of operation.

**Training & Capacity Building**

- Deliver regular security briefings, inductions, and awareness sessions for staff.
- Identify security capacity-building needs and support the design and delivery of relevant trainings.
- Train, mentor, and support designated Security Focal Points across field offices.
- Supervise, train, and develop security staff at office or area level where applicable.

**Coordination, Liaison & Access**

- Maintain strong working relationships with NGOs, UN agencies, INSO, security providers, and relevant coordination platforms.
- Liaise with local authorities, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders to support safe access and programme implementation, in line with humanitarian principles.
- Participate in security coordination forums and inter-agency meetings as required.
- Support access analysis and security input for programme planning and expansion into new areas of operation.

**Assessments & Compliance**

- Participate in security assessments for new locations and evolving operational areas.
- Ensure adherence to NP security risk management standards and country-specific SOPs.
- Support senior management in internal security reviews and audits.

**Safeguarding & Conduct**

- Comply with and uphold NP safeguarding policies, including child protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and policies on bullying and harassment.
- Act in accordance with NP Codes of Conduct at all times.

**Critical Interfaces**

- All NP staff and departments.
- Senior Management Team.
- Programme and Operations teams.
- Logistics and Administration.
- External coordination and security actors.

**Qualifications:**

- Post-secondary education in a related field with at least 2 years related work experience or equivalent in work experience.
- Relevant security experience in humanitarian settings / previous experience working with security providers, law enforcement entities, and/or intelligence resources and utilizing information to create and deploy actionable security plans and programs.
- Understanding of current security management good practice.
- Good grasp of various communications technologies commonly used, including VHF radio systems, satellite phones, cell phones, Power Bi, etc.
- Excellent interpersonal, representation and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence, build consensus and develop partnerships.
- Ability to work well under pressure in unstable and frequently changing security environments.
- Training and facilitator skills; ability to support training sessions is a plus.
- Commitment to and understanding of NP’s methodologies, core values and mission.
- Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English, Ukrainian and Russian.
- Computer literacy, particularly in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, databases.
- Valid Ukrainian driving license.
- Knowledge of and commitment to safeguarding, whistleblowing, PSEA and anti-corruption.

**Skills and Competencies:**

**Independent Judgment/Analytical:**

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Identify safety and security issues and propose solutions.

**Interpersonal:**

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work and live in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to exert solutions-focused, creative behaviour.
- Proven ability to build relationships with the full range of actors including government, military, police and non-state actors.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

**Languages:**

- Ability to interact confidently in English with colleagues and external contacts, including in writing, and to present effectively relevant information.

**Information Technology:**

- High level skills in Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Excel, SharePoint, PowerPoint, Word, Power BI).
- Knowledge of Digital Mapping and GPS tracking software.
- Knowledge of computer software for VHF radios.
- Emergency Response Systems.

**Working Conditions:**

- Ukraine is a complex security environment, and the evolution of the war is completely unpredictable – experience in insecure environments is essential to success in this position.
- A strong motivation to do what’s necessary in a complex environment.
- Willingness to work some weekends and evenings to contribute to security support and preparedness.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

jobs.title: Policy & Advocacy Assistant
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Policy & Advocacy Assistant

**Department:** Advocacy

**Division:** NPUS

**Duty Station:** Washington D.C., U.S. (hybrid)

**Administrative Line Manager:** U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager

**Technical Line Manager:** U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Part-time, non-exempt

**OVERVIEW**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Since 2020, NP has worked alongside local communities in the U.S. to interrupt cycles of violence and build bridges across polarized communities. Responsive to community needs, NP builds relationships with community members, leaders, and organizations to identify risks to safety and ways to work together to keep communities safe through nonviolent strategies. These strategies include protective presence, training, safety planning, and rapid response. This work takes us to demonstrations, marches, courts, voting centers, health facilities, pantries, and other public spaces where people may face violence and intimidation. In partnership with local organizations we help build stronger protection networks, coordinate responses to emerging risks and advance the practice of nonviolent community-led approaches to protection in communities across the country.

**JOB SUMMARY**

Nonviolent Peaceforce U.S. (NPUS) is seeking a Policy and Advocacy Assistant to support NP's Advocacy team within the External Engagement function. The Policy and Advocacy Assistant will support NP’s advocacy to the U.S. government and the broader work of the global Policy and Advocacy team, with a special focus on the federal appropriations process. Under the supervision of the U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager the Policy and Advocacy Assistant will represent NP in coalition meetings, submit congressional appropriations requests, and meet with congressional staffers to educate on the importance of key foreign assistance funds. The role will support NP’s mission and advocacy for the use of UCP methodologies through legislative, policy, and other advocacy opportunities. Training and feedback will be provided.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Federal Advocacy**

- Complete research on the impacts of U.S. government foreign aid funding
- Submit federal appropriations requests to key congressional offices
- Educate congressional staffers on the roles of key foreign aid accounts
- Draft advocacy materials based on NP’s program and policy work
- Track legislative developments and relevant committee hearings
- Reviewing and summarizing key policies, statements, and other documents related to given conflict contexts

**Coalition Engagement**

- Represent NP in meetings and events with civil society. Take notes and prepare meeting readouts.
- Support NP’s programmatic teams in participating in broader civil society organizing efforts

**Administrative Support**

- Support preparation for events
- Assist with data management tasks
- Format public documents
- Additional advocacy projects as needed

**COMMITMENT TO NP PRINCIPLES**

All NP employees are expected to uphold work in alignment with the organization’s guiding principles:

- Nonviolence
- Non-partisanship
- Primacy of local actors
- Civilian-to-civilian action

These principles and beliefs guide our actions and relationships, supporting our mission to protect civilians in violent conflicts through unarmed strategies

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Well-versed in advocacy strategies and forums
- Understanding of U.S. Government legislative process
- Knowledge of current events and social issues, an interest in civilian protection and nonviolent methods
- Current or recent graduate student preferred
- Previous experience with U.S. congressional appropriations process is a significant advantage

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES**

- Independent Judgement/Analytical
- Ability to manage information with discretion
- Ability to set priorities, solve problems, and analyze information
- Attention to detail
- Interpersonal
- Flexible, energetic, and adaptable
- Ability to work in a diverse team environment
- Proven ability to build and manage relationships
- Information Technology
- Ability to use the MS Office Suite, email, and the internet proficiently
- Strong communication (written and spoken) and interpersonal skills in English
- Experience working with multicultural teams
- Ability to clearly articulate complex ideas to policymakers and colleagues
- Clear, concise writing skills
- Able to follow written and verbal directions well, able to work autonomously
- Commitment to work cooperatively and grow personally
- Commitment to the mission of Nonviolent Peaceforce

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

- Consistently operate a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and/or printer.
- Ability to remain in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods.
- Ability to work in small or enclosed spaces.
- Ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.

**NP's Commitment**

- Mentorship & Feedback
- Supervision
- Opportunities to participate in meetings and projects aligned with the candidate's interests

**Experiences Offered**

- High-level policy analysis skills and exposure to advocacy strategy
- Work with and contribute to an international nongovernmental organization
- Deeper understanding of humanitarian protection principles and programming
- Belong to a community committed to learning and growing together
- Work in a professional atmosphere

This is a temporary part-time hourly position expected to run January 2027-May 2027. Selected candidate will be expected to work 15-19 weekly with at least one day a week in-person at NP’s DC office.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector.NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritize ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organization.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.
