jobs.title: Programme Officer - Community Health
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in strengthening and shaping community-led health programmes in Madagascar. Focused in SEEDs maternal and child health programme, you will support the development, funding, reporting and evaluation of this work, offering support to other projects where required and working closely with national teams delivering projects on the ground.

Our work focuses on maternal and child health, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), violence against women and girls (VAWG) and food security - using participatory approaches that place communities at the center of identifying needs and driving sustainable solutions.

You will lead on developing high-quality funding proposals, managing donor reporting, supporting monitoring and evaluation and ensuring the programme is delivered effectively and to a high standard.

We are seeking an early career, public health professional with one to three years experience, strong grant writing experience, particularly in maternal, or gender-based violence programming. Excellent written English is essential; French proficiency is highly desirable. Candidates who do not meet these criteria will not be considered.

\*Title:\*Programme Officer
*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar
\*Timeframe:\*24 months extendable
*Contract Type:* Local salary to support with accommodation and living costs, contribution of £1,200 towards flights and £650 towards insurance

**Duties and responsibilities**:

- Together with the Programme Manager, lead on compiling funding proposals based on past evaluation, team discussion and international best practice in an engaging and professional manner
- Compile project reports that clearly demonstrate the successes and challenges of the projects, learning from the project and providing clear budgetary information
- Provide first-stage editing of all proposals and reports across the Department to a high standard and providing detailed, constructive feedback to interns and Officers
- Support in the management of donor compliance across several projects, working with the Programme Manager and the implementation team to ensure that project milestones are being met
- Work alongside the Programme Manager and Head of Department in problem-solving and providing additional support in line with emerging issues from project implementation
- Support in the recruitment of new staff and provide support, management, review and professional development to any Interns and knowledge share across the team
- Foster essential cross-cultural collaboration, providing support to both the national and international teams to bridge gaps in understanding and priorities for project development and implementation
- Provide pastoral care, guidance and act as a role model, both professionally and personally, for a team of early career professionals living in country
- Work alongside the Project Managers and the Head of Finance in developing and managing the budgets relating to projects
- Develop and update resources to support project development processes, including proposal and budget templates and style guidelines
- Assist the MEL team in developing MEL tools and analysing data, including the writing of MEL reports when needed
- Support the development of project development procedures, guidelines, and training and provide project-specific information to inform policy development across the organisation
- Manage statistics, research, funding trackers, photo database and handovers relating to the project and ensuring this are complete and accurate
- Coordinate the project-specific website and social media content, ensuring a constant flow of information to donors and supporters
- Work with the national team and external partners in increasing their skills and capacity, providing mentoring or training where appropriate
- Take an active role in project management meetings, leading discussions and standing in for the Programmes Managers where appropriate
- Ensure all of SEED’s policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anticorruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are promoted at all times
- Form part of the team representing projects or SEED when required
- Liaise closely with the remote team ensuring clear communication at all times
- Complete any other tasks required by the Programmes Manager or Director of Operations and Heads of Departments commensurate with this role.

**Person specification**

- Hold an undergraduate in or relating to Global Health, Public Health, International Development or have transferable skills or equivalent experience
- Demonstrate sound knowledge and keen interest in MCH, SRHR and/or VAWG and its interface with international development
- At least two years experience with similar programmes
- Experience of working in a similar environment would be an advantage
- Minimum of 1-3 years professional experience of securing funding, project management, donor compliance and donor reporting
- Familiarity with the use of project management tools including Logical Frameworks, Theory of Change models, Budgets, Activity Plans and Monitoring & Evaluation frameworks
- Fluency in written and spoken English with excellent written communication skills, to the level of editing English documents for publication to a very high standard
- Proficiency in French is strongly desired
- Excellent proposal and report writing and editing skills, with previous experience compiling project proposals and reports and the ability to tailor written information to various audiences
- Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to SEED’s ethos and approach and be a good ambassador for the organisation at all times
- Have passion, curiosity and motivation for the job and the ability to enthuse others
- Experience of living and working in a developing country with the ability and desire to work with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers
- Demonstrate proven ability to recognise and appropriately deal with challenging situations and problem solve
- Demonstrate an awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, working at all times with cultural sensitivity and respect
- Demonstrate the ability, social skills and confidence to give clear guidance and support to other members of the team in respect of the philosophy and procedures of SEED in order to protect both their safety and the reputation of the NGO
- Be able to work to and advocate for all of SEED’s policies and procedures, safeguarding those that SEED works with and reporting any concerns appropriately
- Be punctual and be able to work to tight deadlines in an organised manner and to a high standard
- Be able to work both independently and as part of a team
- Excellent listening and verbal communication skills and a flexible and patient attitude
- Ability and desire to develop and support a team of volunteers and staff and to support the Project Development internship programme
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint

**About the Organisation**

SEED Madagascar is a British Charity working in partnership with communities in the southeast of Madagascar. We integrate high-quality community health, sustainable livelihoods; education infrastructure and conservation programmes to support long term, sustainable change and add to international best practice through research and publication across all of our programmatic areas.

jobs.title: Expression of Interest – Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer, Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program
jobs.description:
**About DT Global**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**Program Context**

The Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program is a DFAT funded program that is part of the Pacific Australia Skills work in Solomon Islands. Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across Timor-Leste and the Pacific. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of prior Australian Government support for skills and training in Timor-Leste. The SIRIS program will focus on support for rural training centres (RTCs) and other training providers to strengthen their institutional capability, improve the quality and relevance of skills delivery, and respond effectively to labour-market needs. Effective delivery of the activity will require coordinated planning across program, operational and technical functions, with resources aligned to agreed activities and results.

**About the Role**

We are seeking **Expressions of Interest** for **SIRIS program Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer** position for an upcoming Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program. The SIRIS MEL Officer is responsible for supporting the implementation of Pacific Australia Skills’ MEL Plan and System in the Solomon Islands country office. The role will focus on aligning the Pacific Australia Skills’ overarching program logic and MEL Plan to the Solomon Islands country context. The position will work closely with the Solomon Islands Country MEL Coordinator and other Country MEL Coordinators in data collection and writing reports for their country. The SIRIS program MEL Officer together with the Solomon Islands MEL Country Coordinator will report to the Solomon Islands Country Director. They will receive significant guidance and support from the regional MEL team (based in Suva) to ensure they have relevant tools and skills to fulfil their roles.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

- **MEL Plan and System**: Assist the Country Director to implement and strengthen a country-specific program logic and MEL Plan which flows from the overarching Pacific Australia Skills program logic and MEL Plan.
- **Data collection and monitoring:** Collect, analyse and maintain relevant MEL data to monitor progress against the Solomon Islands Country Strategy, Country Workplan and MEL Plan. This may include implementing student and employer surveys, conduct organisational capacity assessments, and develop case studies. Data will be entered into the Pacific Australia Skills Management Information System (MIS).
- **Reporting:** Support the Country Director and MEL Coordinator to prepare MEL reports for the Solomon Islands Country Office reporting, including the country annex of the program annual report and inputs to monthly reports and any other reports required by DFAT and partners.
- **Adaptive Management & Learning:** Assist the MEL Coordinator with facilitation of regular reflection sessions, learning events, and knowledge-sharing activities to integrate MEL insights into program improvement. Contribute to an ongoing process of testing, refining and further developing the program logic and its key assumptions.
- **Communication**: Support the development of evidence-based communication products that demonstrate the progress, results and contributions to Solomon Islands’ priorities by the SIRIS project and the broader Solomon Islands program. This may include identifying success stories, case studies, photographs and other relevant evidence for use in use in Pacific Australia Skills communications, reporting and public diplomacy activities. Ensure appropriate consent and safeguarding requirements are followed when collecting and using participant information and stories
- **Capacity Building:** Support MEL capacity building for Pacific Australia Skills’ in-country partners, especially the Rural Training Centres, with a focus on assisting them to develop appropriate systems and tools for monitoring, reporting and learning.
- **Evaluation & Research:** Support the implementation of evaluations, reviews and research activities related to the SIRIS project and other Solomon Islands MEL priorities, as required.
- Other duties: Undertake other MEL-related duties as required.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position: [https://tinyurl.com/7xjhb9yp](https://tinyurl.com/7xjhb9yp)

**Selection Criteria**

Essential Experience and Knowledge

- Qualifications in research, MEL, social sciences, international development, or related field.
- Minimum 5 years of experience in MEL, including developing program logics and MEL Plans.
- Experience implementing data collection and analysis.
- Ability to translate complex data into actionable insights and facilitate learning.
- Strong organisational and communication skills, with the ability to train and mentor others.
- Experience working in cross-cultural settings with a strong understanding of participatory approaches.
- Experience working with international development projects, NGOs, or donor-funded initiatives is an advantage.
- Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental protection, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.
- DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities.
- People with lived experience of the regions in which Pacific Australia Skills operate are strongly encouraged to apply.

***Please note:***

***As an Expression of Interest, this position is anticipated as part of a forthcoming program opportunity and remains contingent upon contract award and the availability of funding. At this stage, DT Global is seeking Expressions of Interest from suitably qualified candidates to support delivery subject to funding being confirmed and all necessary approvals are obtained.***

This position will promote a culture of safety and security awareness among all staff and other stakeholders.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

**Workplace Health and Safety (WHS)**

- Support the implementation and review of applicable WHS procedures.
- Conduct regular risk assessments, audits, and inspections of workplace including training delivery sites for Pacific Australia Skills trainings and programs, and program activity practices.
- Support and monitor compliance with the applicable HSE Plan, WHS legislation and DT Global/DFAT requirements.

- Support the development, implementation and monitoring of Country Office and RTCs site security procedures, including visitor access, emergency response, and security operations.
- Coordinate as required, with Operations/ICT and relevant service providers the installation and maintenance of security infrastructure and technology.
- Conduct security audits and security risk assessments to identify vulnerabilities.
- Manage incident response plans for security breaches or emergencies.
- Support the review and update of applicable HSE and Security Plans for the Solomon Islands Country Office in adherence to Pacific Australia Skills processes and procedures.
- Adhere to local laws and liaise with relevant stakeholders and emergency services as required.
- Attend WHS/HSE training sessions and provide ongoing training for staff in security protocols and processes and ensure awareness of roles in emergencies.

- Contribute to developing harmonious working relationships with DFAT, colleagues and key stakeholders, and assist to build the profile and reputation of Pacific Australia Skills as a high performing skills development program.
- As a member of the Pacific Australia Skills team, contribute to integration of GEDSI, First Nation perspectives, environmental considerations and other cross-cutting issues; fostering of a collaborative team; and measurement of results and production of reports.

- Minimum of five years’ relevant experience in Work Health and Safety (WHS), security, or a related discipline.
- Sound knowledge of WHS legislation, codes of practice, compliance requirements, and risk management principles.
- Demonstrated experience supporting workplace health and safety initiatives, including incident reporting, investigations, and follow-up actions.
- Sound knowledge of workplace security principles, security risk management, emergency preparedness, and incident response.
- Demonstrated ability to identify WHS and security risks, undertake risk assessments, and recommend and implement practical risk control measures.
- Demonstrated experience implementing and monitoring WHS and security procedures, systems, and initiatives.

The Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program is a DFAT funded program that is part of the Pacific Australia Skills work in Solomon Islands. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of prior Australian Government support for skills and training in Timor-Leste. Effective delivery of the activity will require coordinated planning across program, operational and technical functions, with resources aligned to agreed activities and results.

**About the Role**

We are seeking **Expressions of Interest** for **SIRIS program Activity Lead** position for an upcoming Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program. The SIRIS programActivity Lead is accountable for coordinating all program activities implemented to support RTCs and training providers. The role will translate approved plans into coordinated delivery; ensure that budgets, staffing and technical inputs match planned activities; oversee the Activity Support Team; monitor progress, risks and results; and provide timely advice and reporting to the Country Director. The SIRIS program Activity Lead will work across operations, skills delivery, skills development reform, communications, MEL and partnerships management to maintain an integrated approach to implementation.

The role is responsible for converting the approved rationale and delivery approach for each activity into sequenced implementation plans, ensuring value for money, managing dependencies and supporting achievement of the agreed outputs and impacts within the work-plan period.

1\. Strengthening Trainer Capability at RTCs and SINU TAFE: Upskill trainers to meet national quality standards, particularly Quality Standard 8 on trainer competence, and strengthen learner-centered, workplace-relevant and inclusive delivery.

2\. Strengthening RTC and SINU TAFE Institutional Capacity: Strengthen selected RTCs and SINU TAFE to deliver quality-assured, inclusive and demand-driven skills development through sustained technical assistance, accompaniment, equipment and improvements to training spaces.

3\. Transitioning RTCs to Technical Colleges: Provide targeted top-up technical assistance and facility upgrades to enable two RTCs to transition to Technical College status and generate practical guidance for future transitions.

**Cross-cutting**

Across all three activities, the SIRIS program Activity Lead will ensure locally led development, gender equity, disability inclusion, youth inclusion and access for rural and remote communities are integrated into planning and delivery. The role will embed safeguarding, accessibility, climate-change and disaster-resilience considerations where relevant; coordinate communications and public-diplomacy opportunities; maintain alignment with SITESA and national TVET reforms; manage synergies with other DFAT investments; and document evidence, lessons and value-for-money decisions.

## **Roles and Responsibilities**

## **Activity Planning and Coordination**

- Lead integrated work planning, scheduling and coordination of all institutional strengthening support to RTCs and training providers.
- Maintain a consolidated activity plan that identifies outputs, milestones, responsibilities, dependencies, resource requirements and delivery timeframes.
- Coordinate inputs from technical and enabling teams and resolve gaps, overlaps, or sequencing issues affecting delivery.
- Ensure activities respond to provider priorities and are consistent with approved program strategies, plans and commitments.
- Convene regular implementation meetings and maintain clear records of decisions, actions and accountabilities.

## **Resource and Operational Management**

- Translate activity plans into realistic budget, staffing, procurement and logistical requirements.
- Work with the Operations team to align forecasts, procurement plans, compliance requirements, resource availability, contracting, travel and payments with implementation schedules.
- Monitor expenditure and staff allocations against approved plans, investigate variances and recommend timely corrective action.
- Confirm that funds, people and other inputs are available when required and are used efficiently, transparently and for their intended purpose.
- Prepare and maintain activity-level costings, cash-flow forecasts and resource plans that support funding decisions and demonstrate value for money.
- Support accurate financial and operational reporting while maintaining appropriate records and compliance with applicable policies and procedures.

## **Team Leadership**

- Provide day-to-day leadership, direction and workload coordination for the Activity Support Team.
- Set clear expectations, delegate responsibilities, monitor performance and provide regular coaching and feedback.
- Promote collaboration, accountability, safeguarding, inclusion and respectful workplace practices.
- Identify capability needs and support staff development and continuous improvement.

## **Training Provider and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Maintain productive working relationships with RTCs, training providers, relevant government counterparts, communities, industry and program partners.
- Coordinate consultation, assessment, planning and follow-up with providers so that support is practical, demand-led and locally appropriate.
- Communicate plans, roles, expectations, progress and changes clearly to internal and external stakeholders.
- Coordinate transparent provider and cohort selection, partnership agreements and MOUs in line with approved criteria, SITESA processes and program commitments.
- Escalate sensitive, strategic or unresolved issues to the Country Director with options for action.

## **Monitoring, Learning, Risk and Reporting**

- Work with the MEL team to establish activity-level indicators, evidence requirements, and practical data collection arrangements.
- Track delivery against milestones, budgets and intended results, and use evidence and feedback to improve implementation.
- Maintain current activity risks, issues and dependencies, assign mitigation actions and escalate matters that may affect scope, cost, quality, timing, or reputation.
- Provide concise, accurate and timely progress, financial and management reports to the Country Director and contribute to broader program reporting.
- Capture lessons, good practice and examples of change, working with Communications and Partnerships Management to share approved information appropriately.

## **Cross-functional Coordination**

- Coordinate closely with Skills Delivery and Skills Development Reform teams to align institutional strengthening with technical assistance, training delivery and reform priorities.
- Work with Communications to plan appropriate visibility, knowledge products and stakeholder communications.
- Partner with Operations, MEL and Partnerships Management to ensure coherent delivery, compliance, evidence use and relationship management.
- Maintain an integrated portfolio view, actively managing sequencing, shared resources, provider readiness and dependencies between institutional strengthening and Technical College transition.
- Undertake other reasonable duties aligned with the role and program objectives, as directed by the Country Director.

**Selection Criteria**

### **Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- Tertiary qualification in skills development, education, combined with qualifications in project management, business development, international development or a related field; or substantial equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, multi-stakeholder activities, preferably in skills development and in school systems strengthening.
- Strong project management capability, including work planning, scheduling, budget monitoring, resource allocation, risk management, and reporting.
- Experience coordinating finance, procurement, logistics and technical inputs to meet delivery milestones.
- Proven ability to lead and supervise staff, manage workloads, and support individual and team performance.
- Strong relationship-management skills and experience working with training providers, government, communities, development partners or similar stakeholders.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation and interpersonal skills, including the ability to present clear advice to senior management.
- Strong analytical, organisational, problem-solving and time-management skills, with attention to detail and follow-through.
- Ability to work effectively across diverse, cross-cultural and geographically dispersed teams and to travel within Solomon Islands as required.
- Experience working on international development programs in Solomon Islands, Melanesia or the wider Pacific.
- Knowledge of the Solomon Islands technical and vocational education and training environment, including RTC operating contexts.
- Experience engaging with donors and managing partner agreements or grants.

### **Desirable**

- Demonstrated high level of customer service skills with experience in solving problems associated with highly complex systems.
- Demonstrated high level of interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills including the ability to relate effectively, collaboratively and ethically to staff, learners and other stakeholders (including the ability to liaise with industry and partner institutions).

jobs.title: Social Citizenship Education Assistant - Vanuatu
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Human Rights and Social Development Division -** For over 20 years SPC has operated as the region’s pioneer in human rights and gender capacity building to Pacific states, institutions and civil society. Through a team of regional advisors and Country Focal Officers (CFOs) based in member states, it provides a comprehensive suite of policy and legislative advice, technical assistance and capacity building to support Pacific states to respond effectively to priority regional human rights priorities, such as gender equality, ending violence against women and children, disability rights, climate change and equitable, sustainable development.

The **Social Citizenship Education Assistant - Vanuatu** will provide support, coordination, monitoring and facilitation of government and SPC’s formal and informal education work at the national level. The role will be responsible for implementing SPC’s component of the Pacific Partnership to End Violence against Women and Girls project in the Republic of Vanuatu.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Country Plan Implementation**

- In consultation with host Ministry and other relevant stakeholders, develops results-focussed, strategic, accurate and realistic annual and six-month work plans, M & E plan and budget.
- Ensures annual work plan is aligned to both the Pacific Partnership EVAWG project objectives and national education priorities.
- Ensures effective implementation of activities and programs in the annual work plan.
- Maintains accurate financial records evidenced by accurate and compliant quarterly financial reports.
- Communicates with the MOET Supervisor on a weekly basis to plan work, implement and providing regular feedback.
- Provides monthly reports of work to the MOET and HRSD Supervisors.
- Communicates with Pacific Partnership EVAWG Project Coordinator (supervisor) on a fortnightly basis, at a minimum.
- Provides quarterly narrative and financial reports to SPC Pacific Partnership EVAWG Project Coordinator in Suva.
- Supports SPC Pacific Partnership EVAWG project activities at the country level.
- Research and updates Pacific Partnership EVAWG Programme Manager on education systems and practices changes in country in close consultation with Focal Person for Education.

**Training and capacity building**

- Supports in-country capacity development programs for pilot schools, capacity building content includes human rights, gender equality and EVAWG.
- Delivers, with Suva staff and Country Programme Associate, capacity building programmes for schools and school communities, drawing on locally available resources and skills.
- Plans and implements appropriate training methodologies for child and adult learners.
- Implements a range of capacity building modalities to build the capacity of schools and school communities, for example through coaching, mentoring, technical assistance.
- Ensures M & E of capacity building interventions.
- Reports on capacity building outcomes.

**Providing Technical Assistance**

- Provides technical assistance (TA) to Host Ministry/Department of Education, in collaboration with SPC Suva staff, regarding the inclusion of human rights and gender equality education in schools.
- Provides coordination and technical assistance to education committees working on the integration of human rights and gender equality education in schools.
- Identifies national education sector human rights and gender equality capacity needs through research, consultations and monitoring data.
- Contributes to the division communications and publications in relation to human rights and gender equality education.
- Maintains information flow through sharing of reports and resource materials on human rights and gender equality education in schools.

**Networking and Partnership**

- Represents SPC effectively at national, regional and international forums vis-à-vis the Pacific Partnership EVAWG project;
- Shares information on Pacific Partnership EVAWG project progress and outcomes with key stakeholders.
- Establishes, strengthens and supports partnerships that advance Human Rights and Social Development Division and Pacific Partnership EVAWG project objectives at national, regional and international levels.
- Ensures that key education stakeholders at the national level are communicating with each other towards common human rights, gender equality and EVAWG goals.

**Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Identifies and documents success stories, case studies and outcomes of Pacific Partnership EVAWG project, including photos demonstrating work in country under the project.
- Researches and maintains up-to-date data on core national educational priorities.
- Contributes to design and implementation of effective M & E system for country work using both qualitative and quantitative indicators.
- Contributes to Pacific Partnership EVAWG project donor reports.
- Applies learnings to improve programme performance.
- Identifies and documents performance stories, case studies and outcomes of SPC Pacific Partnership EVAWG project work in country.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Tertiary qualifications from a recognized university in education, social and gender analysis or development or equivalent body of knowledge and experience

**Technical expertise**

- At least five years’ experience working in the fields of formal education, community development, training and assessment, monitoring and evaluation in Vanuatu.
- Good knowledge of Vanuatu and an understanding of education and broader development challenges in the country and region.
- Proven ability to work independently.
- Proven experience in report writing, analysis, financial and narrative project reporting.
- Basic accounting and financial literacy skills.
- Basic computer literacy.

**Language skills**

- Competency and fluency in the English and Bislama languages.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal communications skills and a commitment to teamwork.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This position is budgeted until 31 December 2027.

**Remuneration –** The **Social Citizenship Education Assistant - Vanuatu** is a Band 7 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a salary range of VUV 175,257-219,071 per month. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration being given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised locally (EPAL) whose duty station is Port Vila –** SPC provides medical and life insurance for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 days of annual leave and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

**Please note that applicants must be Vanuatu Nationals currently residing in the country, or hold the proper work permit for salaried employment there.**

jobs.title: National Officer - Disability Inclusion (Solomon Islands Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23712**
Position Title: **National Officer - Disability Inclusion (Solomon Islands Nationals Only)**
Duty Station City: **Honiara**
Duty Station Country: **Solomon Islands**
Grade: **NO-A**
Contract Type: **Special Short Term Graded**
Recruiting Type: **General Service**
Vacancy Type: **Special Vacancy Notice**
Initial duration: **5 months**
Closing date: **05 November 2026**

**Context:**

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Fiji and the direct supervision of the Project Manager (PM), the National Project Officer – Disability Inclusion will be responsible and accountable for supporting the implementation of programming related to disaster displacements and strengthening resilience to disasters and climate change-related fragility in Solomon Islands. The position will also support programming aimed at strengthening the resilience of persons with disabilities, youth, older persons and women. In addition, the incumbent will support the design and implementation of disability-inclusive early warning systems (EWS), the development of related information, education and communication (IEC) materials, delivery of relevant inclusive trainings, and Community-Based Disaster Response Management (CBDRM).
The incumbent will support community level activities, coordinate with government partners (both national and provincial), and directly work with persons with disabilities, youth, women and older persons.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

1. Under the supervision of the Project Manager, assist in the implementation and monitoring of activities related to disaster preparedness and response, including the coordination of the financial, logistical, administrative and technical aspects in accordance with IOM’s policies.
2. Provide technical input and support the implementation of disability-inclusive disaster preparedness and response activities for IOM Solomon Islands, including CBDRM and EWS for persons with disabilities, women, youth and older persons.
3. Monitor project implementation against approved work plans; document and evaluate results; identify gaps, deviations and bottlenecks; keep the supervisor informed; and suggest actions to improve implementation.
4. Contribute to the integration and mainstreaming of gender, protection, human rights and other pertinent cross-cutting issues into programme implementation.
5. Assist in identifying potential areas for project development and contribute to the development of new projects by selecting and summarizing background information, assessing the local context and drafting segments of project proposals.
6. Coordinate the timely preparation and dissemination of project reports, provide inputs and feedback as required, and facilitate compliance with IOM procedures and donor requirements.
7. Liaise and coordinate with government entities, implementing partners, United Nations (UN) agencies, civil society, donors and other stakeholders.
8. Contribute to the planning, development, organization and delivery of capacity building activities for IOM staff, partners, government officials, and other humanitarian actors.
9. Participate in relevant conferences, working groups, workshops, steering committees, and other forums.
10. Undertake duty travel as required related to project implementation and monitoring.
11. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- Master’s degree in Political Science, Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution; or,
- Bachelor’s degree in the above fields with two years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Experience implementing programming related to climate change and human mobility and/or disaster risk reduction, including CBDRM, disaster risk reduction (DRR) Preparedness, and EWS;
- Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations;
- Experience supporting the design and implementation of accessible and inclusive programming for persons with disabilities, youth, older persons and women, preferably in a disaster-preparedness or disaster-risk-reduction context;
- Experience in developing training materials and facilitating training, knowledge sharing, and learning events; and,
- Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organizations in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of disability inclusion principles and their application to disaster preparedness, disaster risk reduction and community-based programming;
- Knowledge of inclusive early warning systems, CBDRM and accessible communication approaches;
- Ability to analyze and present project information clearly and concisely to diverse audiences;
- Ability to support inclusive consultations, training activities and community engagement; and
- Knowledge of project implementation, monitoring and donor-reporting requirements.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and Pidjin is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this [link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)
