jobs.title: Data Entry Assistants
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/203**
- **Position Title**: Data Entry Assistants
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 2 Months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 21 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 28 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T8NzJatEZrMJtUOG7VOGUkM1-S9Ncvbm/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T8NzJatEZrMJtUOG7VOGUkM1-S9Ncvbm/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon stands at a pivotal juncture in its governance and reform trajectory. Despite years of overlapping crises, the country has made landmark progress in building an integrity and anti-corruption framework, including the adoption and (partial) implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (2020–2025), the establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), and major legislative reforms on access to information, illicit enrichment, whistleblower protection, asset declaration, and public procurement. These milestones have laid the groundwork for the most coherent accountability architecture in Lebanon’s recent history.

However, these achievements remain fragile amid deep economic collapse, weakened institutions, and eroded public trust. While the strategic and legal frameworks are largely in place, implementation and enforcement mechanisms remain underdeveloped, and coordination among oversight institutions is still limited. The evaluation of the NACS highlighted the urgent need to consolidate progress by operationalizing national mechanisms, strengthening institutional capacities, and embedding corruption-risk management practices across public institutions.

In this context, the Integrity in ACTion Project is founded with the objective of improving the implementation of an institutionalised and targeted approach to prevent and combat corruption through improved coordination, operationalized oversight, enhanced preventive and enforcement mechanisms, and institutionalized integrity and risk-management practices, thereby advancing transparency, accountability, and public trust. The Project is designed to achieve this objective by working on three outputs:

Output 1: Institutional capacities to coordinate, monitor, and evaluate the National Anti-Corruption Strategy strengthened and operationalized through participatory and inclusive mechanisms.

Output 2: Legal frameworks and oversight institutions for preventing and combating corruption strengthened and effectively operationalized.

Output 3: Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.

Under output 3, “Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.”, the Ministry of Industry, in collaboration with UNDP, is working to integrate the Sectoral Corruption Risk Management (SCRM) Methodology into its core regulatory functions. This partnership seeks to strengthen institutional integrity, reduce opportunities for corruption, and reinforce rule-based decision-making in the industrial licensing process. By applying the SCRM framework to the directorates/sections responsible for Industrial Permits and Certificates, the initiative has aimed to identify systemic vulnerabilities, enhance risk awareness among staff, and promote a culture of accountability. Furthermore, the Ministry of Industry (MoI) plays a central role in regulating Lebanon’s industrial sector and ensuring compliance with national standards and licensing requirements. At the heart of this mandate lies the responsibility to oversee the issuance of Industrial Permits and Certificates, an essential function for enabling lawful industrial activity, protecting the environment, and promoting sustainable economic development.

Building on UNDP’s support to the ministry of Industry, UNDP is seeking to contract admin assistants to support the ministry in organizing the Ministry's records of industrial permits and industrial certificates into a structured database. The database will use consistent fields and unique identifiers so that it can later be linked to the digitized inspection system. This will also allow the Ministry to track each establishment's permits, certificates, inspections and compliance status over time, and to update them as new inspections are carried out.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP IACT manager, and in close coordination with the NACC, the Admin Assistants will support coordination, documentation, and administrative follow-up functions. The Admin Assistant will be responsible for the following:

- Review the Ministry’s existing permit and certificate files and recording practices. Prepare a short inception note with a work plan, the proposed approach, and a timeline, and agree on it with the technical committee.
- Propose and finalize, in coordination with the committee, the database structure. This includes standardized fields, data formats, and a unique identifier for each establishment and each permit or certificate. The design should allow the database to be linked later to the digitized inspection system.
- Review existing permit and certificate files and sort them, for example:
- by document type (industrial permit or industrial certificate)
- by the five UIIS industrial clusters
- by subsector and activity classification
- Initiate data entry for each establishment, record the key information, including but not limited to:
- permit or certificate number
- issue and expiry dates
- current status
- location
- available inspection and compliance records
- Apply the filtering and classification criteria agreed by the technical committee consistently across all records.
- Identify and flag incomplete, duplicate, or inconsistent records. Maintain a log of flagged records and submit it to the committee for review and decision.
- Update the database as files are verified or corrected by the committee, so that the database stays accurate and current.
- Prepare a brief user guide or data dictionary describing the fields, codes, and update procedures.
- Submit a final report at the end of the assignment, summarizing records processed, data gaps identified, and recommendations for maintaining the database and integrating it with the inspection system.
- Ensure that all information is handled with strict confidentiality, in line with Ministry and UNDP rules. The consultant will not take part in any decision on individual applications, permits, certificates, or files.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities noting that the total duration should not exceed 2 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the day-to-day management of the Ministry of Industry relevant staff.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day to Day transportation from home to office (& vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 2 months.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed 2 months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The Admin Assistants will be based in Beirut in the Ministry of Industry premises.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** At least a High School certificate.
- **Experience:** A minimum of 1 year of Experience in administrative or operational support, including but not limited to, data entry, maintaining filing systems, preparing administrative documentation, and conducting research, etc.
- **Language:** Fluency in Arabic and English.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
The position is open to qualified individuals with experience working in Southern and Eastern Africa. The successful candidate will be expected to work from the REPSSI Head Quarters in Randburg, South Africa.

REPSSI (the Regional Psychosocial Support Initiative) is a renowned pan African organisation that has been supporting governments and non-governmental organisations to provide holistic psychosocial care and support to children and their families in East and Southern Africa for 20 years now. REPSSI works in 13 countries and aims to enhance the psychosocial and mental wellbeing of girls, boys, youth their families and communities to be able to respond to challenges such as HIV and AIDS, conflict, poverty, climate change, environmental disasters and social strife.

The 2026- 2030 strategy is anchored in five SMART outcomes that reflect our intent to deliver mental health and psychosocial wellbeing at scale, with integrity and impact;

- **We will mobilize at least $35 million in diversified funding** to sustain and scale our work across 13 countries, with 60% of new resources aligned to our strategic priorities and community partners.
- **We will generate and disseminate 20 high-quality evidence products**—including regional studies, policy briefs, and practice guides—that influence MHPSS policy and programming across East and Southern Africa.
- **We will ensure that 90% of our direct service delivery meets or exceeds quality benchmarks**, as defined by our regional MERL standards and validated through community feedback and independent surveys and evaluations.
- **We will strengthen the capacity of 250 local organizations and government systems** to deliver integrated, gender-responsive MHPSS services, with at least 50% of these led by youth, women, or marginalized groups and key populations.
- **We will embed psychosocial wellbeing into 10 regional and national policy frameworks**, positioning MHPSS as a core pillar of social protection, education, and climate resilience.

**Job Summary**

REPSSI seeks to appoint an experienced and vibrant **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)** who will provide over-arching inspirational leadership to a dynamic organization operating in a fast paced, highly competitive environment with a national, regional and international footprint. Together with the Board, the CEO assures REPSSI’s relevance to the community, the accomplishment of REPSSI’s mission and vision, and the accountability of REPSSI to its diverse constituents. To thrive as a CEO, you must be a prudent manager and inspiring leader with business acumen who will take bold actions to enhance REPSSI’s global standing as the leading African psychosocial support advocate and provider of technical expertise.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic and Executive Leadership**

Provide visionary strategic leadership, develop, review and ensure effective implementation of the strategic plan for REPSSI to maintain its cutting edge in a competitive market; guide business plans for the REPSSI programmes; ensure effective management of REPSSI’s executive team and day-to-day operations.

**Strategic stakeholder management**

Maintain good relations with current development partners at national, regional and international levels; identify potential / new strategic partners and opportunities; and ensure active and meaningful contribution to strategic partnerships. Lead in ensuring expansion of REPSSI’s reputation and brand through innovative communication mechanisms.

**Resource mobilization**

Engage in aggressive resource mobilization with traditional and non-traditional partners, securing new and additional resources and maximising existing resources.

**Financial sustainability**

Oversee the development and effective management of annual budgets; ensure proper control over expenditure and report accordingly; complete risk analysis on potential investments and advise the Board of Directors with regard to investment risk and return; ensure compliance with all audit requirements; sustain an unqualified audit opinion.

**Research and innovation**

Provide strategic and thought leadership on REPSSI’s key competencies and its role appropriately internally and externally.

**Programme development, delivery and training**

Lead and assure programme quality through development of bold programme elements to respond to new research and opportunities; and organizational stability through implementation of standards and controls, systems and procedures, with regular evaluation.

**Human resources and transformation**

Motivates and leads a high performance management team dispersed in thirteen African countries, and provides mentoring as a cornerstone to career development for the team.

**Board Secretariat and Support**

Provide timely and reliable reports and information to the board and members.

Assist the Board exercise its oversight responsibilities and fiduciary duties.

**Essential Skills and Personality Traits:**

- Strategic leadership and financial management experience
- In-depth knowledge of corporate governance and general management practice
- An entrepreneurial mindset with excellent organizational and leadership skills
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
- Strong negotiation and advocacy skills
- Must thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced, and challenging programme environment
- Ability to set ambitious targets and drive to exceed them
- Ability to work outside of conventional office hours, and across time zones
- Knowledge of Psychosocial Support and Mental Health in Africa
- Strong ethical and governance leadership

**Minimum Qualifications and Experience:**

- Masters degree in Social Sciences or Management or relevant field
- 8 years of experience in a senior leadership position in a relevant field
- 10 years overall relevant professional experience
- Management experience of a global or multi branch organization preferred
- Significant resource mobilisation and advocacy experience (not negotiable)
- Willingness to travel – the position requires up to 50% travel regionally/internationally

This is a 5-year contract position subject to availability of donor funding and good performance.

Remuneration will be commensurate with skills and experience. REPSSI is committed to the principles of employment equity.

jobs.title: Trauma and Healing Expert
jobs.description:
**About Badael**

Badael e.V. is a Syrian rights-based organisation working to foster transformative justice for sustainable peace in Syria. Through feminist, rights-based and participatory approaches, Badael works with grassroots actors and communities to strengthen their agency and ability to shape processes related to justice, reconciliation, peacebuilding and inclusive governance.

**Scope of Work**

**Phase I**: **Inception and contextualisation**

At the beginning of the assignment, the expert(s) will:

- Review the project proposal, reconciliation approach, relevant project materials and existing methodologies provided by Badael.
- Meet with Badael’s team and relevant external experts/trainers to develop a shared understanding of the project, its justice-based reconciliation approach, target groups and implementation context.
- Understand the role of the women participating in the training as peacebuilders, grassroots leaders and facilitators of community reconciliation and inter-group dialogue rather than as mental health practitioners.
- Identify the principal psychosocial and trauma-related considerations relevant to facilitating reconciliation and inter-group dialogue in conflict-affected and socially fragmented communities.
- Contextualise the training approach to the realities of the four project locations and the experiences and roles of participating women.

**Phase II**: **Development of the training methodology and materials**

The expert(s) will develop a structured four-day training programme on Trauma-Informed and Psychosocially Safe Practice specifically tailored to women engaged in reconciliation and inter-group dialogue.

The training should combine conceptual understanding with practical application and should address, at minimum:

- Basic understanding of trauma, prolonged stress and psychosocial wellbeing in conflict-affected settings.
- Individual and collective dimensions of trauma and their relevance to community relationships and reconciliation.
- How trauma, fear, grief, loss and insecurity can manifest within dialogue and reconciliation spaces.
- Understanding triggers and recognising signs of distress without diagnosing participants.
- Principles of trauma-informed practice and their application to peacebuilding and reconciliation.
- Creating emotionally and psychosocially safer spaces for dialogue.
- Preventing unintended harm and re-traumatisation.
- Facilitation approaches when participants share experiences of violence, loss or other potentially traumatic experiences.
- Managing emotionally intense moments, conflict and distress within group processes.
- Boundaries of the facilitator's role and distinguishing psychosocially informed facilitation from psychological or therapeutic intervention.
- Power, identity, gender and intersectionality in relation to trauma and psychosocial safety.
- Self-awareness and the emotional impact of facilitation on women peacebuilders themselves.
- Self-care, collective care and approaches to reducing burnout, secondary stress and emotional exhaustion.
- Practical approaches that women facilitators can integrate into the design and implementation of community reconciliation and inter-group dialogue initiatives.

The methodology should be highly participatory and practice-oriented, making appropriate use of case studies, scenarios, facilitated reflection, group exercises, simulations and practical tools. Activities should themselves model trauma-informed and psychosocially safe facilitation and should not require participants to disclose personal traumatic experiences.

**Phase III: Delivery of four in-person workshops**

- The expert(s) will deliver four four-day in-person workshops, one in each project location, targeting approximately 20 women per workshop.
- Participants will primarily include representatives of women-led or women-focused groups, grassroots women leaders, independent activists, women peacebuilders and practitioners engaged in or preparing to engage in community reconciliation, inter-group dialogue, mediation, civic engagement and related community processes.
- The workshops should enable participants to apply trauma-informed principles directly to situations they are likely to encounter while facilitating community reconciliation and inter-group dialogue.
- Delivery should be participatory, feminist, inclusive, culturally and contextually sensitive, and responsive to differences in participants' experiences and levels of prior knowledge.

**Expected Deliverables**

The consultancy is expected to produce the following deliverables:

1. Inception meeting and brief methodological plan, including the proposed approach, sequencing and coordination arrangements.
2. Four-day training curriculum and methodology on Trauma-Informed and Psychosocially Safe Practice, contextualised to women-led reconciliation and inter-group dialogue.
3. Delivery of four in-person workshops, one in each project location targeting approximately 20 women per workshop.
4. Post-workshop reflection/debriefing with Badael following each workshop or training cycle.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

The expert, or collectively the proposed team, should demonstrate:

- An advanced university degree in psychology, clinical psychology, counselling psychology, psychosocial support, mental health, or another directly relevant discipline.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in trauma-informed practice, psychosocial support, mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, or closely related areas.
- Demonstrated experience designing and delivering training on trauma-informed and psychosocially safe practice.
- Strong understanding of trauma and psychosocial dynamics in conflict-affected environments.
- Demonstrated experience translating psychological and psychosocial concepts into practical approaches for non-specialist practitioners.
- Experience working with civil society actors, community facilitators, women leaders, peacebuilders or similar groups.
- Knowledge of safeguarding, Do No Harm and ethical approaches to working with people affected by conflict and violence.
- Fluency in Arabic, including the ability to deliver professional training in Arabic.

jobs.title: Policy and Communications Advisor
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Scope of Work**

The Policy and Communications Advisor (PCA), Education is responsible for supporting the Senior Director and Education Leadership Team (ELT) in implementing the IRC’s established strategy for influencing external policies and practices, to ensure IRC’s programming, policy and research have a greater impact on our clients. The Policy and Communications Advisor carries out specific policy and advocacy work within this strategy, including writing presentations and think pieces for large audiences, and representing the Education Technical Unit as needed. S/he will help identify relevant relationships and partnerships for the IRC, appraise meetings and opportunities within an agreed remit, attend relevant meetings, and support with follow up. S/he works closely with the Senior Director and is part of the Education Senior Management Team (SMT). The Advisor also serves as the Education Technical Unit’s primary liaison with IRC’s External Relations and Communications teams, ensuring accurate and timely representation of Education’s work across internal and external channels. The Advisor will engage closely with colleagues in Communications, International Philanthropy and Partnerships and Awards Management Unit.

*This role is open to candidates located in and with the legal right to work in the United Kingdom or Germany.*

*This position is expected to end on 10/31/2028.*

**Responsibilities**

***1. Support delivery of IRC’s influence strategy for education***

- With the Senior Director and ELT, support implementation of the agreed strategic direction for the external policies and practices the IRC seeks to influence, to achieve the biggest impact in early childhood development and education in conflict and crisis contexts.
- Identify strategic opportunities, tactics and audiences that will most effectively influence policies and practices of our targets and raise our profile as needed to achieve impact.
- Seek out and appraise opportunities for policy advocacy and engagement on a regular basis; be disciplined and discriminating in this appraisal to make best use of scarce resources.
- Alongside the Director and Deputy Director, help Country Offices to understand, deliver and advocate for IRC’s education strategy.
- Support internal profile raising around IRC’s education portfolio including preparing presentations, Brown Bags, and regular updates for an internal audience through newsletters etc.
- Work closely with the Policy and Advocacy Department tointegrate education / ECD into global objectives for humanitarian reform and high-level talking points for IRC’s CEO.

***2. Support with executing Global Education Strategy***

- Coordinate and support with strategic opportunities, including but not limited to:
- Arrange and attend meetings to further IRC’s education policy goals;
- Draft talking points and accompanying materials for presentations and present as needed,
- Write / edit think pieces and content showcasing IRC’s programs and evidence;
- Inputting into global consultations and frameworks;
- Horizon scan global trends/donor developments and policy landscape;
- Choreograph key policy events with support from the Education TU Unit Manager;
- Maintain a collection of core briefs and policy documents for use by program teams; Country Offices and headquarters.

***3. Communications liaison and materials***

- Serve as the Education Technical Unit’s point of contact with IRC’s External Relations and Communications teams on media opportunities and relevant content for IRC’s digital channels (rescue.org, social media).
- Support fact-checking and review of communications materials (press releases, op-eds, reports) drafted by global Communications to ensure technical accuracy.
- Maintain and update the Education Unit’s core library of briefs and communications products, including corresponding content on rescue.org’s education pages, in coordination with Internal Communications.
- Support review of donor-facing and marketing materials for accuracy and appropriate tone, in coordination with Fundraising colleagues.

***4. Provide coordination support to the Senior Director for Education***

- Help coordinate relevant meetings and fora for the Senior Director and ELT on education and early childhood development; flag opportunities and requests for the Senior leadership’s time*.*
- Coordinate and participate in opportunities alongside senior leadership; ensure follow-up*.*

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Senior Director, Education.
- Position directly supervises: No current direct reports, potential for supervision of consultants, specialists, or officers as work evolves.
- Indirect Reporting: Deputy Director, Global Practice Leads and US and European Policy and Advocacy Departments.
- Internal: position is part of the Education Senior Management Team (SMT). Works closely with colleagues in Communications and External Relations.
- External: education in emergencies, development and humanitarian stakeholders, policy makers and advocates.

**Professional Profile**

Success in this position requires an individual with strong policy and advocacy skills, expertise in development or humanitarian settings and a keen interest in furthering IRC’s strategy and vision. Expertise in education is preferred but not essential.

**Work Experience:**

- A minimum of 6-8 years of relevant experience, with field and programmatic experience in a donor, NGO or comparable international agency required.
- Experience and familiarity with donors, peer agencies and national contexts required, preferably in education, humanitarian and transitional, post-crisis contexts.
- Experience and expertise raising funds from bilateral, multilateral, and private donors.
- Experience producing communications materials (press-facing content, digital/social content, donor materials) for diverse audiences, in addition to policy/advocacy products.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Self-directed, able to independently set priorities and solve problems within established procedures and guidance from the Senior Director; comfortable working for a supervisor who is remotely located.
- Excellent interpersonal and oral and written communication skills; demonstrated ability to successfully work in a fast-paced environment and develop positive relationships with locally and remote based staff.
- Highly effective strategic planning, policy development and execution.
- Private and statutory business development/ fundraising.
- Excellent writing skills, with the ability to translate technical and programmatic content into clear, audience-appropriate language across formats and channels.
- Experience contributing to or managing social media content in a professional context (preferred).

**Education:** First degree in relevant field.

**Language Skills:** Excellent spoken and written English essential. Proficiency in additional IRC relevant languages (Arabic, French, Spanish, Kiswahili, etc.) strongly preferred.

**Working Environment:** Travel may be required.

**Compensation:** (London/UK: GBP 52,210 - GBP 61,999/Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Safeguarding Advisor - Francophone
jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

The Safeguarding Adviser role primarily supports the effective implementation of MSI’s Safeguarding work and Code of Conduct in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, DRC and Madagascar. Using relevant materials and resources, it also supports LSDC’s training programme on other subjects such as AFB, practical Data Privacy and Due Diligence *(together with Safeguarding and Code of Conduct*, “Core Policies”).

As Safeguarding Adviser, you will be expected to have experience in designing and delivering effective behaviour change programmes, promoting an in-depth understanding of the conduct expected of team members, creating a supportive organisational culture which values team member feedback, and quickly responds to concerns raised. The Safeguarding Adviser is also responsible for monitoring safeguarding implementation and reporting on compliance in line with policy and donor expectations.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Excellent verbal and written communicator: ability to convey concepts and influence behaviour in plain English and French to non-technical audiences
- Ability to organise and prioritise workloads to meet deadlines
- A people centred approach and passion for working on people focused behaviour change initiatives
- Strong people skills: ability to build and manage relationships with other stakeholders quickly and effectively
- Ability to maintain confidentiality, recognising when to escalate issues and respond to urgent issues
- Excellent problem-solving skills, with ability to think laterally when confronted with problems
- Excellent report writing skills
- Ability to work as part of a team and with cross-department stakeholders to deliver on projects

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Designing and delivering effective face-to-face and remote learning programmes and behaviour change initiatives (essential)
- Experience in Safeguarding in Africa (essential)
- Implementing policies and guidance (essential)
- Incident investigation, documentation, and reporting (desirable)
- Familiarity with the Core Policies referenced above (desirable)
- Effectively managing stakeholder needs and expectations (essential)
- Managing a significant cross departmental and/or international workload which involves the need to prioritise, plan, collaborate etc (desirable)

**Formal education/qualification**

- No formal education / qualification requirements

Please see job description [here.](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2026.10.07-Safeguarding-Advisor-JD-.pdf)

**Location:** Dakar, Senegal

**Full-time:** 40 hours per week

**Contract type: Fixed Term to end 2028.**

**Salary**: Competitive

**Closing date: 12th November 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be positioned within the existing salary structure of the country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

jobs.title: GCF Project Manager-National-Damascus
jobs.description:
**TEAM/PROGRAMME:** Programme Development and Quality (PDQ)
**LOCATION:** Damascus / Syria Country Office, with travel to relevant locations as required
**GRADE**: 2
**CONTRACT LENGTH:** Fixed term – 9 months
**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**
Level 3: The post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work in country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process for staff.

**ROLE PURPOSE:**
The GCF Project Manager will provide country-level coordination and project management support for the implementation of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) Project Preparation Facility (PPF) and the preparation of the full GCF project for Syria.
The post holder will coordinate the delivery of PPF activities and assessments in close collaboration with Save the Children, the Government of Syria, relevant ministries and authorities, local partners, consultants, technical specialists and other stakeholders. The role will ensure that PPF activities and assessments are well coordinated, delivered according to agreed timelines and budgets, and supported by appropriate stakeholder engagement, consultation and evidence generation. The post holder will organise and facilitate workshops, consultations and technical meetings; coordinate government and partner engagement; support the mobilisation and management of consultants; monitor data collection and technical deliverables; maintain project documentation and tracking systems; and support the preparation of the GCF funding proposal and associated project documentation.
The GCF Project Manager will serve as a key coordination focal point between the country-level team, MO team, consultants, government stakeholders and local partners, ensuring that inputs are consolidated and actions are followed up in a timely manner.
The role will also support quality assurance, risk management, reporting, learning and knowledge management throughout the PPF process and contribute to ensuring that the proposed GCF project is technically sound, conflict-sensitive, child-centred, aligned with national priorities and responsive to the needs and priorities identified through the project preparation process.
**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

Reports to: Operations Director

Staff reporting to this post: No direct line management responsibility. The post holder will report to PDQD for technical aspects of the proposal development. The post holder will coordinate and provide day-to-day support to consultants, partners and relevant internal teams involved in PPF activities. The role will also work closely with the Climate Resilience Global and Member Technical Advisors. The role will be expected to also maintain close coordination with other countries part of the proposal

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY**
1\. GCF PPF Project Management and Coordination
• Coordinate the activities of the GCF Proposal Preparation Facility (PPF) activities and assessments at country level in accordance with the approved workplan, budget, timelines and agreed responsibilities to put together a strong proposal
• Develop and maintain a detailed PPF implementation tracker covering activities, milestones, responsibilities, deliverables, dependencies and deadlines.
• Coordinate inputs from Save the Children teams, consultants, local partners, government stakeholders and other relevant actors.
• Monitor progress against the PPF workplan and proactively identify delays, gaps, risks and required follow-up actions.
• Organise regular coordination meetings with Syria team and Member office teams and ensure that agreed actions are documented, assigned and followed up.
• Maintain an up-to-date overview of all PPF activities, deliverables, consultations, technical studies and project preparation requirements.
• Support the Project Lead/management team in identifying and addressing implementation bottlenecks and coordination issues.
2\. Stakeholder and Government Engagement
• Support and facilitate engagement with relevant government ministries, authorities and GCF-related national stakeholders (Particularly NDA) throughout the PPF process.
• Coordinate meetings, consultations, technical discussions and validation processes with government counterparts and other stakeholders.
• Support the preparation of agendas, presentations, briefing materials, meeting notes and follow-up actions.
• Maintain regular communication with relevant government focal points and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions and requests.
• Support the process of securing relevant government inputs, endorsements, clearances and other documentation required for GCF project preparation.
• Support coordination with national and sub-national stakeholders in target locations.
3\. Workshops, Consultations and Technical Meetings
• Lead the logistical and coordination arrangements for PPF workshops, consultations, validation meetings and technical sessions.
• Coordinate participant invitations, agendas, presentations, background materials, logistics and documentation.
• Support consultants and technical teams to prepare consultation materials and facilitate data and information collection.
• Ensure that workshop and consultation outputs are properly documented and incorporated into relevant project preparation deliverables.
• Support participatory processes involving government, partners, communities, children and other relevant stakeholders, as appropriate.
• Maintain an organised record of consultation findings, recommendations and agreed actions.
4\. Consultant and Technical Support Management
• Support the mobilisation and onboarding of consultants and technical experts engaged under the PPF in coordination with the Technical Advisors.
• Coordinate communication between consultants, SCI teams, partners and government stakeholders.
• Support consultants in accessing relevant data, documents, stakeholders and field-level information.
• Monitor consultant workplans, timelines, data collection processes and deliverables against agreed terms of reference.
5\. Data Collection, Evidence and Knowledge Management
• Coordinate and monitor data and information collection required for the GCF project preparation process.
• Work with consultants, partners and technical teams to identify data gaps and facilitate access to relevant national, sectoral and local information.
• Maintain a database/tracker of key data sources, assessments, studies, consultation findings and evidence generated through the PPF.
• Support documentation of lessons learned, good practices and recommendations emerging from the PPF process.
6\. Partnership Coordination
• Support effective coordination between Save the Children, consultants, and local partners involved in the GCF PPF.
• Coordinate partner inputs to assessments, consultations, workshops, technical studies, and project design.
• Monitor partner deliverables and agreed contributions to the PPF workplan.
7\. Monitoring, Reporting and Risk Management
• Monitor progress against the PPF workplan, milestones, budget and deliverables.
• Prepare regular internal progress updates and coordination reports highlighting achievements, pending actions, risks and required decisions.
• Maintain a PPF risk and issue tracker and support mitigation and escalation as required.
• Support financial and administrative tracking in coordination with Awards, Finance and Operations teams.
8\. Logistics and Administrative Coordination
• Coordinate logistical and administrative arrangements required for workshops, consultations, field missions, meetings and other PPF activities.
• Work closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, MEAL and other relevant teams to ensure timely delivery of activities.
• Support procurement and contracting processes related to PPF activities, in accordance with SCI policies and procedures.
• Support travel and field mission arrangements for consultants, technical teams and relevant stakeholders where required.
**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)**
Accountability
• Takes responsibility for coordinating activities, following up on agreed actions and ensuring timely delivery.
• Holds partners, consultants and relevant stakeholders accountable for agreed responsibilities while maintaining constructive working relationships.
Ambition
• Demonstrates a strong focus on achieving PPF milestones and preparing a high-quality GCF project.
• Proactively identifies opportunities to improve coordination, efficiency and project quality.
Collaboration
• Builds effective working relationships across SCI teams, government institutions, partners and consultants.
• Facilitates collaboration and information sharing across different technical workstreams.
Creativity
• Identifies practical solutions to coordination, implementation and logistical challenges.
• Adapts approaches to complex and changing humanitarian and operational contexts.
Integrity
• Demonstrates transparency, professionalism and accountability in managing information, relationships and project processes.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:**
Essential
• Bachelor's degree in climate change, environmental sciences, development studies, international development, project management, agriculture or a related field.
• Minimum 4 years of relevant professional experience in project/programme coordination, project management, climate change, resilience, development or humanitarian programming.
• Experience working with government institutions, international organisations, NGOs and/or development partners.
• Strong experience organising workshops, consultations, meetings and stakeholder engagement processes.
• Strong project management, planning, coordination and follow-up skills.
• Experience monitoring deliverables, workplans, timelines and project milestones.
• Strong report writing, documentation and communication skills.
• Excellent English language skills, both written and spoken.
• Strong interpersonal, facilitation and negotiation skills.
Desirable
• Previous experience with the Green Climate Fund (GCF) or other international climate finance mechanisms.
• Experience supporting a GCF Project Preparation Facility (PPF), GCF concept note or funding proposal development process.
• Familiarity with GCF project preparation requirements, investment criteria and funding proposal processes.
• Experience working on climate change adaptation, climate resilience, environmental sustainability or disaster risk reduction programmes.

Additional job responsibilities
The duties and responsibilities set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties commensurate with their skills and experience.
Equal Opportunities
The role holder is required to carry out duties in accordance with SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.
Child Safeguarding:
We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.
Safeguarding our Staff:
The post holder is required to carry out duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy.
Health and Safety
The role holder is required to carry out duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

***“Save the Children does not charge any fees or request any form of payment at any stage of the recruitment process”***

jobs.title: CSOs' Capacity Building Workshop Facilitation
Country Managing Director
jobs.description:
ForAfrika is an African-founded and led organisation with over 40 years of impact across the continent. We partner with communities through our integrated development continuum: saving lives and building resilience to reach self-sufficiency through our Humanitarian & Development work and unlocking commercial viability through our Social Enterprise activities. We are Africans, delivering African-led solutions for Africa, and we stand by our promise: we’re committed to the long run, until the job is done and communities are enabled to thrive.

**Role Thesis**

The Country Managing Director is the accountable leader for the ForAfrika South Africa platform and the principal architect of its next phase of growth and transformation. The MD will steward country operations, impact, people, governance, financial sustainability and risk while building the future South Africa platform. This includes developing the operating model, leadership capability, strategic partnerships, revenue pathways, market positioning, and organizational culture required for long-term success. The role is responsible not only for running the office, but for transforming it into a commercially credible, impact-led and financially resilient platform that can operate effectively across enterprise development, catalytic CSI funding and other appropriate growth opportunities. The MD will build on the foundations established during the interim leadership period and lead the next phase of ForAfrika South Africa's evolution into a market-relevant, scalable and sustainable organization.

**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Group Chief Operations Officer, the Managing Director (MD) is ForAfrika’s senior accountable leader in South Africa, with overall responsibility for the performance, resilience and future relevance of the country platform. The MD owns the full Country Office P&L, impact, revenue, delivery, people and transition outcomes, and is accountable for bringing Pre-Commercial Viability (PCV) and Commercial Transactions/FASE together within a single country strategy and operating model.

A core responsibility of the MD is to build the future South Africa operating platform — transforming the foundations established into a commercially credible, impact-led and sustainable country operation. This includes shaping the organisation, capabilities, leadership and operating systems required to support ForAfrika’s evolution, while protecting existing humanitarian, institutional, government, corporate and community commitments.

The MD translates ForAfrika’s enterprise strategy and 2026–2031 Revenue Plan into an executable country model, balancing strong operational stewardship with the development of new commercial and social enterprise opportunities. The MD brings Social Enterprise, Revenue, Operations, Finance and Impact & Evidence together around one country strategy, one P&L, one operating cadence and one accountable leadership team.

The South Africa Country Office must be flexible by design, balancing institutional funding and public-system strengthening with time-bound pre-commercial viability (PCV), corporate partnerships, transaction-linked opportunities, blended finance and FASE revenue. The MD is accountable for selecting, executing and rebalancing this mix in line with South Africa’s operating context and within enterprise guardrails.

The role therefore requires a leader who can operate simultaneously as country executive, external representative, growth leader, P&L owner and steward of mission, people and risk.

**Key Roles and Responsibilities**

1. **Leadership, Management, and Accountability**

- Model ForAfrika’s core values of Deep Love ForAfrika, Dependability, Compassion, Initiative and Discipline, while building a culture of accountability, collaboration, commercial discipline and timely execution across the South Africa Country Office.
- Translate ForAfrika’s enterprise strategy and the South Africa transformation priorities into clear country plans, Rocks, scorecards, timelines and accountabilities, ensuring the Country Leadership Team is aligned around PCV, FASE, operational delivery, financial sustainability and impact.
- Lead and manage the Country Leadership Team through clear expectations, regular performance reviews, disciplined operating cadences and timely follow-up, ensuring that each leader understands their responsibilities, decision rights and required outcomes.
- Maintain effective management oversight of country P&L, revenue and diversification, contractual delivery, cash and financial sustainability, impact, people, risk and transformation, taking timely corrective action where performance is off track.
- Establish and maintain a consistent Country Office operating cadence, including P&L reviews, pipeline and revenue reviews, delivery reviews, PCV/FASE portfolio reviews, Rocks and scorecards, ensuring issues are identified early, decisions are made and actions are followed through.
- Hold senior leaders accountable for delivery against approved plans and ensure decisions have clear owners, timelines and measurable outcomes, escalating material risks or decisions requiring enterprise approval to the VP Operations/COO.
- Coordinate effectively with GSO functions, FASE, Revenue and other Country Offices on One ForAfrika priorities, ensuring clarity of roles, accountability and execution while avoiding duplication of functional ownership.
- Ensure the South Africa Country Office consistently applies organisational policies, delegated authorities, financial controls, risk and compliance requirements, safeguarding standards and other governance requirements.
- Provide timely, accurate and decision-ready reporting to the VP Operations/COO on country performance, financial sustainability, revenue, delivery, transformation progress, leadership risks and material decisions required.
- Take overall accountability for execution of the approved South Africa strategy and operating model, ensuring that the Country Office protects existing commitments while progressing towards a sustainable, commercially credible and impact-led operating platform

**2. Strategic Mandate**
- Protect today's obligations while building the next operating model. Delivery continuity, safeguarding, duty of care, cash and donor/partner commitments cannot be compromised by transformation.
- Build the future South Africa platform, translating the foundations established into a scalable operating model, high-performing leadership team, differentiated market position and sustainable growth engine.
- Own a differentiated country strategy. Configure the country around its funding mix, humanitarian context, operating maturity, assets, risk profile, leadership capacity and strongest credible revenue pathways.
- Build financial resilience. Reduce dependence on a single donor, programme, affiliate or funding channel through disciplined renewal, replacement, diversification and full-cost recovery.
- Connect operations to growth. Convert local legitimacy, government relationships, operating assets, evidence and technical capability into competitive propositions for donors, governments, corporates, DFIs, investors, primes and strategic partners.
- Operate as One ForAfrika. Share capabilities, intelligence, talent and delivery assets across countries and contribute to multi-country opportunities rather than optimising only for the local office.
- Lead the transition to one Country Office operating platform with clearly governed PCV and Commercial Transactions/FASE lanes.
- Lead the change-management process and establish clear accountability across the new leadership structure.

**3. Country P&L, Financial Stewardship and Sustainability**
- Own the country P&L, annual operating plan, budget performance, cash forecast, cost recovery, working-capital visibility and structural cost base.
- Ensure every material programme, contract, PCV activity and commercial proposition has realistic costing, funding separation, mobilisation assumptions and an identified financial owner.
- Maintain disciplined fixed-cost management. Add capacity only where funded delivery, approved growth or strategic investment justifies the cost.
- Maintain a credible renewal/replacement plan for expiring revenue and actively manage concentration exposure.
- Partner with Finance to ensure auditable separation of restricted humanitarian/institutional funding, PCV co-capital and FASE/commercial activity.
- Ensure the South Africa platform is positioned to compete effectively across corporate, institutional, public and other appropriate funding markets.
- Sponsor priority strategic relationships and major country opportunities.
- Ensure revenue opportunities are supported by credible delivery capability, realistic costing, evidence and mobilisation plans.
- Hold the relevant executives accountable for pipeline, propositions, conversion, delivery and renewal performance.

**4. Delivery, Impact and Operational Continuity**
- Deliver all contracted commitments safely, compliantly, on time and to agreed quality and outcome standards.
- Maintain fit-for-purpose country controls for procurement, logistics, fleet, warehousing, safeguarding, security, partner management, HR, legal compliance and business continuity.
- Own mobilisation readiness for new awards and contracts, including people, partners, supply chain, systems, cash and risk controls.
- Intervene early when programme, partner, cash, security, leadership or compliance issues threaten performance; implement recovery plans and escalate material exposure.
- Use country evidence to demonstrate outcomes, unit costs, operational reliability and value for money - not only activity completion.
- Maintain appropriate controls for procurement, supply chain, safeguarding, security, duty of care, partner management and business continuity.
- Intervene early where delivery or operational risks threaten performance or reputation.

**5. Revenue Growth, Capture and Market Positioning**
- Own the country revenue target and country account plan in partnership with Global Revenue / Business Development.
- Maintain a 36-month view of priority opportunities, renewals, replacements and strategic accounts; ensure accurate country pipeline inputs and disciplined Salesforce use.
- Personally cultivate senior relationships with government, donors, corporates, DFIs, investors, primes, foundations, faith networks and strategic partners relevant to the country model.
- Participate actively in capture before proposal release: buyer intelligence, problem definition, partner selection, solution shaping, evidence, operational feasibility and win strategy.
- Convert local assets, government access, community legitimacy, technical capability and past performance into differentiated, market-facing implementation propositions.
- Do not pursue revenue that creates capability overreach, unpriced risk, unfunded infrastructure or unsupported past-performance claims.

**6. Government, Partnerships and Market Access**
- Serve as a senior representative of ForAfrika South Africa with government, corporates, institutional partners, investors, communities and strategic stakeholders.
- Build a deliberate country relationship portfolio across donors, embassies, corporates, DFIs, investors, industry platforms, UN agencies, civil society, universities, faith institutions and local organisations.
- Use partner-led delivery where it strengthens localisation, market access, technical capability or entry discipline; ensure clear roles, due diligence, safeguarding, commercial terms and accountability.
- Position the country office for strategic industries and transaction-linked opportunities where relevant - including mining, energy, logistics, agriculture, health, water, infrastructure and economic corridors - without presenting ForAfrika as the mine operator, engineer, lender or security provider.
- Leverage and strengthen strategic country relationships to support national, regional and multi-country opportunities, enhance organisational positioning, sustainability and delivery, and protect ForAfrika’s reputation, and mission

**7. People, Organisation and Culture**
- Build a high performing country leadership team around the approved operating model and funded work; eliminate duplicated roles and unsupported structural cost.
- Ensure right people / right seats, clear accountabilities, measurable scorecards, succession coverage and timely performance action.
- Develop national leadership and technical capability wherever feasible, consistent with ForAfrika's African-led operating model and address underperformance decisively and fairly.
- Create an accountable, collaborative culture that can operate across humanitarian, institutional and commercial disciplines without forming internal silos.
- Lead change with clarity and respect while remaining decisive when role, cost or performance changes are necessary.
- Build succession and leadership capability for critical roles.

**8. Risk, Compliance, Safeguarding and Duty of Care**
- Own the country risk register and ensure legal, regulatory, sanctions, anti-corruption, safeguarding, security, financial and partner risks are actively controlled and escalated.
- Maintain country-specific security, access, medical evacuation and business-continuity arrangements proportionate to operating context.
- Ensure proposals, partnerships and commercial commitments are operationally realistic and within ForAfrika's risk appetite before commitments are made.
- Apply heightened controls in high-risk expansion markets, including beneficial-ownership, sanctions, anti-corruption, responsible-sourcing and partner due diligence where relevant.
- Protect organisational reputation by ensuring no revenue target overrides safety, compliance, evidence integrity or mission guardrails.

**9. Evidence, Systems and Decision Quality**
- Treat Evidence & Learning (DMEAL) as management and revenue infrastructure. Use verified data to make decisions and prove results to government, donors, investors and partners.
- Maintain current evidence and past-performance packages for the country's strongest capabilities, including outcomes, references, delivery metrics, unit costs and lessons learned.
- Operate within common enterprise systems and standards for finance, revenue, contracts, evidence, HR, procurement, risk and technology while configuring legitimate local requirements.
- Ensure country operating data and revenue pipeline data reconcile sufficiently for mobilisation, capacity and investment decisions.
- Use AI and digital tools to improve productivity, market intelligence and analysis only within approved information-security, source-verification and human-accountability controls.
- Enterprise Contribution - One ForAfrika
- Contribute talent, assets, evidence, partners and technical capacity to enterprise priorities and other countries when this increases overall ForAfrika value.
- Support regional strategic accounts, cross-border humanitarian responses and multi-country investment opportunities through coordinated planning.
- Adopt enterprise standards and decision gates even where local practice previously differed, unless an approved country exception is justified.
- Share wins, losses, lessons, market intelligence and operating innovations so that the country network compounds learning rather than repeating it.

**First 12-Month Priorities**

- Validate and build upon the foundations established, including the existing diagnostic across contracts, cash, people, systems, assets, revenue mix, pipeline, partners, evidence, risk, humanitarian readiness and PCV / FASE potential.
- Refine and agree the country target operating model and transformation sequence with the SVP Operations; protect all current obligations before structural change.
- Establish the country EOS cadence: leadership accountability chart, annual and quarterly Rocks, weekly scorecard review, issue-solving discipline and decision log.
- Produce a 36-month country revenue and strategic-account plan covering renewals, replacements, institutional opportunities, government, corporate/DFI relationships and suitable PCV / FASE propositions.
- Reset the fixed-cost base and organisation structure against funded work and future strategy; identify critical talent, succession and capability gaps.
- Create or refresh the country's evidence and past-performance package for its highest-value humanitarian, institutional and commercial propositions.
- Establish a prioritised government and external relationship map with named objectives, relationship owners and next actions.
- Validate country risk, security, safeguarding, legal, partner and business-continuity controls; close material readiness gaps.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities.**

**Leadership Standard.**-The next-generation ForAfrika Managing Director must be a country enterprise executive - not solely a technical programme leader. The successful candidate must combine operational depth, financial discipline, external credibility and growth judgement, with the adaptability to lead a humanitarian-heavy, commercially led or mixed country platform.

- Bachelor's degree required in Business, International Development, Public Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Supply Chain, International Relations or another relevant field; Master's degree or equivalent executive experience strongly preferred.
- 12-15+ years of progressively responsible professional experience, including at least five years in a senior country, business-unit or multi-functional leadership role in Africa.
- Demonstrated responsibility for a material operating portfolio with budget / P&L, delivery, people, risk, compliance and external-stakeholder accountability.
- Proven ability to protect current operations while leading organisational change, turnaround, integration, restructuring or operating-model transformation.
- Demonstrated ability to connect operations to growth: diversify revenue, build senior relationships, shape opportunities, develop partnerships and convert organisational capability into funded programmes, contracts or transactions.
- Strong understanding of institutional and humanitarian funding and delivery. Experience with UN agencies, bilateral donors, multilateral institutions or government-funded programmes is highly valuable.
- Commercial and financial literacy sufficient to understand customers, contracts, pricing, cost recovery, unit economics, working capital, investment readiness and the difference between grant-funded, PCV and commercial risk.
- Experience engaging corporates, investors, DFIs, infrastructure sponsors, prime contractors, philanthropy or strategic industries strongly preferred, particularly in commercially led or corridor markets.
- Strong government-relations capability and the judgement to operate credibly across national ministries, local authorities, donors, communities and private-sector leaders.
- Deep experience in operational risk, safeguarding, security, duty of care, procurement, supply chain, partner management and legal/compliance oversight, especially in complex or fragile contexts where relevant.
- Track record of using evidence, data, digital systems and performance dashboards to improve decisions, demonstrate outcomes and strengthen external credibility.
- Established professional networks in the country and/or region across government, donors, civil society, business, finance, academia or implementing partners, with the credibility to open and sustain senior relationships.
- Exceptional judgement, communication, negotiation and influencing skills; able to move from strategy and external representation to detailed operating decisions when required.
- Demonstrated ability to build high-accountability teams, coach senior leaders, confront underperformance and develop national succession capacity.
- Fluency in English required for enterprise engagement; proficiency in relevant national or regional languages is a significant advantage and may be required for specific countries.
- Willingness and ability to travel extensively, including remote, fragile or high-risk operating locations where appropriate.
- Balanced Experience Requirement-ForAfrika does not require every Managing Director to have identical career experience. A candidate may bring deeper humanitarian/institutional expertise or deeper commercial/private-sector expertise depending on the country. However, every MD must demonstrate enough fluency to govern all three operating lanes, use specialist enterprise functions effectively, and make disciplined decisions outside their original professional comfort zone.

**DISCLAIMER**: Please note candidates must have a right to live and work in South Africa

jobs.title: Director Programs Afghanistan
jobs.description:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 2 years. There are very good prospects for an extension. Employment location will be Kabul, Afghanistan (AF).

For more than four decades, Welthungerhilfe has been supporting people in Afghanistan, providing humanitarian aid since the early 1980s and maintaining a permanent presence in the country since 1992. After a shift towards long-term development programming post-2002, the organisation returned to large-scale humanitarian assistance following the international sanctions of August 2021, which brought development funding to a halt. Today, Welthungerhilfe operates in nine provinces across Afghanistan, delivering life-saving interventions that reach up to 600,000 people. With food security under severe strain and widespread acute malnutrition (IPC Phase 3) as well as critical pockets of IPC Phase 4, the need for effective humanitarian programming is urgent and growing.

As Director Programs, you work under the supervision of the Country Director and play a central role in steering Welthungerhilfe’s strategic and operational program direction in Afghanistan. Positioned in the salary scale below the Head of Programs, you support the implementation of the multi-annual country strategy to ensure maximum impact in line with Welthungerhilfe’s global strategy, relevant concept papers, and quality standards. In agreement with the Country Director, you represent Welthungerhilfe in the country and contribute to the development and implementation of programs and projects, continually strengthening the overall intervention concept. You oversee the implementation of the full project portfolio, guide project managers in applying Welthungerhilfe’s standard project cycle management, and support them in analyzing implementation challenges and identifying mitigation measures. Working closely with area managers, you assess and address access-related risks to ensure safe and effective project delivery. In addition, three international experts—covering food security & nutrition, agriculture & natural resource management, and grants management—report directly to you, enabling you to coordinate technical excellence across all program areas. Within the framework of responsibilities agreed with the Country Director, you also assume specific specialised duties essential to the effectiveness and quality of Welthungerhilfe’s work in Afghanistan.

## Your responsibilities

- Coordinate and monitor the implementation of projects and programmes according to WHH quality standards, including an effective M&E system, and supervision of the use of funds and financial requirements
- Provide leadership, direction, and constructive performance management to Project Managers, Technical Experts, Grants/Donor Coordinator, and MEAL Coordinator, promoting a culture of accountability, collaboration, and mutual trust.
- Contribute to organisational planning, strategic reviews, donor engagement, and resource mobilisation.
- Identify, examine and assess (pre-select) new project ideas on the basis of the country and intervention strategy as well as the concept papers and orientation framework and set standards.
- Coordinate the development of new project proposals and assure the quality donor reporting
- Participate in the recruitment and training of team members
- Operationalize and periodically review WHH Afghanistan’s multi-year country strategy, translating strategic ambitions into annual programme priorities, technical approaches, and measurable results.
- Support the Country Director in ensuring the impact of the country programme and provide regular updates on the status of the programme
- Develop partnerships, identify new partners and advise partner organizations on organizational and conceptual matters, ensuring the quality of projects and programmes and identifying capacity building measures
- Monitor the evolution of possible crises through early warning indicators
- Monitor, and where applicable, update or modify, in consultation with the Country Director, the WHH preparedness and contingency plan
- Represent Welthungerhilfe vis-à-vis other national and international, governmental, and non-governmental bodies as well as relief and development organizations

## Your profile

- A university or college degree in humanitarian/development studies or an equivalent degree related to the position
- At least 5 years of professional experience in a similar position in which two years in fragile context,
- Regional experience working in Afghanistan, the global South, and/or in an insecure environment would be an asset
- Demonstrated experience in resilience or development programming is preferred. Specific expertise in one or more of the following technical areas is considered a strong asset: market/food systems development, economic empowerment, climate resilience, and anticipatory action.
- Experience in developing divers partnerships, including local partners, private sector, technical and research institutes
- Proven leadership and organizational skills, including financial planning and oversight
- Proven reporting skills, with excellent writing capacities for different audiences
- Ability to work under time pressure and high workload with high cultural sensibility
- You recognize the growing value of data within an organization and inspire teams to make decisions grounded in analysis and evidence
- Ability to work in an insecure environment and committed to adhere to strict security procedures
- Excellent spoken and written English

## What we offer
