jobs.title: Assistant du projet Transport Humanitaire International (H/F)
jobs.description:
**Date de début de contrat :** Janvier 2027

**Type de contrat** : Contrat à durée déterminée jusqu’au 30/04/2028

**Localisation** : Montreuil (93) / France (télétravail possible en France métropolitaine)

**QUI SOMMES-NOUS ET QUE FAISONS-NOUS…**

La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi connue sous l’appellation « hulo », est la première coopérative humanitaire fondée en juin 2021. Dirigée par des organisations humanitaires et intégrant de nouveaux membres régulièrement, hulo a pour objectif d'améliorer l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant la collaboration et la mise en place de projets communs dans ses pays d’intervention. Chez hulo nous sommes convaincus que le partage et la mise en commun de ressources et d’expertises entre organisations contribue à augmenter la performance de la logistique humanitaire et de la chaine d’approvisionnement

Notre action s’appuie sur une approche collaborative et participative, l’intelligence collective et l’animation d’une communauté de pratiques. Toutes nos activités sont structurées autour d’un objectif commun, impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes autonomes et interdépendantes, qui coopèrent de manière horizontale. Le pilotage y est distribué, fondée sur la concertation, la co-responsabilité et l’engagement volontaire.

Dans nos 7 pays d’intervention répartis dans 3 régions nous mettons en place des initiatives mutualisées dans les domaines des achats, des ressources humaines et de l’environnement. En support aux organisations humanitaires nous coordonnons des initiatives de transport international humanitaire mutualisées à destination des crises humanitaires les plus graves. Enfin nous développons constamment des solutions digitales au service de la communauté humanitaire.

Pour en savoir plus, vous pouvez consultez le rapport annuel 2026 en cliquant sur le lien [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

**DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE**

L’assistant.e du projet THI contribue activement à la mise en œuvre des opérations de transport humanitaire international, notamment dans le cadre du pont aérien humanitaire (EUHAB).

Il/elle apporte un appui administratif, opérationnel et logistique à l’équipe projet et participe également à des missions transversales (reporting, communication, gestion de données, plateforme digitale). Il/ elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les chargées de projet.

Il/elle joue un rôle clé dans la coordination des activités et contribue à la performance et à l’amélioration continue des projets.

**MISSIONS PRINCIPALES**

**\#1 : Support aux opérations de transport international EUHAB**

- Contribuer activement à l’organisation des opérations de transport humanitaire mutualisé
- Participer à la collecte et à la consolidation des besoins exprimés par les organisations.
- Assurer le lien opérationnel avec les organisations participantes et les accompagner tout au long des opérations.

**\#2 : Reporting, analyse et gestion des données**

- Saisir et consolider les données opérationnelles
- Contribuer à l’élaboration de rapports interne et externe.
- Produire des supports de visuel de présentation.
- Participer à la conception et à l’analyse des enquêtes de satisfaction.

**\#3 : Appui technique sur la plateforme en ligne dédiée "Transport by hulo"**

- Contribuer au déploiement des nouvelles fonctionnalités de la plateforme en ligne.
- Participer au support utilisateur (gestion des tickets, assistance, diagnostic).

**\#4 : Communication**

- Concevoir et actualiser des outils et contenus de communication
- Appuyer l’organisation de séminaires, webinaires et événements.

**\#5 : Appui au projet Cost Recovery**

- Centraliser et sécuriser l’ensemble des documents contractuels et financiers liés aux vols.
- Répondre aux demandes d’information opérationnelles.
- Préparer les éléments nécessaires au devis et à la facturation.

**VOTRE PROFIL**

**Expérience et formation :**

- Formation niveau Bac+5 en gestion des relations internationales, solidarité internationale, gestion de projet ou domaine équivalent.
- Une première expérience professionnelle (stage, alternance, bénévolat) dans le secteur humanitaire au sein d’un environnement humanitaire ou à forte composante internationale est appréciée.
- Expérience humanitaire terrain appréciée.

**Compétences Techniques et transversales :**

- Maîtrise du Pack Office complet, particulièrement d’Excel et des outils collaboratifs.
- Maîtrise des outils digitaux et gestions des données (Power BI, Canva)
- Rigueur, polyvalence, planification, gestion des priorités et organisation du travail.
- Excellent relationnel interpersonnel.
- Notions en gestion de projet.
- Capacité à rédiger des rapports / Compte rendus professionnels.
- Force de proposition et capacité à prendre des initiatives, proposer des solutions.
- Capacité à travailler de façon autonome et indépendante.
- Capacité à travailler avec des équipes à distance.
- Anglais indispensable, Espagnol est un plus

**HULO VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES :**

Un poste salarié temps plein

- Basé à Montreuil avec possibilité de travailler à distance en France métropolitaine.
- Contrat de travail de droit français à durée déterminée de 16 mois (jusqu’au 30/04/2028).
- Statut cadre au forfait annuel sur base de 1607 heures par an.
- Conditions salariales :
- Salaire brut annuel : 29 620€ sur 13 mois
- 22 jours de RTT par an
- Mutuelle et Prévoyance AXA (prise en charge à 100% par hulo)
- Tickets restaurants : valeur faciale de 8€, pris en charge à 60% par hulo
- Conditions et aptitudes spécifiques : station assise prolongée, expression orale, travail sur écran, contacts téléphoniques.

jobs.title: Logistics Manager - Manila (Filipino Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Duration : **6 months (with a possibility of an extension)**
Start date : **01-Nov-2026**

## **You'll contribute to ending world hunger by ...**

- Ensuring coordination between Logistics and the other departments in the Mission, in order to provide the adequate level of support to Action Against Hunger operations in the Philippines.
- Managing the Logistics department, monitoring its performance in all the processes related to Logistics and Security to ensure they are in line with the Headquarters and the Mission´s Logistics Strategy, policies and guidelines.
- Contributing to the development and implementation of the mission logistics strategy in coordination with the members of Coordination Team
- Engaging and representing Action Against Hunger Philippines in consortium -led logistics strategies and participate in relevant logistics coordination platform

## **Key activities in your role will include**

**Objective 1: Coordinate logistics at the national level**

Internal coordination of the Logistics team in the mission:

- Analyze and define logistics team members' role and responsibilities on regular basis based on the mission and project/program requirement resources between bases
- Manage, monitor and follow-up of logistics, IT and security staff and functional management of base Logistics Officers
- Lead the consolidation and monitoring of the Mission Procurement Plan
- Manage and follow up to the logistics staff when deployed in the field to support emergency response
- Ensure compliance and support to the standardization of logistics procedures and templates, particularly at Manila and field level
- Lead and ensure the implementation of Action Against Hunger´s logistics procedures (KitLog) and strategy across the operations, including application and promotion of the LINK system across the mission
- Ensure procurement forecasting is conducted regularly with programme and support departments
- Monitor compliance and escalate significant risks and deviations to senior management
- Support the mission with partners and service providers as delegated by the senior management

Drafting of Proposals and Reports to donors:

- Lead and contribute technical, logistics and security related inputs to proposals and budgets in coordination with the Head of Departments
- Ensure timely coordination between the Program, finance, HR and communication departments
- Provide logistics information and supporting documentation required for donor reporting

Supervision of the supply chain:

- Lead and ensure implementation and monitoring of Action Against Hunger´s Supply Chain Management Tools
- Monitor and ensure compliance with Action Against Hunger and donors' logistics procedures
- Monitor procurement lead times and identify bottlenecks affecting programme implementation
- Implementation of the anti-fraud policy and its tools within the logistics department
- Facilitate the preparation of tender plans and procurement schedules for major purchases
- Ensure procurement activities are aligned with project implementation timelines

Budgeting:

- Contribute logistics budget forecasts and resource planning for projects and annual budgeting
- Contribute to any budget/proposal to be submitted to donors
- Review and validate the monthly logistics expenditure forecast across the mission in coordination with field offices and Head of Departments

Reporting, analysis and information management:

- Control and analyze the Mission´s Logistics costs on a monthly basis
- Consolidate, monitor and analyze Logistics Department's information submitted by the field offices and departments
- Analyze and optimize equipment use, including forecasting, disposal and replacement of equipment in line with Action Against Hunger and donor policy and guidelines
- Ensure the implementation of Action Against Hunger´s Archiving Policy
- Support audit processes and provide logistics documentation as required
- Ensure that monthly reporting requirements to Headquarters is met by the Mission

Communication Management:

- Implement adequate and relevant communication systems
- Analyze new requirements and the cost/efficiency of existing systems
- Lead and implement Action Against Hunger´s IT policy in the Mission, including troubleshooting and addressing IT related concerns in the mission in coordination and consultation with HQ

Equipment/asset management:

- Create and implement an equipment policy for the Mission
- Manage equipment according to Action Against Hunger and donors’ guidelines
- Ensure the correct and documented transfer of equipment on the completion of projects
- Ensure adequacy and efficient management of equipment in the Mission
- Lead ensuring accommodation/office/guest house contracts are drafted, reviewed, signed and renewed based on the needs in coordination with the line manager and finance department

Fleet Management:

- Ensure an efficient fleet planning and management in the Mission
- Create and disseminate a vehicle use policy and monitor safety compliance
- Monitor the maintenance and control of vehicles in accordance with Action Against Hunger´s procedures, including renewal of Framework Agreement

**Objective 2: Contribute to the definition of the mission strategy**

- Contribute operational logistics analysis and recommendations to support the development of the Mission's strategy
- Lead and support the implementation and dissemination of the Mission's Logistics Strategy
- Lead, promote and contribute to the implementation of the carbon footprint reduction plan over the mission and ensure collection of data to measure our contribution to Co2 emissions and implementation of environmental policies
- Lead the review, identify operational improvement opportunities on regular basis and propose corrective actions to the management

**Objective 3: Line-management of the Logistics team in Manila, and technical management of the Base Logisticians in the Bases**

- Ensure the cohesion and good communication within the department
- Lead, develop and regularly monitor individual logistics staff objectives and action plans
- Contribute to the implementation of Mission Training Plan, and monitor its implementation within the logistics department
- Provide technical support to field logistics team through weekly meeting and regular field visits
- Evaluate the performance of every team member, and contribute to the development their relevant skills

**Objective 4: Support humanitarian activities of Action Against Hunger**

- Lead and ensure systems and process are in place for emergency response in the Philippines
- Build logistics staff capacity and maintain emergency response deployment ready at any time
- Be available to be deployed in the field for new emergencies as requested by the line manager
- Lead the development, monitoring and periodic renewal of Framework Agreements for frequently purchased goods and services
- Ensure Framework Agreements are strategically established to reduce procurement lead times and support emergency response capacity
- Monitor Framework Agreement utilization and supplier performance
- Monitor supplier performance against agreed service levels and contractual obligations
- Conduct periodic market assessments to identify qualified suppliers and procurement risks
- Support the development of sourcing strategies for key categories of expenditure
- Assess supplier capacity, financial stability and operational risks
- Ensure adequate supplier diversification to mitigate operational and emergency response risks

**Objective 5: Operational support to the Mission´s security management**

- Lead and analyze the safety and security context in operational areas in coordination with the assigned Security Officer, Heads of Base and Country Director
- Advise the Country Director on matters related to safety and security management
- Contribute to monitor the compliance of all staff with the Mission´s security regulations
- Lead and ensure local standard operation procedures are developed and updated according to the timeline established at the mission and HQ level in coordination with the assigned Security Officer, Head of Base and Country Director
- Ensure physical status and availability of contingency measures and equipment (e.g. hibernation boxes, back-up vehicles), as needed
- Coordinate and ensure regular updating of Business Continuity Plans of the mission, including bases in coordination with line manager and head of departments
- Support Risk Assessment and Management in the mission

## **Do you meet the profile required criteria?**

- University Degree
- Experience of logistics management with an INGO in the Philippines
- Knowledge of donor guidelines and procedures
- Ability to work strategically
- Understanding of safety and security context in the Philippines
- Good analytical skills
- At least 3 years previous hand on logistic management experience in emergency response and development programs with a NGO in the Philippines
- At least 3 years of experience in safety and security management
- Experience working with and supporting people remotely
- Experience overseeing IT services, communications systems and IT support functions is desirable
- English is a must
- MS Office very strong command
- Advanced level of Excel
- Valuable prior experience in issues related to the promotion of gender equality or personal commitment to gender equality

## **Our remuneration package:**

- Compensation: based on Action Against Hunger grid
- Benefits: health insurance, accident and life insurance, leave entitlement, government-mandated benefits
- Fixed-term Employment

**Action against Hunger is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work such as but not limited to sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and/or financial misconduct; We expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through endorsing our code of conduct and other related policies and only those who share our values and code of conduct will be recruited to work for us.**

jobs.title: Senior Advisor – Government Liaison and EU Coordination (TA Hub)
jobs.company: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.description:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organizations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopens its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 14 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

As part of an EU and BMZ-funded project, the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) Technical Assistance (TA) Hub will support the Syrian government to enhance the capacities of national and subnational authorities and public institutions by strengthening their institutions, systems, and governance through coordinated, transparent, and demand-driven technical assistance by various European Agencies. The project will coordinate with and advice the Syrian Foreign Ministry as well as coordinate with the EU and the EU Delegation. Furthermore, the project foresees a Project Management unit which will steer and manage the demands as well as support the coordination with the other agencies.

**Your tasks**

The Senior Advisor will act as the principal interface between the Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Syrian ministries, the EU Delegation and the TA Hub. The role translates institutional needs into well-scoped technical assistance requests and supports their prioritisation, coordination and allocation among European implementing partners.

- Provide strategic advice to MoFAEx, Syrian government counterparts, the EU Delegation, and international partners on TA cooperation and the effective use of the TA Hub.
- Ensure TA requests by engaging with Syrian governmental counterparts to scope, prioritize, and refine TA requests, conducting pre-assessments of institutional needs, for submission to the EU Delegation.
- Development and implementation of a communication and visibility strategy for the EU TA Hub
- Coordinate donor engagement by mapping ongoing TA initiatives, managing a real-time database, and representing the TA Hub in international coordination fora.
- Monitor, analyze, and report on TA mechanism performance in line with Syrian and EU priorities, in close cooperation with the PMU.
- Representing the TEI TA Hub to national and international stakeholders.
- Leading a small team of advisors of the Project Management Unit.
- Where appropriate and reasonable, performing additional tasks upon request of the management or in order to support successful delivery.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- Master’s degree in political science, international relations, public administration, law, development economics, or a related field
- At least 8 years of relevant experience in international cooperation
- At least 8 years of relevant leadership experience
- At least five years of experience in government advisory, donor coordination and/or EU-funded cooperation, including substantial direct cooperation with ministries or public institutions.
- Proven professional experience in Syria is required, combined with experience in fragile or post-conflict contexts in the Middle East.
- High cultural, context and conflict sensitivity and awareness for the topic of discrimination
- Experience with risk, security and reputation management in high-risk contexts, confidence to work in high-level diplomatic settings and diplomatic tact
- Professional fluency in written and spoken English and Arabic

Desirable qualifications (optional criteria)

- Sound practice in cooperation with EU delegations/EU institutions and application of EU instruments (NDICI/Team Europe, TA instruments)
- Experience in leading/coordinating multi-partner hubs or TA centers
- Knowledge of EU funding and reporting requirement
- Network of relevant international donors and Syrian institutions

jobs.company: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.description:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organizations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopens its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 14 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

The project “Strengthening the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) System in Syria” is due to start on 1. December 2026 for a duration of 3 years. Given the continued high demand for MHPSS services across Syria, the aim of the project is to strengthen the Syrian MHPSS system by

- supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services
- developing practice-oriented training and continuing professional development programs for MHPSS professionals and ensuring these are permanently established in local training institutions
- supporting partner organizations in offering MHPSS services for particularly distressed population groups, including survivors of torture, some of them through non-traditional (e.g. creative) interventions
- working with researchers to scientifically accompany and evaluate the MHPSS-services offered through the project and preparing the findings for professionals, thereby expanding target-group-specific knowledge and promoting the application of effective approaches
- training and advising professionals from the fields of education, peacebuilding, transitional justice and disaster risk management on how to work in an MHPSS-informed manner with people affected by crises and conflicts.

In this position as MHPSS Technical Advisor, you will be responsible for supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services, in close coordination with the Directorate for MHPSS at the Ministry of Health, the Council for Mental Health and Addiction and the institutions represented within it. You will be working on these tasks in close collaboration with two other colleagues in a project team of overall 8 staff.

**Your tasks**

- Supporting governmental entities in strengthening MHPSS-systems and structures, for example by supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and quality standards on MHPSS.
- Providing continuous technical and process-oriented advisory services to governmental actors on strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria
- Facilitating capacity development measures on MHPSS-related topics for governmental actors depending on need and demand (through consultants or self-conducted)
- Preparing and giving technical inputs in the sub-groups of the Council for Mental Health and Addiction
- Preparing, organizing and moderating technical exchanges and coordination meetings between different (governmental) institutions involved in MHPSS
- Supporting different governmental institutions in integrating MHPSS considerations into their policies and standard operating procedures
- Where suitable, bringing in expertise and ideas into the other work streams of the project (mentioned above), which will be mainly covered by your colleagues
- Supporting with team-internal tasks, including monitoring and evaluation, reporting, preparation of team workshops etc.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- A completed post-graduate degree in mental health, clinical or general psychology, psychological counselling, psychiatry or a related field
- At least 6 years of professional experience in MHPSS, preferably in the Middle East, particularly in/ for Syria
- Experience in interacting with government stakeholders, particularly regarding the development of MHPSS strategies and standards
- Experience with strengthening national or sub-national MHPSS-systems and structures
- A high degree of understanding of the Syrian MHPSS system (governmental, civil society, and academic)
- A high degree of understanding of the cross-sectoral nature of MHPSS, its interactions and relevance for other sectors such as peacebuilding, transitional justice, education and disaster management and how to work in an MHPSS-informed way
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- High intercultural competence and diplomatic skills
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria
- Resilience and frustration tolerance
- Business fluency in Arabic and English
- An existing network of MHPSS actors (preferably governmental, civil society, and academic) in Syria is an asset
- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is an asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

jobs.title: Appel à propositions pour la mise en œuvre du contrôle qualité indépendant d’une enquête de couverture de la Supplémentation en Vitamine A soutenue pa
jobs.description:
Guidée par l'héritage remarquable de sa cofondatrice, Helen Keller, Helen Keller Intl s'associe à des communautés qui s'efforcent de surmonter les cycles de pauvreté de longue date. En fournissant les éléments essentiels d'une bonne santé, d'une bonne nutrition et d'une vision claire, nous aidons des millions de personnes à créer un changement durable dans leur propre vie. Travaillant dans plus de 20 pays – à travers l'Afrique, l'Asie, l'Europe et les États-Unis – et avec une communauté mondiale de sympathisants, nous veillons à ce que chaque personne ait la possibilité – comme Helen l'a fait – d'atteindre son véritable potentiel.

Helen Keller Intl soutient la supplémentation en vitamine A de 40 millions d'enfants chaque année dans 14 pays d'Afrique subsaharienne. Lorsqu'elle est administrée deux fois par an à au moins 80% des enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois dans les pays où la mortalité des enfants de moins de cinq ans est élevée et où les taux de carence en vitamine A sont élevés, la supplémentation en vitamine A peut contribuer à réduire la mortalité infantile jusqu'à 24%.

A Madagascar, Helen Keller Intl appuie techniquement et financièrement le Ministère de la Santé Publique pour la prestation de Supplémentation en Vitamine A (SVA) dans 08 régions à savoir Menabe, Ihorombe, Betsiboka, Boeny, Sofia, Melaky, DIANA et SAVA par le biais de l’activité de routine.

Afin d'évaluer le nombre d'enfants touchés par ces distributions en mode routine, Helen Keller Intl mène des enquêtes transversales auprès des ménages en suivant la méthodologie développée par l'OMS pour mesurer la couverture de la SVA.

Conformément aux procédures en vigueur au sein de Helen Keller International et afin de garantir la qualité des données collectées, toute enquête de couverture doit être accompagnée et suivie d’un monitorage indépendant.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d'un cabinet de consultance pour accompagner les équipes de Helen Keller Intl dans le pays afin de mener cette activité de contrôle qualité de l’enquête de couverture prévue en janvier 2027. Elle concernera une strate qui sera composée des huit (08) régions soutenues par Helen Keller International, dont la liste est la suivante : DIANA, SAVA, SOFIA, BOENY, BETSIBOKA, MELAKY, IHOROMBE, MENABE

Le cabinet sera responsable de la préparation de l'activité de monitorage indépendant, y compris le re-dénombrement sur les grappes tirées, l’administration de questionnaire ménages sur les ménages déjà enquêtés par les agents du cabinet responsable de l’enquête de couverture, l’audit audio d’un extrait de fichiers audios capturés par les enquêteurs de couverture, le recrutement et la formation des moniteurs ainsi que la supervision de la collecte de données sur le terrain, l'analyse des données et la production de rapports de monitorage.

- **Location:** Beirut, Lebanon, with regular field visits

- **Languages:** Fluency in English and French is required. Arabic is an asset.

### About Amel

Amel Association International is a Lebanese, non-sectarian, non-governmental organisation established in 1979. Through 40 centres, seven mobile medical units, two mobile education units, and one protection unit, Amel provides accessible services to underserved communities across Beirut and its southern suburbs, Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and South Lebanon.

For more than 45 years, Amel has worked in health, education, food security, protection, child protection, gender-based violence prevention and response, livelihoods, human rights, and rural development.

Working closely with project coordinators, health field coordinators, and Amel’s Health Department, the Health Program Coordinator will oversee health and mental health projects and strengthen the quality of care across primary healthcare centres, mobile units, and homecare teams.

The Coordinator will harmonise processes, tools, and guidelines; oversee emergency preparedness and response; support programme development and fundraising; and contribute to implementing Amel’s health-sector vision and objectives.

- Work with the monitoring and evaluation team to strengthen data collection, information management, performance analysis, and evidence-based programme decisions.
- Support learning exercises, technical reviews, and technical missions.

**Project management and financial oversight**

- Ensure projects are implemented in accordance with donor and partner agreements.

**Partnerships, coordination, and programme development**

jobs.title: Executive Transformation and Strategy Officer
jobs.description:
**Internal Job Title:** Transformation, Strategy and Communications Steward

**External Job Title:** Executive Transformation and Strategy Officer

Heifer International is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with disability.

**About Heifer International**

Heifer International is a global nonprofit dedicated to partnering with smallholder farmers to sustainably address hunger and poverty in their communities while caring for the Earth. Since 1944, we have helped more than 52 million families around the world break the cycle of poverty. We operate in 19 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Americas, including the U.S., working with small-scale farmers to achieve living incomes and ensuring that they have adequate food, housing, and other essential resources to lead decent and dignified lives.

**Our Values**

At Heifer, our work and culture are grounded in our twelve Cornerstones and six Cultural Guiding Principles, which reflect our deep commitment to dignity, fairness, and impact. These values shape how we lead, collaborate, and grow as an organization. We believe in Passing on the Gift, accountability, caring for one another, sustainability, gender and social inclusion, and environmental stewardship. We prioritize full participation, open communication, and continuous learning rooted in self-awareness and human-centered leadership. Together, we foster a culture of belonging and shared purpose that drives meaningful, lasting change in the communities we serve.

**The Organizational Context: A Global Ecosystem in Transformation**

Heifer is transforming toward an agile, adaptive, farmer-centered, locally led, and globally connected network organization. Over the past several years, the transformation journey has focused on redefining our Program Model, exploring and experimenting with an emerging operating logic, evolving our thinking about the Business Model, and grounding our shared values and ways of working in the 12 Cornerstones.

Heifer is now moving from a predominantly design-focused phase toward shared language, experimentation, learning, and activation. The transformation spans multiple interdependent streams, including the Program Model, Operating Model, Business Model, Culture and Cornerstones, governance, experimentation and activation all forming a Regenerative Network Organization (RNO).

As this work becomes increasingly distributed across countries, networks, ecosystems, functions and capabilities, transformation can no longer depend on a small central team to make change happen. Heifer is intentionally building the capability to transform itself: enabling people across the organization to experiment, learn, adapt, make decisions and activate the emerging model in context.

This role is an amazing opportunity to contribute to a locally led, globally connected organization, being a member of a mission-aligned team, and the chance to reshape one of the world’s most respected development organizations. You will join an executive team that has the courage to be vulnerable on their way to building trust. You will receive proper support and onboarding to catch up with the transformation journey and support your journey towards belonging.

**Role Contribution**

The Transformation Steward provides executive stewardship of the next phase of Heifer’s transformation, protecting the integrity and coherence of the transformation while enabling it to evolve through experimentation, learning, and adaptation.

Working closely with the CEO, Transformation Stewardship Committee, the Board of Directors, and distributed transformation capabilities, the Steward holds a whole-system view across Heifer’s emerging Regenerative Network Organization (RNO), organizational design, governance, human and cultural systems, and broader transformation portfolio. The role provides leadership to the Sr. Director, Integration and Adaptation and the Communications Team (Node), helps ensure that all these interconnected dimensions evolve coherently and that the conditions, resources, relationships, and decisions needed for transformation are in place for operationalization.

The Steward does not own or execute all transformation activities. Instead, the role cultivates distributed transformation capability, shared stewardship, participation, and co-creation across Heifer—helping the organization build the capacity to continuously sense, learn, adapt, and transform itself. In this networked way of working, the role will make decisions jointly with the SC and TSC core teams and facilitate the decision-making process with those teams and key stakeholders.

**Job location: Global (Remote/Hybrid Possible), preferably in a country where Heifer has an office. Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Nepal, Ecuador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Mexico, USA.**

**Key Collaborators**

Internal: TSC Core Team, the CEO, Transformation Stewardship Committee (TSC), the Board of Directors, Chief People Officer & People Department, distributed transformation capability leads and circles, Network and Node Leaders, and relevant functional and enabling teams.

External: Local and organizational partners, Board members, transformation consultants and advisors, specialist capability partners, and other organizations engaged in locally led, networked and organizational transformation.

**Core Accountabilities**

**1. Steward Transformation Architecture & Coherence**

Steward the integrity and evolution of Heifer’s transformation architecture and overall transformation portfolio.

Maintain a whole-system view across the Program Model, Operating Model, Business Model, culture, governance, organizational capabilities, and other transformation streams all emerging as an RNO.

Design for interdependencies and surface tensions, gaps, competing signals, and emerging implications that require attention for collective stewardship and decision-making.

**2. Enable RNO Operationalization**

Enable the translation of Heifer’s emerging RNO operating logic into organizational practice.

Ensure coherence across organizational designs and structures, meta-systems, policies and processes, decision roles, governance, and fiduciary responsibilities.

Connect emerging design choices with the capabilities, conditions, and safeguards required for responsible activation and operationalization.

**3. Enable Transformation Governance & Shared Stewardship**

Work closely with the Transformation Stewardship Committee, TSC and Node Leads to enable healthy transformation governance, shared stewardship, and collective decision-making.

Surface enterprise-level choices, tensions, and barriers requiring stewardship while preserving appropriate distributed authority.

Help mobilize the decisions, relationships, resources, and conditions needed for transformation to progress.

Synchronize Heifer’s organizational transformation with the evolution of Board governance so the two journeys inform and reinforce one another while respecting their distinct roles, authority, and responsibilities.

**4. Cultivate Distributed Transformation Capability**

Build the conditions for transformation to be carried across countries, networks, ecosystems, functions, and capability communities rather than concentrated within a central team.

Enable participation, facilitation, co-creation, experimentation, and shared stewardship across the organization ensuring countries receive resources, connections, support, and continuous feedback.

Strengthen Heifer’s internal capacity to continuously transform itself and reduce dependency on individual transformation leaders.

**5. Steward Human & Cultural Transformation**

Ensure culture, mindsets, behaviors, leadership practices, capabilities, and ways of working evolve alongside structural and operating-model changes.

Partner with People Department, Human Potential & Culture, and other capabilities to embed transformation readiness as an ongoing organizational discipline.

Help create the human and relational conditions required for distributed leadership, agency, accountability, and regenerative ways of working.

**6. Integrate Learning, Sensing & Adaptation**

Embed learning, sensing, and adaptation into transformation stewardship so emerging evidence continually informs the evolution of the transformation.

Define meaningful indicators through co-creation of transformation progress and organizational health and assess whether Heifer is increasingly becoming locally led and globally connected, farmer-centered, agile and adaptive, regenerative and networked.

Use evidence and learning to challenge assumptions, inform adaptation, and identify where additional stewardship and/or intervention is needed; share with teams how their learning has influenced decision-making and collectively determine if changes are working in practice.

**7. Build Heifer’s Long-Term Transformation Ecosystem**

Help shape the longer-term ecosystem of capabilities Heifer needs to continuously adapt and transform.

Connect transformation, organizational development and design, culture and human systems, governance, learning, and other enabling capabilities into a coherent organizational capacity.

Build toward a future in which transformation is increasingly embedded in how Heifer operates rather than dependent on a central transformation function.

**Shared Accountability**

Transformation is a shared organizational responsibility, not the accountability of one role or team. The Transformation Steward works collectively with the Transformation Stewardship Committee, CEO and Node Leaders to provide whole-system stewardship while enabling transformation to remain distributed. It means:

Stewardship & Direction: The Transformation Stewardship Committee collectively provides direction, makes enterprise-level transformation decisions and creates conditions for progress.

Distributed Activation: Countries, networks, ecosystems and functions activate, experiment, learn and adapt transformation in their contexts.

Specialist Capabilities: Learning & Experimentation, Integration & Effectiveness, Governance, Human Potential & Culture, and Narrative & Facilitation each contribute distinct capabilities to the transformation system.

Transformation Steward: Holds the whole and connects the system by maintaining a working view across the portfolio, identifying dependencies and trade-offs, and bringing key choices to the appropriate decision-making groups. The role cultivates the conditions for distributed transformation and helps ensure collective stewardship is informed by what is emerging across Heifer.

**Critical Capabilities**

- Experience leading or stewarding major transformation across distributed, international, networked, or federated organizations.
- Experience working in global, multicultural contexts—preferably in international development, philanthropy, networks, or federated systems.

jobs.title: Director, Transformation Integration and Adaptation
jobs.description:
**Internal Job Title:** Transformation Integration and Adaptation Enabler

**External Job Title:** Director, Transformation Integration and Adaptation

Heifer International is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with disability.

**About Heifer International**

Heifer International is a global nonprofit dedicated to partnering with smallholder farmers to sustainably address hunger and poverty in their communities while caring for the Earth. Since 1944, we have helped more than 52 million families around the world break the cycle of poverty. We operate in 19 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Americas, including the U.S., working with small-scale farmers to achieve living incomes and ensuring that they have adequate food, housing, and other essential resources to lead decent and dignified lives.

**Our Values**

At Heifer, our work and culture are grounded in our twelve Cornerstones and six Cultural Guiding Principles, which reflect our deep commitment to dignity, fairness, and impact. These values shape how we lead, collaborate, and grow as an organization. We believe in Passing on the Gift, accountability, caring for one another, sustainability, gender and social inclusion, and environmental stewardship. We prioritize full participation, open communication, and continuous learning rooted in self-awareness and human-centered leadership. Together, we foster a culture of belonging and shared purpose that drives meaningful, lasting change in the communities we serve.

**The Organizational Context: A Global Ecosystem in Transformation**

Heifer is transforming toward an agile, adaptive, farmer-centered, locally led, and globally connected network organization. Over the past several years, the transformation journey has focused on redefining our Program Model, exploring and experimenting with an emerging operating logic, evolving our thinking about the Business Model, and grounding our shared values and ways of working in the 12 Cornerstones.

Heifer is now moving from a predominantly design-focused phase toward shared language, experimentation, learning, and activation. The transformation spans multiple interdependent streams, including the Program Model, Operating Model , Business Model, Culture and Cornerstones, governance, experimentation and activation all emerging as a Regenerative Network Organization (RNO).

As this work becomes increasingly distributed across countries, networks, ecosystems, functions and capabilities, transformation can no longer depend on a small central team to make change happen. Heifer is intentionally building the capability to transform itself: enabling people across the organization to experiment, learn, adapt, make decisions and activate the emerging model in context.

This role is an amazing opportunity to contribute to a locally led, globally connected organization, being a member of a mission-aligned team, and the chance to reshape one of the world’s most respected development organizations. You will join a collaborative team that has the courage to be vulnerable on their way to building trust. You will receive proper support and onboarding to catch up with the transformation journey and support your journey towards belonging.

**Role Contribution**

This role, reporting to the Transformation Steward (Executive Transformation Officer), is broader than project coordination and narrower than executive transformation stewardship. The Director/Sr. Director, Transformation Integration develops the whole-system picture with Country Teams, Catalysts, and those closest to the work, and shares useful insights and support back with them. The role also provides durable integration and transformation adaptation and advancement capability, connecting distributed transformation work without centralizing ownership of it.

This role does not own transformation activities or project-manage them in the traditional sense. It creates the connective mechanisms that allow Heifer’s transformation to work as one system: seeing the whole, connecting interdependencies, sequencing work, sensing progress and organizational load, enabling decisions and integrating transformation activities, and translating learning into adaptation.

The role maintains an integrated, evidence-informed view of Heifer’s transformation and helps the organization move from design to activation without fragmentation, duplication or overload. The Senior Director makes dependencies, progress, risks, organizational capacity and implications visible so that the role and appropriate stewardship bodies and capability owners can co-create solutions.

**Key Collaborators**

- Internal: Transformation Steward, TSC Core Team, Transformation Stewardship Committee, CEO, distributed transformation capability leads and circles, Network and Node Leaders, Learning & Experimentation and Human Potential & Culture Catalysts, and relevant functional and enabling teams.
- External: Local and organizational partners, Board members, transformation consultants and advisors, specialist capability partners, and other organizations engaged in locally led, networked and organizational transformation.

**Core Accountabilities**

**Transformation Integration & Coherence**

- Maintain the integrated transformation architecture and whole-system view across Program Model, Operating Model , Business Model, Culture, governance, experimentation and activation all emerging as an RNO.
- Connect initiatives, capability groups, experiments, decisions, resources and interdependencies so the organization can see how the pieces fit together.
- Surface contradictions, duplications, gaps, competing signals, and unintended consequences across the transformation portfolio.
- Coordinate with the Transformation Steward, TSC, and capability leads to strengthen coherence in terms of shared language, activities, sequencing, understanding, enabling conditions, etc. without becoming the owner of their work.

**Sequencing, Prioritization & Organizational Load**

- Maintain a practical transformation roadmap showing priorities, major decisions, experiments, capability-building work, independencies, communications and activation milestones.
- Assess sequencing and organizational capacity, identifying when work should accelerate, pause, combine, or be re-timed through an evidence-based approach; facilitate decision-making process for transformation activities and provide substantial recommendations.
- Help prevent transformation activity from becoming a collection of simultaneous initiatives that overwhelm teams or compete for attention.
- Connect design choices with the conditions required for responsible activation and coordinate transformation activation activities.

**Sensing, Learning & Adaptation**

- Establish rhythms and mechanisms for sensing progress, readiness, tensions, divergence, and unintended effects across the organization.
- Work with the Learning & Experimentation Catalysts to synthesize evidence and ensure learning feeds back into design, governance and activation.
- Identify patterns across countries, networks, ecosystems and functions and connect them back to transformation design, governance, and activation.
- Ensure learning becomes adaptation and decision-making rather than documentation alone.

\*Note: Clarification of Boundaries around learning loops within the TSC work:

- Learning & Experimentation works with teams and circles to frame experiments, reflect on experience, and share learning that is useful locally and across Heifer.
- The Transformation Integration Enabler connects that learning with other work and evidence across the transformation. Working with those closest to the experience, the Enabler identifies patterns, tensions, and possible enterprise implications and brings choices to the appropriate decision makers.
- Governance capability works with affected teams and leaders to develop and test changes to decision rights, guardrails, and operating mechanisms, within the authority of the appropriate decision bodies.
- Together, these capabilities close the loop: decisions and changes are shared with the teams whose experience informed them, and those teams help assess whether the changes work in practice.

**Transformation Advancement & Evidence**

- Develop a focused set of meaningful indicators that show movement in operating logic, capability, agency, behavior, coherence, and activation.
- Maintain an integrated picture of progress and provide concise synthesis to the Transformation Steward and Committee, and TSC.
- Track key transformation decisions, assumptions, open questions and dependencies so the organization does not repeatedly reopen decisions or quietly treat hypotheses as settled.
- Use evidence to inform organizational readiness, prioritization, resource deployment, experimentation, and adaptation.

**Decision Enablement**

- Help frame enterprise decisions by making the choices, evidence, implications, interdependencies and risks visible to the appropriate stewardship body.
- Distinguish matters requiring enterprise-level stewardship from matters that should remain distributed to capabilities, networks, ecosystems or country nodes.
- Coordinate decision follow-through and ensure implications are visible across the transformation system.

**Distributed Transformation Capability**

- Connect Learning & Experimentation, Human Potential & Culture, Governance & Operating-System Design, Facilitation & Narrative, Communications and other transformation capabilities into a functioning system.
- Create common rhythms, information- flows, and integration practices while preserving distributed ownership.
- Build and strengthen internal capability for integration so that Heifer becomes progressively less dependent on any one individual or central team to hold the transformation together.

**Shared Accountabilities**

- Transformation is carried collectively across Heifer. The Integration Enabler helps distributed transformation capabilities operate as a connected system while preserving ownership with the appropriate teams, networks, nodes, and stewardship bodies.
- Transformation Coherence & Decision Support: Shared with the Transformation Steward and Stewardship Committee to maintain visibility across the transformation, surface interdependencies, and enable informed decisions.
- Learning, Adaptation & Progress: Shared with Learning, Human Potential and Culture capability leads, and initiative leads to connect evidence and learning across the portfolio and translate it into implications for adaptation.
- Distributed Activation & Capability: Shared with Network and Node Leaders, capability leads, and initiative leads to support sequencing, information flow, and coordination while preserving distributed ownership and accountability.

**Critical Capabilities:**

**Core**

- Systems thinking & integration
- Synthesis, sense-making and adaptation
- Transformation integration & sequencing
- Relationship cultivation & connectivity
- Risk intelligence and decision enablement
- Commitment to locally led development

**Behavioral**

- Influence without authority
- Collaborative & distributed leadership
- Curiosity & deep listening
- Comfort with ambiguity
- Cultural agility and sensitivity
- Detail orientation with a whole-system lens

**Technical**

- Enterprise transformation knowledge
- Organizational capability sensing and analysis
- Road mapping, sequencing & organizational readiness
- Evidence & learning synthesis
- Facilitation & decision support
- Transformation communication & information flow

**Candidate Profile**

- Bachelor's degree in Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Business Administration, Management, Social Sciences, International Development, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
- At least ten (10) years of experience in organizational transformation, strategy execution, organizational advancement, adaptability, operating-model work, or comparable enterprise change.
- Exceptional systems-thinking, synthesis and ability to make complex interdependencies understandable.
- Strong executive judgment and influence without relying on positional authority.
- Experience in project management, integrating portfolios of interdependent initiatives, and managing organizational capacity and sequencing.
- Strong facilitation, sensing and adaptive-learning capability; able to listen to what is happening beneath formal reports.
- Ability to translate evidence into clear implications, choices, and action.
- Comfort working across cultures, countries, functions and ambiguous or evolving environments.
- Experience working with senior leaders in a global, multicultural and distributed organizational environments
- Ability and willingness to travel internationally, up to 30%

**Preferred**

- Experience with transforming or working in a networked or regenerative organization; familiarity with living system principles
- Proficiency in other languages is a plus

**What success looks like for this role**

Heifer has a clearer whole-system view of its transformation, fewer competing signals, better sequencing, visible learning loops, stronger decision support, and growing internal capacity to integrate and activate transformation without depending on one person to hold it all.

**How to Apply**

Applications should consist of:

**1. A concise response of no more than two pages in total to the following two questions:**

Tell us about a time when you were responsible for connecting multiple interdependent initiatives, teams, or workstreams during a significant organizational change. How did you make sense of the whole, identify critical interdependencies or competing priorities, and help the organization adapt or make decisions? What did you learn from the experience?

Heifer is moving toward a model in which transformation capability is increasingly distributed across countries, networks, ecosystems, and functions. How would you create enough integration, visibility, and coherence for the organization to move together without centralizing ownership of the transformation? Drawing on your experience, what principles or practices would guide your approach?

**2. An up-to-date resume; and**

**3. Names and contact details of three references** (although references will only be approached at the final stage of the process, and only with your express permission).

**Application deadline:** EOB November 6, Friday

**Position and Compensation Details**

This is a full-time, global role with a flexible base location. However, it will require significant international travel up to 30%, including time spent at Heifer International’s head office in Little Rock, Arkansas, and in the 19 countries where we operate. Compensation for this role will be determined based on the candidate’s location, experience, and qualifications, with a commitment to fair and equitable pay that reflects both local market standards and the value brought to the position. jobs.title: Special Assistant, Executive Office (hybrid, New York City)
jobs.description:
Orbis is an international nonprofit building sustainable eye care systems worldwide and making treatment and prevention accessible to all. We are seeking a Special Assistant, Executive Office.

**JOB SUMMARY**

- The Special Assistant is a key member of the Executive Office, reporting to the Chief of Staff and working closely with the President & CEO and members of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT).
- This is not a traditional Executive Assistant role. It is a fast-paced, high-trust position combining executive support, project coordination, communications, international travel, ELT and Board support, and special projects. It offers an unusual opportunity for an ambitious, early-career professional to learn how a complex global organization is led while taking on increasing responsibility.
- The Special Assistant helps ensure that the CEO's time, information, travel, communications, and engagements are aligned with Orbis's highest priorities. The role also supports the Chief of Staff in ensuring that the ELT operates effectively, decisions translate into action, and important organizational priorities move forward.
- Sitting at the center of a complex global organization, the Special Assistant will have visibility across Orbis's programs, regions, functions, Board, and external partnerships. The individual will move easily between strategic and practical work: coordinating a multi-country CEO program visit; working with colleagues to prepare a briefing for a government meeting; attending an ELT meeting and coordinating follow-up; preparing CEO talking points; supporting a Board engagement; drafting an internal communication or social media post; or helping manage a special project that cuts across the organization.
- We are looking for someone who is **intellectually curious, flexible, highly responsive, calm under pressure, exceptionally organized, and eager to learn**. The successful candidate will anticipate needs rather than wait to be asked, ask good questions, absorb new information quickly, and become increasingly comfortable connecting dots across the organization. They will know when to act independently, when to seek guidance, and when to engage the Chief of Staff or CEO.

**LOCATION, TRAVEL & WORKING STYLE:**

- **Work style:** Flexible/global
- **Work location:** This role is hybrid and requires the Assistant to work for our NYC offices about 30% of the year. Orbis is a global organization. Candidates should be willing and able to **commute or travel quarterly to New York City** and work effectively with colleagues across global time zones.
- **Working hours:** Given the global nature of Orbis and the Executive Office, this is not always a conventional 9-to-5 role. International travel, changing CEO schedules, and engagements across time zones will require flexibility outside traditional working hours.
- **Growth opportunities:** In return, the role provides exceptional exposure to the day-to-day leadership of Orbis International and an opportunity to learn from colleagues, partners, and leaders across a truly global organization.
- **Travel:** Regular domestic and international travel required
- **Compensation:** $90,000-110,000 USD/year for candidates working within the United States

jobs.title: Wash Officer - Venezuela
jobs.description:
Location: Caracas/La Guaira

Duration: Short-term contract

Reporting to: WASH Coordinator

Closing date: 3 November 2026

**Job purpose**

The WASH Officer will serve as the primary technical and operational liaison to ensure the smooth implementation of water, sanitation and hygiene interventions following the June 2026 earthquakes.

Under the supervision of the WASH Coordinator, the WASH Officer will lead the execution of technical assessments, the rehabilitation of community and health infrastructure, and hygiene promotion. They will also ensure effective coordination with local stakeholders and adherence to quality standards and reporting deadlines for programme funders.

**The main responsibilities of this post include:**

**1. Technical implementation and infrastructure**

- Lead the data collection and needs assessments for WASH in the intervention areas to identify gaps in water and sanitation services.
- To technically supervise the construction, rehabilitation or adaptation activities of sanitation structures and community water infrastructure.
- Lead the evaluation of essential equipment and coordinate the implementation of handwashing stations at scale in priority clinics in La Guaira.
- Ensure that all technical interventions comply with Sphere standards and WASH methodologies in emergencies.

**2. Supervision of community activities and promotion of hygiene**

- Carry out follow-up visits and continuous monitoring of the implementation sites to verify the development of activities and ensure that the project objectives are achieved.
- Develop, organise and support training processes, guiding communities and local teams on the use, maintenance and good practices of water and sanitation.
- Support the logistics of community activities, maintaining fluid and assertive communication with community leaders, institutions and operational partners to facilitate access and implementation.
- Proactively identify risks, problems, or delays in the execution of field activities and propose timely corrective actions.

**3. Logistics and operational coordination**

- Support the monitoring of field budgets and the tracking of requests for the acquisition of critical WASH supplies.
- Oversee community distribution and inventory control of water purification tablets and hygiene kits, ensuring that they conform to current budgetary adjustments.
- Collaborate with the logistics team to ensure that transport contracts, warehouse space rentals and material branding are aligned with distribution schedules\*.\*

**4. Monitoring, data and reports**

- Prepare periodic field reports, records, attendance lists, minutes and other qualitative-quantitative verification means related to the activities carried out.
- Consolidate and validate the information collected in the field using mobile information collection tools (e.g., Kobo Collect).
- Ensure the timely delivery of technical draft progress reports to strictly comply with the cut-off dates and reporting deadlines of the various donors.

**5. Protection and safeguarding**

- Ensure that all procedures developed in the field protect and seek dignified treatment towards programme participants and partners.
- To act with the highest level of honesty and integrity in the detection, care or referral of any possible case of mistreatment, abuse or sexual exploitation.
- Promote a protective culture, guaranteeing the privacy and strict confidentiality of the organisation's data, facts and procedures.

**5. Others**

1. Any other function that may be assigned by the WASH Coordinator.

The MENTOR Initiative works in a constantly changing humanitarian environment - reasonable duties that do not fit the above job description but help to further the overall aims and goals of the programme may be requested.

**Role requirements**

- Have the legal right to live and work in Venezuela.
- University degree in environmental health, sanitation, civil or environmental engineering, public health or related fields (Essential)[\[SB1\]](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_1) .
- Minimum two years of verifiable experience in supervisory roles, monitoring and implementation of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities in Venezuela (Essential).
- Previous experience in community activities and hygiene promotion.
- Practical knowledge of Sphere and WASH standards in emergencies and methodologies such as Community Led-Total Sanitation (Desirable).
- Basic or intermediate proficiency in Office 365 and mobile data collection tools.
- Excellent skills in developing qualitative and quantitative reports, and good communication skills (oral and written).
- Proactive, empathic, strong service orientation and ability to work in a team.
- Experience working with NGOs in emergency contexts (Desirable).

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure the constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Chef d'Equipe (Team Leader) basé à Bria
Chef de Projet basé à Bria
Chef de Projet FH LAM
jobs.description:
Créée en 1922, DanChurchAid (DCA) est une organisation non gouvernementale Danoise dont l’action est basée sur les droits. Installée en RCA depuis 2015, DCA fournit une assistance aux communautés les plus démunies en situation de conflit et de post-conflit au travers de son Programme d’Action Humanitaire «Communautés Plus Sûres » : éducation aux risques des Armes Légères et Petit Calibres (ALPC), des Restes et Explosifs de Guerre (REG) ; Réduction de la Violence Armée (RVA) et consolidation de la paix & Support Psycho social , distribution des biens non alimentaires et ménagers (NFI), Cash conditionnel et inconditionnel (coupons alimentaires, etc), distribution des semences et outils, appui aux organisations de la Société Civile pour leur implication dans la réforme du Secteur de Sécurité (RSS).

DCA recherche **un (01) Chef de Projet** très expérimentés pour participer au développement et la mise en œuvre des activités dans les zones de **Amdafock, Birao, Batangafo, Kabo, Paoua, Obo, Zémio**.

**OBJECTIF DU POSTE :**

DanChurchAid (DCA) lance un appel à candidatures pour un(e) Chef (fe) de Projet Lutte Antimines Humanitaire (LAMH) pour son Bureau Pays en RCA. Le lieu de travail est Bangui avec des déplacements fréquents sur le terrain (localités de Amdafock, Birao, Bria, Batangafo, Kabo, Paoua, Obo, Zemio).

Le rôle principal du/de la Chef (fe) de projet est de :

- Assurer de la gestion du projet dans sa totalité, y compris (mais sans s’y limiter) la coordination, suivi et assurance qualité des activités ;
- Assurer le rapportage interne/externe ainsi que la coordination et renforcement des capacités des acteurs locaux
- Garantir l’engagement externe vis-à-vis d’autres acteurs LAMH et de protection, ainsi que toute autre responsabilité permettant de contribuer aux objectifs envisagés dans les limites de la portée, du budget et de l'échéancier définis dans le cadre du projet.

Le/la Chef.fe de projet devra avoir d'excellentes compétences opérationnelles, en communication, en leadership et en résolution de problèmes, ainsi qu'une expérience des méthodologies et des outils de gestion de projet. Le(la) Candidat(e) idéal(e) aura également des compétences préalables et des connaissances de base dans le domaine de la lutte antimines humanitaire (éducation aux risques d’engins explosifs, enquêtes non techniques, assistance aux victimes). En plus, le/la Chef.fe de projet doit être capable de bien travailler sous pression et d’être capable de gérer plusieurs tâches simultanément.

**RÔLES & RESPONSABILITÉS**

**Gestion de projet et planification :**

- Assurer la planification globale des activités du projet et veiller au respect des délais et de la qualité dans la mise en œuvre,
- Organiser avec l’équipe MEAL les activités d’évaluation du projet (Baseline, enquête de satisfaction, Endline) et de mise à jour des outils de pilotage du projet,
- Coordonner et suivre l’implémentation des activités (lancement, ciblage, renforcement des capacités etc.) en lien avec d’autres collègues de DCA, tout en assurant la qualité technique des activités de mise en œuvre,
- Faire le suivi de la mise en œuvre des planifications conformément aux planning établis par le biais de rencontres périodiques avec les partenaires et/ou autres parties prenantes du projet,
- Veiller à l’efficacité des planifications par rapport aux réalisations et analyser les facteurs de blocage dans la mise en œuvre.

**Gestion du budget :**

- Être responsable de tout aspect lié à la bonne gestion budgétaire, notamment la planification mensuelle, la mise à jour régulière des outils de suivi budgétaire, le tracking des taux de dépense, en lien avec l’équipe support (finance et logistique),
- Participer à l’élaboration et à la mise à jour continue du plan d’achat du projet, et contribuer à sa mise en œuvre (préparation de la documentation requise, participation au processus de sélection des fournisseurs, coordination des activités de distribution, au besoin), conformément aux procédures internes de DCA,
- Veiller au respect des procédures de DCA et bailleurs dans le cadre de la réalisation des activités,

**Communication et coordination :**

- Assurer la liaison avec les parties prenantes (autorités locales, services techniques de l’Etat, etc.), les membres de l'équipe et les bénéficiaires du projet afin de garantir une communication et une coordination efficaces tout au long du projet,
- Documenter les avancées du projet, l’impact des activités et assurer le partage d’informations clés avec les équipes de mise en œuvre et en lien avec l’équipe MEAL de DCA,
- Favoriser le partage d’informations et la coordination entre les partenaires de mise en œuvre, notamment pour assurer le lien entre les activités terrain et les activités de recherche-action participative.

**Gestion de l’information, rapportage et capitalisation :**

- Mettre à jour les documents clés du projet, y compris le plan de travail, les calendriers, les budgets et les rapports, ainsi que contribuer au suivi du cadre logique et des résultats du projet,
- Documenter les leçons apprises et les cas de succès en collaboration avec l’équipe MEAL,
- Assurer la bonne gestion, stockage et partage des documents clés du projet,
- Communiquer régulièrement avec le Responsable des Programmes LAMH de DCA sur les avancées du projet ainsi que les défis rencontrés par les équipes de DCA et des organisations partenaires,
- Collecter et analyser les informations qualitatives et quantitatives par le biais des équipes terrain,
- Rédiger tous les rapports narratifs internes et bailleur en respect strict des échéances prévues et des formats,
- Participer mensuellement aux réunions de suivi budgétaire organisées au niveau de la coordination de DCA,
- Centraliser et compiler les leçons apprises et les recommandations aux différentes étapes clés du projet et à la suite de l’atelier de capitalisation/ clôture,
- Rédiger de façon ad hoc selon les demandes et besoins de la mission des histoires à succès et/ou études de cas pour mettre en avant l’impact et les approches des projets.

**Mise en œuvre et suivi opérationnel :**

- Faciliter l’organisation des sessions de formations thématiques avec les équipes DCA et partenaires,
- Participer aux instances de coordination humanitaires,
- Veiller au respect des règles de sécurité par le personnel sous sa supervision et la coordination avec les ONG nationales partenaires,
- S’assurer de la bonne planification et suivi des activités terrain en collaboration avec le Coordinateur de projet de l’ONG partenaire,
- Veiller à une mise en œuvre conforme aux directives et approches du projet et conformément aux procédures de DCA et du bailleur, ainsi que des procédures spécifiques au domaine de la lutte antimines.

**Contrôle qualité :**

- Être responsable de la qualité de toute activité de mise en œuvre, ainsi que des livrables prévues dans le cadre du projet ; garantir la qualité des produits et activités envisagés dans le cadre du projet,
- S’assurer que les livrables du projet répondent aux normes de qualité requises par le bailleur ainsi que les normes de qualité de DCA,
- S’assurer de la mise en œuvre des opérations conformément aux exigences de DCA en matière de gestion de la qualité des activités LAMH (SOP), en collaboration avec le Responsable des Programmes LAMH de DCA,
- Réaliser des missions de suivi régulières permettant de veiller à la qualité des livrables du projet, et accompagner le processus de renforcement des capacités techniques des partenaires locaux,
- Partager avec les partenaires de mise en œuvre des recommandations issues des missions et assurer leurs suivis afin d’améliorer la qualité des interventions,
- Assurer le respect des principes humanitaires, y compris la redevabilité envers les bénéficiaires et l’efficacité des interventions, tout en veillant à la mise en œuvre des activités selon les bonnes pratiques de la programmation humanitaire et de développement,
- Contribuer à l’élaboration, planification et facilitation des évaluations effectuées sur le terrain par les équipes des projets et l’équipe MEAL DCA,
- Evaluer la pertinence des activités menées, l’efficacité des interventions et leur adéquation au regard de l’évolution du contexte et des besoins des populations,
- S’assurer de l’atteinte des résultats et des indicateurs du projet en lien avec l’équipe MEAL de DCA, tout en contribuant à renseigner les outils de suivi demandés par le bailleur,
- S’assurer de l’exigence de durabilité des objectifs du projet, de la pérennité des actions et, le cas échéant, du respect des normes et standards établis,
- Contribuer à l’élaboration, planification et facilitation des évaluations effectuées par le Chargé MEAL,
- Coordonner et contribuer à la production de supports de communication sur le projet.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Pré-requis :**

- Nationalité centrafricaine,
- Une qualification académique pertinente de niveau maitrise en gestion, études de développement, ou tout autre sujet pertinent ou une expérience professionnelle équivalente,
- Au moins 4 ans d'expérience, de préférence au sein d'organisations non gouvernementales dans le domaine de l’action contre les mines (Education aux risques des engins explosifs, assistance aux victimes, enquêtes non-techniques)
- Bonne capacité d'analyse et de recherche,
- Expérience de travail dans un contexte instable et capacité à travailler sous pression,
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint),
- Langues : excellente maîtrise du français à l’écrit et à l’oral nécessaire ; une connaissance de l'anglais est un atout,
- Solides compétences en matière de leadership, de constitution d'équipes et de communication,
- Attitude de résolution de problèmes, approche organisée et structurée et capacité à planifier, coordonner et diriger des processus incluant de multiples parties prenantes et intérêts,
- Engagement, flexibilité, orientation vers les résultats et fortes compétences interpersonnelles, y compris la capacité à gérer une journée de travail chargée avec des délais contradictoires dans un environnement multiculturel.

**Le poste est réservé uniquement aux candidats de la nationalité centrafricaine.**
