jobs.title: Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator !**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

We are looking for a Climate, Environment & Health (CEH) Coordinator to join MSF OCG.

Reporting to the Deputy General Director, the CEH Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating OCG’s strategic approach to reducing the environmental impact of its activities, while strengthening the integration of the health and humanitarian consequences of climate change into operational planning.The position works closely with the Logistics, Medical, Communication and Operations departments, supporting field missions and contributing to more relevant, responsible and effective humanitarian operations.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

- Develop and implement OCG’s strategy to address climate change and environmental issues across its activities.
- Support the integration of climate risks and evolving patterns of climate-sensitive diseases into operational planning to strengthen the relevance of operational responses.
- Promote the reduction of environmental impacts across OCG’s activities to enhance the environmental responsibility of MSF operations.
- Coordinate cross-functional initiatives on climate and environmental issues to ensure alignment and consistency across OCG.
- Develop frameworks, guidelines, and tools to support teams in effectively addressing climate risks and environmental impacts.
- Monitor progress towards climate and environmental objectives to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including overseeing the organisation’s annual carbon accounting process.
- Represent OCG in intersectional and external meetings on climate, environment, and health.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Essential: Advanced university degree in environmental health, climate change, sustainability, environmental engineering, or a related field.
- Desired: Certification in carbon accounting.

*Experience*

- Essential: Experience in a similar role or in leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders without direct hierarchical authority.
- Field experience with MSF or another humanitarian organization is an asset.

*Languages*

- English and French are mandatory.
- Additional languages are an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Carbon accounting.
- Environmental sustainability and climate change.
- Health and humanitarian impacts of climate change.
- Strategic planning and change management.
- Data analytics, monitoring, reporting, and performance tracking.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Strategic thinking.
- Influencing and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Coordination and facilitation skills.
- Communication and presentation skills.
- Project and change management skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment to diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviours and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Geneva
- Ideal start date: 1st of December 2026
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 119’964.- to CHF 137’640.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Information Technology Analyst - AI and Emerging Technologies, IPSA-9, New York, USA, UNCDF [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

The Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit (DTI) leads UNCDF's enterprise-wide digital transformation, including the integration of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies into UNCDF's investment, programmatic, and operational workflows, while also ensuring compliance with UN AI policy and guidelines. Under UNCDF's Strategic Framework 2026–2029, DTI is responsible for operationalizing a portfolio of AI agents and emerging-technology pilots that strengthen the quality of catalytic capital deployment, accelerate programme delivery, and expand financial inclusion in Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and fragile settings.

The Information Technology Analyst - AI and Emerging Technologies will work on the implementation and scaling of the AI portfolio, building on the foundational AI actions and the first deployed AI system (Strategic Alignment Intelligence, or SAI). The position is central to helping to translate UNCDF's strategic AI commitments into a mature, governed, and institutionally embedded ecosystem of digital solutions serving UNCDF's catalytic mandate, while aligning with UN and UNDP AI frameworks.

Duties and Responsibilities

The AI and Emerging Technologies Integration Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit, UNCDF. The incumbent will collaborate closely with the Executive Secretary, Regional Team Leads (RTLs) and the Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Head of Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit, the Information Technology Analyst : AI and Emerging Technologies will be responsible for the following key result areas:

1. Operation and continuous development of UNCDF's enterprise AI agent portfolio

- Operate, maintain and improve the portfolio of AI agents deployed across UNCDF's investment, programmatic and operational workflows, including agents supporting investment pipeline analysis, investment proposal review and stress-testing, programme document drafting, donor reporting, market analysis, internal guidance on roles and workflows, and other operational processes..

- Design, prototype, test and deploy new agents on the enterprise AI platforms in use or under institutional adoption, including Google Gemini Enterprise, Salesforce Agentforce, agent development frameworks such as the Google Agent Development Kit, and additional frontier large language model providers and agentic platforms as they are integrated into UNCDF's technology stack, ensuring compliance with broader UN policy on AI governance and related technology.

- Support in identification and prioritizing of new use cases through structured discovery with teams at Headquarters and in Regional Offices, and translate them into technical designs and delivery roadmaps.

- Extend deployed agents beyond retrieval and analysis toward document generation, forecasting and workflow action, including production of analytical outputs and presentation materials directly from institutional data.

- Conduct iterative validation of agent outputs against historical institutional decisions and documented outcomes, record performance metrics, and refine agent reasoning logic and system instructions accordingly.

- Maintain version-controlled technical documentation and user guidance for each deployed agent, and coordinate onboarding across Headquarters and Regional Offices.

2. Enterprise AI architecture, data integration and institutional knowledge infrastructure

- Develop, test and maintain assigned components of the shared technical layer connecting UNCDF AI agents to institutional and external data, including interoperable connectors (Model Context Protocol servers or equivalent) that can be reused across enterprise AI platforms.

- Develop and maintain retrieval and grounding capabilities over UNCDF document repositories, enabling agents to use relevant institutional documentation, results, evaluations and lessons learned with appropriate source attribution.

- Integrate approved external development-finance, macroeconomic and credit-risk data sources into AI-agent workflows, including sources such as the World Bank, OECD, IMF and commercial risk-data providers.

- Contribute technical analysis to UNCDF’s enterprise AI initiatives, including assessment of platform capabilities, licensing approaches, costs, and user-access requirements, to inform management decisions on the multi-platform architecture.

- Work with UNCDF ICT, enterprise-systems teams and relevant UNDP counterparts to implement interoperability, authentication and security requirements, and identify potential duplication across platforms.

3. Integration of emerging technologies beyond AI

- Contribute to UNCDF’s technical exploration and integration of emerging technologies relevant to development finance, including distributed ledger technologies (e.g., Hyperledger Fabric), digital public infrastructure (DPI), digital identity and eKYC systems, tokenization, and programmable-finance applications.

- Design and implement defined feasibility assessments, technical pilots and proofs of concept demonstrating how emerging technologies may accelerate capital deployment, reduce transaction costs and enhance financial inclusion in LDCs, SIDS and fragile settings.

- Translate, when assigned, defined use cases from UNCDF’s priority financial, programmatic and operational areas into technical requirements, implementation options and draft roadmaps, in line with agreed strategic direction and technical architecture.

- Research selected emerging technologies relevant to development finance—such as CBDCs, blockchain-based financial infrastructure and interoperable payment systems—and prepare concise analysis on possible uses for UNCDF.

4. AI governance, responsible deployment and risk management

- Contribute to the development and implementation of UNCDF’s internal AI governance framework, in alignment with the UN’s policies and governance framework, including model-selection criteria, prompt governance, data-handling protocols, human-in-the-loop requirements and escalation procedures for higher-risk use cases.

- Review proposed AI use cases and deployments against applicable UN-system guidance, including the UN Principles for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence, the Global Digital Compact, and relevant UNDP/UNCDF data-protection and cybersecurity policies.

- Support the preparation and maintenance of responsible-AI monitoring documentation and basic evaluation materials, including benchmark results, limitation disclosures and validation records.

- Identify and document potential risks associated with AI integration, escalate significant issues to the supervisor, and contribute to practical mitigation measures and management briefings.

5. Partnerships, capacity building and knowledge management

- Support the Digital Transformation and Innovation unit in engagement with external AI and emerging-technology providers, including research, meeting coordination and follow-up related to potential partnerships and collaboration with relevant UN-system entities.

- Contribute to development and delivery of practical user-orientation, prompt-engineering and role-specific training sessions and materials to help UNCDF personnel use approved AI tools effectively.

- Prepare and maintain technical and programme documentation, including architecture diagrams, decision logs, reports, and updates to UNCDF’s AI priorities.

- Participate in relevant internal UN-system forums on AI for development finance, and support the preparation of materials presenting UNCDF’s work.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Thematic Area

Definition

Digital

Systems thinking & transformation

Understand that complex problems need a non- reductionistic, holistic approach. Ability to explore challenges from multiple perspectives by zooming in and out, with a focus on relationships and flows rather than individual elements; understand how certain dynamics and conditions are driving and influencing an

issue. Ability to develop a collective understanding by a mapping systems and their dynamics (e.g. flows or resources, information; power relations); is able to handle ambiguity and can help others navigate it. Being able to identify intervention points to leverage change and system transformation by setting out a coherent collection of multiple interventions to probe the system for desirable effects. Ability to engage with industry experts, government representatives, and academics to stay updated on latest trends and to form partnerships. Strong skills in conducting and interpreting research to support thought leadership initiatives, including white papers, policy briefs, or case studies. Understanding of global trends and cultural nuances, as they relate to the field of AI. Familiarity with international laws and standards regarding technology, particularly in a multistakeholder environment like the UN.

Business Direction & Strategy

Ability to design workshops that considers and addresses multiple interests, agendas, worldviews; set out clear objectives and engaging activities; select appropriate tools, materials, resources that are needed to enable or support the activities. Ability to swiftly build rapport with participants and create a safe space (on- and offline) where they feel comfortable to share their views, concerns, experiences and reflections; supporting this with a range of tools to stimulate active participation. Ability to facilitate inclusive conversations, ability to work with a diverse set of people with

different backgrounds, seniority and expert levels, using different approaches tailored to fit the people in the room, drawing out the perspectives and ideas of each individual and making decisions through deliberation and discussion across a group. Ability to pace a session, adjust to the abilities and energy levels of attendees and the nature or purpose of an exercise. Being flexible and able to improvise; adapting and changing approaches in response to the needs, while staying true to the intent and objectives of the session.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Economics, Finance, Development Studies, Public Policy, Sustainable Development, International Development, or a related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

Required:

- Minimum of two (2) years (with master's degree) or four (4) years (with bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in the design and management of innovation, technology or development programmes, projects or partnerships, including demonstrated hands-on experience designing, developing or deploying AI systems or other emerging technologies in a development, public-sector or multilateral context.

- Demonstrated hands-on experience designing and operating multi-agent AI systems, including using orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, Google ADK, or equivalent platform-native agent builders (e.g., Microsoft Copilot Studio multi-agent configurations).

- Working knowledge of at least two enterprise AI platforms from across the current market (e.g., Google Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce AgentForce, or equivalent frontier-model agentic platforms).

- Proficiency in Python, with demonstrated experience deploying AI-powered applications on modern cloud platforms (e.g., Google Cloud Platform, Vercel, AWS, or equivalent), including familiarity with serverless hosting, authentication integration, and AI SDK / LLM API integration.

- Demonstrated technical knowledge of blockchain / distributed ledger technologies (e.g., Hyperledger Fabric etc).

- Demonstrated ability to translate institutional workflows (e.g., investment review, programme documentation, donor reporting) into structured AI agent designs.

Desired:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

OFFICE/UNIT/PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with Governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

The 2030 Agenda for SDGs and the pledge to leave no one behind reflect the interconnectedness of health and sustainable development, including widening economic and social inequalities, the climate crisis, rapid urbanization, the continuing burden of HIV and other infectious diseases (e.g., malaria, tuberculosis), the growing burden of non-communicable diseases and the emergence of health threats. The scope and scale of delivering health and well-being for all demands innovative partnerships and financing. As affirmed in the Political Declaration of the 2019 High-Level Meeting on Universal Health Coverage (UHC), the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (Global Fund), the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi) and others are critical partners for delivering on the health-related goals of the 2030 Agenda. Stronger Collaboration, Better Health: Global Action Plan for Healthy Lives and Well-being for All outlines how a dozen multilateral health, development and humanitarian agencies, including UNDP, the Global Fund, Gavi and others will collaborate to be more efficient and effective in supporting countries to deliver UHC and achieve the health-related SDG targets.

UNDP’s partnership with the Global Fund makes a vital contribution to UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the SDGs and the pledge to leave no one behind.

As a long-standing partner of the Global Fund, UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance to Global Fund grants in 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of the integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach in supporting countries with significant national capacity constraints to manage large-scale health programmes. By providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including financial management, health information systems, procurement and supply chain management, UNDP is able to deliver results whilst sustainably transitioning to national entities. UNDP’s track record as interim PR over the last 20 years and capacity to deliver in challenging operating environments has been critical for strengthening its positioning as a health implementation support partner.

As a trusted, long-term partner of the Global Fund, UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including financial management, health information systems, procurement and supply chain management. Within the Prosperity & Well-being Hub, the Health Funds and Systems team (HFST) is a dedicated team providing support to UNDP Country Offices implementing health and development programmes.

UNDP has been appointed as the non-governmental Principal Recipient (PR) by the CCM (Country Coordination Mechanism) to implement the Global Fund GC8 Malaria grant, with the main objective of eliminating malaria and strengthening health systems in Guinea-Bissau.

To provide strategic planning, programmatic and operational management and oversight to the Global Fund portfolio to achieve the defined programme goals, targets and effective delivery, a dedicated Health Team has been established within UNDP country office in Bissau.

Within this context, the Finance Analyst leads the finance unit within the health team and is responsible for leading high-quality financial management, grant budgeting, expenditure monitoring, financial reporting, cash management, Sub-Recipient financial oversight, audit preparedness and fiduciary risk control. The role ensures that the finance function provides timely, accurate and strategic support to programme delivery while maintaining robust segregation of duties, compliance with UNDP and Global Fund requirements, sound internal controls and strong fiduciary safeguards across all levels of implementation in Guinea-Bissau.

SCOPE OF WORK

Lead strategic financial management, planning and budget control for the Global Fund Grant managed by UNDP.

- Lead preparation, review and monitoring of annual and quarterly budgets, workplans, cash forecasts and financial plans for UNDP, Sub-Recipients and programme delivery partners.

- Provide strategic financial analysis to programme management, including budget variances, absorption rates, commitments, burn rates, pipeline analysis and funding gaps affecting malaria activities in Guinea-Bissau.

- Ensure that all financial planning and budget revisions are aligned with approved Global Fund budgets, grant conditions, UNDP regulations and programme priorities for malaria prevention, diagnosis, treatment and supply chain support.

- Comply with all UNDP and donor financial reporting requirements, including Progress Updates to the Global Fund.

Ensure robust financial operations, accounting, reporting and cash management.

- Oversee accounting, payment processing, financial records, reconciliations and transaction quality assurance for the Global Fund grant, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timeliness.

- Lead preparation and quality review of financial reports, expenditure statements, supporting schedules and donor reporting inputs required by UNDP management and the Global Fund.

- Monitor cash flow, advances, liquidations, bank balances and payment schedules to ensure timely programme implementation and adequate liquidity for approved malaria activities.

- Ensure proper use of UNDP corporate systems, financial coding, document retention and audit trails for all grant-funded transactions.

Provide finance management and programme finance support for the Global Fund Grant.

- Monitor Quantum project budgets, expenditures, commitments, pre-encumbrances, budget availability, donor fund utilization and financial dashboards to support timely decision-making, accurate reporting and resolution of exceptions affecting the Global Fund grant.

- Coordinate closely with the Country Office finance team on Quantum workflows, payment processing, bank reconciliations, cash management, vendor management, month-end and year-end closure, financial controls, audit trails and compliance with UNDP financial rules and delegation of authority.

- Provide programme finance support to the Global Fund Programme by linking financial analysis with programme delivery, including activity-level budget monitoring, expenditure forecasting, variance analysis, liquidation follow-up, Sub-Recipient financial tracking and alignment of financial information with programmatic results, grant performance indicators and implementation priorities.

Ensure fiduciary risk management, internal controls and Sub-Recipient financial oversight.

- Ensure implementation of fiduciary controls, financial risk assessments, spot checks, financial verifications and follow-up actions for Sub-Recipients involved in Global Fund grant programme delivery.

- Develop and di

Coordinate audits, assurance activities, compliance follow-up and management action plans.

- Coordinate preparation for internal and external audits, Local Fund Agent reviews, assurance visits and financial monitoring missions related to the Global Fund grant.

- Ensure timely follow-up of audit findings, management letters, spot check recommendations and assurance observations, ensuring implementation of corrective actions by UNDP teams and Sub-Recipients.

- Maintain a strong compliance culture by advising programme and operations colleagues on financial rules, donor conditions, eligible expenditures and documentation standards.

Manage the finance team, strengthen partner capacity and support knowledge transfer.

- Supervise, guide and quality assure the work of finance personnel supporting the Global Fund grant, promoting clear roles, effective workload management and adherence to internal control standards.

- Build the capacity of finance staff, programme colleagues and Sub-Recipient teams through coaching, training, practical guidance and dissemination of tools, templates and good practices.

- Engage with UNDP management, programme teams, operations units, national counterparts, Global Fund stakeholders, auditors, suppliers and service providers on finance-related matters requiring coordination and informed decision-making.

The Finance Analyst reports to the Programme Manager of the Health team.

The incumbent leads the Finance Unit and supervises two Finance Associates.

S/he heads the project finance function and works in close collaboration with the Country Office finance team, programme, procurement, supply chain and operations colleagues, national counterparts, Sub-Recipients, Global Fund stakeholders, auditors and relevant service providers. Background

The UNDP Country Office success in its delivery of UNDP programmes is dependent on ensuring an adequate security framework is in place. The Host Government has primary responsibility for the security and protection of personnel employed by United Nations Security Management System organizations, their eligible family members, and property.

The UN House Security Team provides security coverage for UN House personnel, visitors, premises and assets, including 24/7 coverage of designated security posts and daytime coverage during UN House working hours.

Position Purpose

This position serves a dual function, supporting both the UN House/Common Services security arrangements, while also supporting UNDP's broader operational and programmatic objectives.

Under the guidance and supervision of the UNDP Operations Manager, the UNDP- UN House Security Associate supports the activity of the UN House Security Team and provides reliable security services for UN House Agencies. The assignment will include supporting the security arrangement with an outsourced security service, including preparation of technical requirements, technical support to related procurement process and monitoring of contractor performance. Further to support UNDP as required in the implementation of security and safety management in Moldova

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the UN House Management Committee, UNDP Procurement and other relevant functions for the outsourced security services transition and contract implementation. He/she will also work in close coordination with the UNDSS Security Associate for technical security guidance on UN House related matters as well as with UNDP Security Office, through the RSA/SRSS for technical guidance on UNDP related security matters.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Performance monitoring of the security company (Guards team):

- Check, against contractual requirements, that deployed contractor personnel meet the required qualifications, training and documentation requirements and that the contractor has the required staffing/replacement arrangements in place.

- Monitor service delivery against the contract, technical specifications and agreed KPIs, including staffing levels, attendance, post coverage, response to incidents, reporting, replacement arrangements and compliance with UN House security procedures.

- Maintain regular operational communication with the contractor’s designated supervisor/team leader and promptly escalate performance gaps, security incidents or non-compliance with the UNDP Operations Manager, with technical coordination with UNDSS as appropriate.

- Monitor the performance and conduct of Security Guards and ensure compliance with applicable SOPs and security instructions and support follow-up on corrective actions and prepare periodic performance observations/reports as required.

- Support verification that the contractor operates in accordance with applicable Moldovan legislation and contractual obligations, while referring legal or contractual compliance issues to the responsible UNDP functions for determination.

Monitor the Access Control and Control Center:

- Control admission of authorized personnel and movement of United Nations property into and out of the premises.

- Ensure that unauthorized personnel and prohibited items do not gain access to UN House facilities.

- Conduct patrols and physical security checks of the compound, offices, perimeter and parking areas, and report irregularities.

- Use relevant technical screening and access-control equipment and maintain control of the emergency key system and related records.

- Maintain and/or supervise operation of the security control center.

- Prepare, print, issue, activate/deactivate and replace UN House access cards for personnel, as required, and maintain accurate records of cards issued, returned, lost, damaged or cancelled.

- Monitor and control, as applicable, the UN House Emergency Line and Panic Button, video surveillance system, fire safety and suppression system, electronic door locking/access-control system and VHF working channel.

- Act as a support response during emergencies or security incidents and promptly report to the designated supervisors.

- Be familiar with emergency procedures, Security Standard Operating Procedures and contingency plans and support their implementation.

- Know how to use firefighting equipment and support emergency response measures on the premises.

- Respond to emergencies affecting the safety and security of UN House personnel, visitors, assets and facilities in accordance with authorized procedures.

- Provide support in keeping UNDP management informed of security matters affecting UNDP programmes and its personnel.

- Assist in implementing the Country Security Plan, Contingency Plans, and Business Continuity Management.

- Provide support to the UNDP Operations Manager on implementation of relevant security arrangements, including Warden System support, maps, security routes and related documents, as requested.

Background

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Project Assistant will support the implementation of the Green Transition Portfolio Pillar 1 – Decarbonization (hereinafter, “GTP - Pillar 1”), funded by Sweden.

The Portfolio aims to contribute to a just green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina by empowering policymakers, businesses, communities, entrepreneurs, and scientists to devise and implement policies and solutions driving significant decarbonization and CO2 reduction. Key focus areas include transitioning from fossil fuels to clean energy (aiming for the most vulnerable to escape energy poverty), eliminating waste and pollution, combating environmental harms, introducing circular and climate-neutral business models, and protecting natural resources. The portfolio supports effective, fair, and sustainable development through policy dialogue, regulatory improvements, capacity building, and incentives in energy sustainability, waste management, sustainable business models, green chemistry, and environmental protection, driving system-level changes for Bosnia and Herzegovina’s green transition.

The intervention is an integral part of a wider set of reform and investment interventions in Bosnia and Herzegovina guided by the Portfolio “Catalysing the Green Transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina”. This Portfolio is a 5-year programmatic framework of UNDP in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which leverages new development thinking and aims to anchor and catalyse a broader just transformation towards a green and zero-carbon Bosnia and Herzegovina. Interventions elaborated in this Concept Proposal cover a three-year period, while potential continuation of activities will be determined in 2027.

Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager, the Project Assistant will provide support services ensuring high quality, accuracy, and consistency of work. Project Assistant will be responsible for technical and logistical assistance to the Project Manager while implementing activities under the GTP - Pillar 1.

Background

The Philippines' recent transition to upper-middle-income status has increased the importance of aligning economic growth with sustainability, digital transformation, and human rights accountability. As sectors such as mining, renewable energy, agribusiness, tourism, infrastructure, and digital platforms expand, governance challenges related to community grievances, land and resource disputes, labor rights, environmental impacts, and stakeholder participation persist, often disproportionately affecting women and marginalized groups.

To address these challenges, the Philippines initiated work on a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights (NAP-BHR), led by the Presidential Human Rights Committee Secretariat (PHRCS). While several ASEAN countries have already institutionalized their NAPs, the Philippines remains in the development stage. Recent efforts have accelerated under the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan 2024-2028, including the establishment of a multi-agency technical working group to develop a NAP-BHR focused on responsible business conduct, Indigenous Peoples' rights, and ancestral domains.

The FAIR BHR Project seeks to strengthen Business and Human Rights (BHR) governance by promoting more integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approaches that connect sustainability, human rights, accountability, conflict sensitivity, and stakeholder engagement. The project will support the Philippine government in building evidence, raising awareness, strengthening coordination, and fostering inclusive dialogue to inform BHR reforms.

The initiative will also promote stronger collaboration among UN agencies, leveraging complementary expertise and positioning UNDP as a strategic convener. As an initial pilot, the project will generate evidence and lessons to inform longer-term programming and the development of a comprehensive Project Document supporting the institutionalization of BHR in the Philippines.

- Ensure delivery of outputs and contribution to outcomes through an effective implementation plan and close coordination with UNDP management and technical teams and other key stakeholders;

- Work closely with CO programme and finance teams to ensure efficient and transparent use of project resources in line with approved budgets and within UNDP rules and regulations.

Established in 1965, UNDP plays a pivotal role in supporting nations in their efforts to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and advance socio-economic development. With a focus on inclusive and equitable growth, UNDP provides technical expertise, mobilizes financial resources, and delivers policy and other services to support the formulation and implementation of effective development strategies and solutions that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates in over 170 countries and territories, collaborating with local partners, governments, and other stakeholders to build resilient communities and foster sustainable development. UNDP's initiatives span a wide range of areas, including climate change, gender equality, governance, and crisis response, embodying its commitment to creating a better and more sustainable future for people across the globe.

- Support implementation of effective internal controls and proper functioning of a client-oriented financial resources management system.

- Assist in monitoring People Programme financial resources, reconcile donor accounts and prepare forecasts.

- Support in monitoring of financial exception reports for unusual activities, transactions and investigation of anomalies or unusual transactions. Provision of information to management on the results of the investigation when satisfactory answers are not obtained.

- Support in reviewing and approving cost estimates, including update and development of tools for calculation of JPO/SDP/Seconded expert costs and continuous alignment with UNDP finance policies.

- Assist in monitoring and follow up on contributions from donors to the JPO Programme positions.

- Support in controlling and monitoring of Centrally Management Costs arrangements and processes

- Support implementation of JPO Programme financial management model and suggest improvements as applicable.

- Assists in preparation of reports containing analysis of the People Programme financial situation.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

Within the Global Policy Network (GPN), the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for SDGs. As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

Through SFH, UNDP’s Istanbul Center for Private Sector in Development (ICPSD), one of the five Global Thematic Policy Centers of UNDP, acts as an enabler for the private sector and foundations to become more active partners in development, encouraging them through policy advice and technical services on how to contribute towards the achievement of the 2030 Agenda. ICPSD was established in 2011 in partnership with the Government of Turkey. The Center’s work to engage foundations and the private sector focuses on delivering policy advice and technical services in four thematic areas:

- Private sector engagement through South-South cooperation for the SDGs

- Digital transformation and private sector engagement in skills development

- SDG Financing and Private Sector Development

- Resilience and crisis response

Under its “SDG Financing and Private Sector Development” thematic area, the Center offers research, advocacy and multi-stakeholder partnership services to diversify sources of financing for the sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with a focus on attracting private impact capital. Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will support UNDP ICPSD’s SDG Financing and Private Sector Development portfolio Country Offices and in advancing strategic knowledge management objectives, leading research, content development, partnership building and project management for the design and implementation of projects and activities in coordination and collaboration with the COs, RBx and SFH teams. Under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Lead, SDG Finance and Private Sector Development, the Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will provide technical support to the design and implementation of technical assistance products across the portfolio's multi-country pipeline, including credit guarantee mechanisms, and energy-sector investment facilitation, drawing on engineering experience in the energy sector and private sector engagement experience in post-conflict and crisis-affected settings.

Under the guidance of and reporting directly to the SDG Financing and Private Sector Development Portfolio Lead, the Private Sector and Energy Investment Specialist will be responsible for performing and contributing to the following:

Research, Partnership Intelligence and Knowledge Generation:

- Lead qualitative and quantitative background analysis and technical due diligence on energy infrastructure and energy transition investments to inform new project design and partnership development across ICPSD's portfolio.

- Conduct desk research and analytical work on energy markets, tariff structures, and generation/grid technologies to inform the design and operationalization of new private sector engagement initiatives.

- Develop and quality-assure evidence-based briefs, concept notes, strategy papers, partnership proposals, and programme documents on energy and private sector engagement in support of new project pipelines, including partnership agreements/MOUs and monitoring and evaluation frameworks, ensuring readiness for management approval and external engagement.

- Contribute to the implementation of ICPSD's knowledge management activities in the energy and private sector development area, including maintaining an updated repository of technical data, research, and partner intelligence to support ongoing partnership identification and pipeline development.

- Lead qualitative and quantitative background analysis on energy-sector investment opportunities, private sector engagement modalities, and blended finance mechanisms as they relate to the identification of new partnership and co-financing opportunities across ICPSD's portfolio.

- Conduct other research and information collection tasks related to energy and private sector engagement as required by ICPSD.

Programme, Partnership and Event Management:

- Lead end-to-end coordination of ICPSD programme and partnership-related activities on energy and private sector engagement, including identifying and securing venues, speakers, and guests; drafting and distributing outreach and invitations; managing event registration; and performing other related event management tasks.

- Develop and quality-assure the full suite of event documentation including press kits, logistics notes, briefing materials, and background papers on energy investment and private sector engagement, for stakeholder workshops and partner engagements.

- Design and deliver substantive research inputs for events, trainings, and workshops, including speaker briefings and evidence syntheses on energy investment, private sector development, blended finance, and partnership and resource mobilization opportunities.

- Support the content development and organization of national and international conferences, workshops, retreats, partner and donor engagement events, and other events organized by ICPSD in support of new energy and private sector engagement project and partnership development.

Management Coordination, Partnership Development, facilitate knowledge management and Strategic Support:

- Prepare and quality-review notes, presentations, and strategic summaries on energy and private sector engagement for senior management and external advisory functions, exercising independent judgment on framing, accuracy, and positioning.

- Identify and escalate emerging issues, risks, or opportunities relevant to ICPSD's energy and private sector engagement project and partnership pipeline, providing management with timely, evidence-based situational assessments.

- Lead the development of knowledge management products including methodologies, reports, and thematic briefs on energy and private sector engagement, ensuring outputs meet ICPSD quality standards and are fit for external dissemination.

- Participate in events and organizations related to energy and private sector engagement, actively identifying and cultivating new partnership and project development opportunities.

- Participate in project and partner/donor coordination meetings on energy and private sector engagement, as required.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC), part of UNV’s Management Services, supports a growing global portfolio of over 15,000 UN Volunteers (2025), delivering timely and high-quality services across the full volunteer lifecycle. This includes recruitment, pre-assignment processing, contract administration, payroll, separation, and evacuation support for UN Volunteers serving with UN agencies, funds, programmes, and missions. With a presence in 13 locations worldwide, VSC ensures consistent and compliant service delivery across diverse operational contexts.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the duty station, the Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end volunteer lifecycle services within the VSC. The role contributes to timely onboarding, contract administration, and accurate management of benefits & entitlements, and lifecycle events.

The incumbent ensures the integrity, transparency, and accuracy of service delivery in line with the UN Volunteers Conditions of Service (COS), policies, and procedures, while maintaining high-quality outputs and consistency across multiple countries and stakeholders.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS), headquarter units, Regional Offices, Field Units, the UNDP Global Shared Services Centre, and other UN partners to deliver coordinated services. The Operations Associate advises stakeholders on policies and procedures, promotes a collaborative and client-focused approach, and supports the timely implementation of the VSC work plan.

Scope of Work

The Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end UN Volunteer lifecycle services, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant execution of operational processes from onboarding through separation across multiple countries and stakeholders.

3.1 Provision of Volunteer Lifecycle Services

- Administer volunteer contracts and manage lifecycle processes, including benefits, entitlements, claims, and life events in line with the UNV Conditions of Service.

- Handle complex and sensitive cases, including medical and security evacuations, contract amendments, resignations, terminations, and recovery of overpayments, ensuring confidentiality and compliance.

- Administer and certify processing of benefits in full compliance with applicable provisions of the UN COS.

3.2 Data Management and Compliance

- Support timely resolution of operational issues, coordinating with relevant teams and service providers where required.

Background

Afghanistan for more than 50 years on climate change and resilience, gender, governance, health, livelihoods, and rule of law.

Following the power shift in August 2021, the situation for the country remains largely uncertain and fragile, with approximately seventy percent of the population facing multifaceted vulnerabilities affecting their well-being, human security and long-term development while nearly a third of the population are estimated to be acutely food insecure. Over the recent years, international assistance has played a vital role in averting a socioeconomic collapse by providing lifesaving, resilience-building and livelihoods-sustaining assistance to millions of people, hundreds of critical healthcare and educational centres, and tens of thousands of small and medium enterprises, often owned and managed by women. Nevertheless, the humanitarian challenge in Afghanistan is one of the biggest in the world, and basic human needs and priorities remain extremely high. In 2024, 95 percent of households experienced at least one shock of an economic or natural disaster nature such as floods, droughts and others.

To help tackle the pressing challenges for enduring livelihoods and climate resilience, UNDP is designing fit-for-purpose portfolios of programs to create new livelihoods, income opportunities, basic services and to build resilience against climate-induced natural calamities that continue to haunt millions of households in the country.

Afghanistan remains one of the most gender-unequal countries in the world, with women facing systemic challenges hindering their access to education and employment opportunities in the public sector and restricting their participation in public life. UNDP remains committed to women's empowerment through capacity-building initiatives, livelihoods and self-employment/employment support, enhancing gender-responsive decision-making at community level, and supporting local communities to include women, in line with UNSCR 1325 (Women, Peace, and Security).

To support UN joint programming in the provision of basic human needs, a Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan (hereinafter referred as the Fund or STFA) was established on 20 October 2021.

The Fund serves as an inter-agency mechanism to enable donors to channel their resources and coordinate their support to the UN joint programmes in support of the UN Strategic Framework for Afghanistan (UNSFA) which serves as the strategic planning framework for the United Nations in Afghanistan. The Steering Committee is the decision making structure for the Fund while the Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTF Office) acts as the Administrative Agent. The Trust Fund Management Unit (TFMU) is the Fund Secretariat for STFA and is the entity responsible for the operational functioning of the Fund and provides technical and management support to the Steering Committee. The STFA will be directly supervised by the Resident Coordinator while UNDP will provide administrative support to the Secretariat, TFMU.

Under the direct supervision and overall guidance of the Resident Coordinator and matrix reporting of the UNDP Resident Representative, the Trust Fund Manager supports the Trust Fund governance structures to engage with relevant stakeholders (donor community and development partners) through the Trust Fund Steering Committee and Technical Coordination Working Group (TCWG) mechanism. The Trust Fund Manager leads the Project Management, Finance, Communications as well as Monitoring and Evaluation teams housed in the Trust Fund Management Unit. The team composition shall be adjusted over time as and when approved by the Steering Committee. The Trust Fund Manager will report administratively to the UNDP Resident Representative.

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

The Trust Fund Manager performs functions related to (1) management and coordination of the activities financed by the Trust Fund and advice to the Steering Committee on the Fund strategic priorities; (2) advocacy and building strategic partnerships; (3) knowledge management and impact analysis of the activities financed by the Trust Fund; and (4) management and oversight of the TFMU.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Management and coordination of the activities financed by the Trust Fund and advice to the Steering Committee on the Fund strategic priorities

- Provide strategic advice to the STFA Steering Committee on Fund related matters.

- Support the Resident Coordinator, donors and Participating UN Organizations in the review and redesign of the governance arrangements; strategies and coordination arrangements, as needed, ensuring alignment to Agenda 2030 as well as national sectoral and cross-cutting priorities.

- Ensure the development of the Fund’s strategic planning documents.

- Oversee the review and updating of the Fund ToR and the Operations Manual.

- Ensure effective technical and administrative support to the Steering Committee and TCWGs’ processes and follow-up of on decisions.

- Liaise and ensure close coordination with the Fund Administrative Agent (MPTF Office in New York).

- Guide the Participating UN Organizations on the programming processes and requirements as laid out in the TF Operations Manual.

- Implement call for proposals in line with the Fund procedures and Resource Allocation Criteria.

- Ensure quality control of the MPTF funded projects, including coherence, risk management and application of cross-cutting approaches within the Fund.

- Ensure Fund monitoring through the Fund-level Results Management System.

- Ensure the development and implementation of the Fund Risk Management Strategy.

- Ensure and oversee the production of the Fund annual reports and other updates.

2. Advocacy and Building Strategic Partnerships

- Develop and ensure implementation of the Fund's communication strategy and visibility plan.

- Develop and ensure implementation of the Fund's resource mobilization strategy.

- Liaises and coordinates with donor focal points and other TF stakeholders.

- Establishes and maintains strategic partnerships with additional potential donors, and identify and initiates key resource mobilization opportunities.

- Facilitates UN multi-agency engagement in the programming.

- Ensures linkages and consistency between the MPTF and other related initiatives.

- Lead outreach efforts vis-à-vis civil society actors, foundations, and the private sector and facilitate the identification of collaboration arrangements as appropriate.

3. Lead Knowledge management and impact analysis of the activities financed by the Trust Fund

- Analysis and management of Fund's knowledge, including knowledge systematization, establishment of good practices and lessons learned and proposals of recommendations.

- Commission assessments, studies, surveys as instructed by the Steering Committee and the TCWGs.

- Contribute to strategic and policy discussions with the MPTF stakeholders.

- Identification and synthesis of best practices and lessons learnt directly linked to country policy goals.

4. Management and Oversight of the Trust Fund Management Unit / Team

- Oversee the activities of the TFMU and its team.

- Prepare and monitor the Annual Work Plan(s) and budget for the TFMU.

- Prepare job descriptions and vacancy announcements, and identify, hire and supervise staff and consultants.

- Ensure monitoring and control of operational risks of the TFMU.

Other

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Achieve Results:

Think Innovatively:

- Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems. ​

Learn Continuously:

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. UNDP helps countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define the organization’s contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across the portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

In alignment with the UNDP Strategic Plan, the Regional Programme for Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) 2026-2029 outlines UNDP strategic offers and priorities for the next four years in the LAC region and identifies sustainable finance as a key accelerator. At the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4), UNDP also launched the LAC Facility for Financing Resilient Human Development (LAC Facility), which is a multi-stakeholder platform focused on enhancing the region’s capacity to mobilize public and private investments. The LAC Facility will be an essential mechanism to support the roll-out of the Regional Programme 2026-2029 in LAC.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development. SFH work is delivered through three interconnected portfolios: 1) Public Finance for the SDGs; 2) Private Finance for the SDGs; and 3) Global & Country Financing Policy Frameworks.

SFH Public Finance for SDGs (PF4SDGs) portfolio supports governments to strengthen public finance systems for sustainable development. Operating across 99+ countries with a portfolio exceeding $200 million, the portfolio provides integrated technical assistance across four core pillars: 1) Tax/Domestic Resource Mobilization, 2) Public Expenditure Efficiency and Effectiveness, 3) Fiscal Policy Coherence, and 4) Digital Fiscal Governance. The portfolio works with Ministries of Finance, Planning, and line ministries to align fiscal policies, tax systems, debt strategies and public expenditure with national development priorities and the 2030 Agenda. UNDP’s comparative advantage in public finance stems from its unique position at the nexus of fiscal policy and development outcomes. Rather than focusing on isolated technical reforms, UNDP empowers governments to adopt whole-of-government and whole-of-society strategies that link fiscal instruments directly to sustainable development impact. This includes facilitating cross-ministerial policy dialogue, building coalitions for reform, integrating governance, climate, gender, health, and resilience priorities into fiscal frameworks, and supporting countries in translating SDG ambitions into fiscally viable implementation pathways.

The Regional Public Finance for SDGs Specialist will report to the Head of Public Finance for SDGs, SFH (Madrid), with a matrix reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Latin America and the Caribbean, in the Regional Hub for LAC (Panama), while maintaining strong working relationships with the relevant teams/experts from the global SFH, Regional Hub, and Global Policy Network (GPN), as well as the OECD TIWB Secretariat in Paris. The position will be responsible for contributing to the delivery of activities under UNDP’s Public Finance for SDGs initiative in the region, hosted within the Regional Hub for LAC in Panama and the activities will contribute to the implementation of UNDP’s Regional Programme for LAC (2026-2029) and the LAC Facility for Financing Resilient Human Development.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Policy Advisory Support

- Provide strategic and technical support to the Regional Hub and SFH for PF4SDGs implementation in the region, working closely with Country Offices, Regional Hub and SFH teams.

- Support Country Offices to provide policy advice to Ministries of Finance, Planning, and matincluding by connecting and building on existing work on the Integrated National Financing Frameworks (INFFs) and financing strategies for SDGs/NDCs/NBSAPs.

- Work with Regional Hub and global SFH teams to provide technical support to the County Offices for the country-level implementation of PF4SDGs related interventions, drafting/reviewing ToRs and concept notes/FPC related materials, technical reporting, and backstopping.

- Guide research and analysis to identify public finance reforms, drawing on PF4SDGs analytical tools and the fiscal policy coherence process.

- Support the Regional Hub and Country Offices to facilitate dialogue and coalition building with government, donors, civil society, and private sector stakeholders.

- Develop/refine frameworks, methodologies, and tools for PF4SDGs implementation.

- Support the design and implementation of TIWB (Tax Inspectors Without Borders) initiatives in the region, including coordination with COs and relevant partners, and ensuring alignment with PF4SDGs objectives.

Advise and support knowledge, Evidence, and Learning

- Conduct horizon scanning and original research on tax, fiscal policy, public financial management (PFM), debt management and related topics.

- Produce policy papers, case studies, and knowledge products for expert and non-expert audiences based on ongoing CO work and regional level initiatives.

- Contribute to UNDP flagship publications, policy briefs, and working papers

- Document lessons learned, innovations, and impact from PF4SDGs interventions, promoting global uptake.

- Support management of communities of practice and facilitate knowledge exchange at regional level.

- Design and deliver training materials, e-learning modules, and capacity-building resources.

- Support the Regional Hub to facilitate South-South and triangular cooperation for peer learning.

Advise on Advocacy, Engagement, and Partnerships

- Support dissemination of key results and recommendations of PF4SDGs in international conferences, expert meetings, and policy dialogues.

- Prepare background papers, briefing notes, and talking points for senior leadership.

- Provide technical and advisory inputs to the Regional Hub and Country Offices to support and cultivate partnerships with IFIs (World Bank, IMF), UN entities, bilateral donors, technical networks, CSOs, and research institutions.

- Provide technical inputs to resource mobilization efforts and contribute to communications products.

Ensure Programme Management and Coordination

- Contribute to results-based management for PF4SDGs, including indicator tracking, performance monitoring, and outcome documentation.

- Prepare technical inputs for donor reports, internal reviews, and portfolio analyses.

- Support recruitment and roster development for public finance expertise.

- Coordinate and monitor regional budget planning, execution, and reporting for PF4SDGs activities, ensuring effective use of resources and compliance with UNDP financial procedures.

- Work closely with Country Offices to support their budget management for PF4SDGs and related initiatives, providing guidance and oversight as needed.

- Support the operational and logistical aspects of TIWB deployments and activities in the region, including reporting, knowledge sharing, and follow-up with Country Offices and partners.

Perform other duties within incumbent’s functional profile as assigned and deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the office and Organization

Institutional Arrangement

The Regional Public Finance for SDGs Specialist will report to the Head of Public Finance for SDGs, SFH (Madrid), with a matrix reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Latin America and the Caribbean, in the Regional Hub for LAC (Panama), while maintaining strong working relationships with the relevant teams/experts from the global SFH, Regional Hub, and Global Policy Network (GPN), as well as the OECD TIWB Secretariat in Paris.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3- Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3- Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3- Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3- Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Business Management - Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Business Management - Results-based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

- Business Development - Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Partnership management - Multi-stakeholder engagement and funding: Knowledge and ability to forge multi-stakeholder partnerships, and remove any obstacles to resource mobilization and multi-stakeholder funding platforms.

- 2030 Agenda: Partnerships - SDG Finance: Public Finance for the SDGs

- 2030 Agenda: Partnerships - SDG Finance: Taxation and the SDGs

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of five (5) years (with Master's degree) or seven (7) years (with Bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in positions directly linked to public finance, taxation, budgeting or financing for development is required.

- Experience in advising international institutions and/ or governments on public finance management, taxation, budgeting and financing for development in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) is required.

- Experience in policy research in public finance in LAC is required.

- Demonstrated experience in producing written analytical products such as concept notes, outcome reports, or other project/programme documentation is required.

Desired additional skills/ experiences

- Experience working with international organizations, UN agencies, development banks, or similar developmental institutions is an asset.

- Experience supporting regional or multi-country programmes in Latin America and the Caribbean is an asset.

- Experience with the Tax Inspectors Without Borders (TIWB) programme or similar public finance related technical assistance programmes is an asset.

- Experience with SDG financing frameworks or Integrated National Financing Frameworks (INFFs) is an asset

- Experience with interpreting economic data and translating complex analysis into clear, policy-relevant insights is an asset.

- Experience producing concise, high-quality written outputs for technical and non-technical audiences is an asset.

- Experience with the regional context of Latin America and the Caribbean is an asset.

Required Language(s)
