Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

- Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in São Tomé and Príncipe supports the Government in advancing sustainable development pathways that address poverty, inequality, and environmental sustainability. As a Small Island Developing State (SIDS), the country faces structural vulnerabilities linked to its size, remoteness, and exposure to external shocks, particularly climate change and environmental degradation. At the same time, São Tomé and Príncipe is endowed with exceptional natural capital, hosting rich terrestrial and marine biodiversity and functioning as a net carbon sink. The country’s global environmental significance is further reflected in its designation as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and the recognition of its traditional cocoa production system as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS/SIPAM), highlighting the intrinsic link between biodiversity conservation, sustainable livelihoods, and cultural heritage. UNDP works in close partnership with national institutions, civil society, and development partners to strengthen capacities, mobilize resources, and deliver integrated solutions aligned with national priorities and global commitments.

Within this framework, the Climate and Nature portfolio constitutes a core pillar of UNDP’s programme, focusing on supporting the implementation of the country’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), advancing climate resilience, and promoting the sustainable management of natural resources. The portfolio encompasses a growing pipeline of projects addressing climate mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, disaster risk reduction, and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy. Key areas of intervention include strengthening climate governance systems—such as transparency, monitoring and reporting—supporting national adaptation planning and implementation, enhancing resilience to climate-related risks (including flooding and water insecurity), and advancing nature-based solutions and biodiversity finance mechanisms.

UNDP’s interventions are characterized by an integrated, cross-sectoral approach that combines policy advisory, institutional capacity development, and on-the-ground implementation. The portfolio places strong emphasis on stakeholder engagement—working closely with government entities, local communities, private sector actors, and development partners—and ensures that climate and environmental actions are inclusive, gender-responsive, and aligned with broader socio-economic priorities, including the promotion of green and blue economy opportunities. As the portfolio continues to expand in scope and complexity, there is a growing need for strengthened programme management and coordination capacity to ensure effective delivery, monitoring, and reporting across multiple projects and funding streams

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

2. Scope of work

The National Coordinator will report through a matrixed structure to both the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist. The Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the SGP at the country level, including direct supervision of the SGP Programme Associate/Assistant and coordination of the National Steering Committee.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Supervise the SGP Country Programme Associate/ Assistant and provide necessary guidance and coaching;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNOPS rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts, and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations ( CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

Ensure Monitoring and Progress Controls

- Sound SGP programme results and impacts, in alignment with national strategies and priorities and SGP strategy and approaches, that contribute to transformational change in society and economy to conserve the global environment and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, Innovative, technically sound and socially inclusive grant portfolio is developed and implemented. Effective and efficient use of resources to create maximum project/programme impact. Increased trust by clients and donors and increased opportunities for visibility, partnerships and co-financing. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

3. Institutional Arrangement

- The incumbent will be based in the UNDP São Tome e Principe CO office;

- The incumbent will have a matrixed reporting line to the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and to the SGP Regional Programme Specialist, in accordance with SGP Operational Guidelines;

- The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision and development of the SGP Programme Associate

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for the execution of the tasks under this assignment;

- The incumbent will be provided with a workstation (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and access to reliable internet connection

4. Competencies

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Core

Achieve Results LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Business Direction & Strategy Strategic Thinking Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Business Management Results-based Management Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Business Management Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Business Direction & Strategy Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Partnership management Strategic engagement Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives

2030 Agenda: Planet Nature Local Action

• Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental related domains or Natural Resource Management, Engineering, Economy, Public Policy, Law, Environmental Economics, Management, Business Administration or a related field is required. Or

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Antecedentes / Unidad / Proyecto

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

El PNUD trabaja en más de 170 países y territorios, dando asistencia para desarrollar políticas, habilidades de liderazgo y asociación, capacidades institucionales y construcción de resiliencia, fomentando el desarrollo humano sostenible. En Panamá trabaja a nivel nacional, nivel municipal y comarcal. El PNUD hace parte de las Agencias, Fondos y Programas de las Naciones Unidas en Panamá aportando al logro del Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo

Por más de 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

✓ Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

✓ Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

✓ Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos. Dentro del Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental, se brinda asistencia al Gobierno de Panamá en alineamiento con el Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible en Panamá 2026-2030 y el Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2030, los cuales destacan la necesidad de fortalecer el capital humano, reducir las desigualdades y apoyar la innovación y el crecimiento sostenible.

El proyecto “Latidos del Barrio: Cultura que Transforma Comunidades” es una iniciativa impulsada por el Ministerio de Cultura con apoyo del PNUD, orientada a fortalecer la inclusión social, la cohesión comunitaria, la participación ciudadana, el acceso a servicios culturales y formativos, la activación deportiva y la economía creativa en territorios priorizados. El proyecto operará mediante una Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto, con enfoque territorial, gestión basada en resultados, articulación interinstitucional, acompañamiento comunitario y cumplimiento de los procedimientos aplicables del PNUD.

Alcance del trabajo

Bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Coordinador/a de Proyecto, el/la Auxiliar de Proyecto será responsable de las siguientes funciones:

Brindar apoyo administrativo de proyecto

- Asistir en la preparación de informes de avances, asegurando la precisión y consistencia de la información.

- Asistir al Coordinador/a de Proyecto en la gestión diaria de las actividades del proyecto.

- Apoyar en otras tareas administrativas asignadas según las necesidades del proyecto.

- Apoyar en el seguimiento a los procesos de contrataciones y compras relacionados con el proyecto.

Brindar apoyo logístico y operativo

- Proveer apoyo logístico para la ejecución de las actividades del proyecto, tales como reuniones, foros y otros, incluyendo la obtención de cotizaciones, preparación de materiales, coordinación de aspectos logísticos, entre otros.

- Gestionar las solicitudes logísticas, tales como reservas de transporte, preparación de materiales y coordinación de actividades con proveedores.

- Garantizar la gestión electrónica del inventario de los equipos adquiridos por el proyecto, y tramitar el traspaso de los activos del proyecto a la Institución, cumpliendo con la documentación y trámites respectivos para el caso.

Asegurar una eficiente gestión documental

- Proporcionar apoyo administrativo y logístico a la gestión diaria, en particular para la redacción de notas, memos, minutas y mensajes vinculados al proyecto, y cualquier otra tarea administrativa que se le solicite.

- Apoyar en la elaboración de términos de referencia (TDR) para consultores, contratistas y otros servicios del proyecto.

- Organizar las comunicaciones y gestionar los archivos del proyecto.

El titular desempeñará otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

El titular desempeñará otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la Auxiliar de Proyecto, estará bajo la supervisión del/de la Coordinador(a) del Proyecto.

Movilización: Esta posición estará basada en la sede del Ministerio de Cultura, Ciudad de Panamá. En caso de requerirse desplazamientos a los territorios priorizados (Centros Latidos del Barrio), los gastos de movilización, hospedaje y alimentación serán cubiertos por el proyecto conforme a los procedimientos aplicables.

Competencias Básicas

1. Logro de Resultados

2. Piensa de manera innovadora

3. Aprende continuamente

Nivel 1: De mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación

4. Se adapta con agilidad

Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja constructivamente la ambiguedad/incertidumbre, es flexible.

5. Actúa con determinación

Nivel 1: Muestra impulso y motivación, capaz de rendir con calma frente a la adversidad confiado.

6. Compromiso y Asociación

Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión, comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

7. Diversidad e Inclusión

Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, confronta la discriminación

Comunicación

Comunicarse de forma clara, concisa y precisa, tanto de manera escrita como verbal; personalizar los mensajes y seleccionar los métodos de comunicación según la audiencia. Capacidad para aplicar los conceptos existentes a nuevas situaciones y desarrollar nuevos conceptos para generar soluciones viables y nuevos enfoques. Conocimiento de conceptos, modelos conceptuales y teorías relevantes que puedan resultar útiles para abordar situaciones nuevas.

Desarrollo Institucional

Integración dentro de las Naciones Unidas

Capacidad de identificar e integrar la capacidad y los activos del sistema de las Naciones Unidas, y de participar en las labores conjuntas.

Conocimiento del sistema de las Naciones Unidas y capacidad para aplicar dicho conocimiento a situaciones estratégicas o prácticas.

Gestión basada en los resultados

Capacidad para gestionar la puesta en marcha de estrategias, programas y proyectos que se centren en la mejora del rendimiento y los resultados demostrables. Conocimiento y comprensión de las teorías, los conceptos, las metodologías, los instrumentos y las herramientas relevantes.

Competencias Técnicas

Gestión de eventos (incluyendo retiros, capacitaciones y reuniones)

Capacidad para gestionar eventos, lo que incluye tareas como la identificación del lugar donde se celebrarán, el alojamiento, la logística, el suministro de alimentos, el transporte, los desembolsos en efectivo, entre otros.

jobs.title: Grant Implementation Expert
jobs.description:
Terms of Reference (TOR) for functions under a National Personnel Service Agreement

Grant Implementation Expert

1. Position Information

Office/Unit/Project

Türkiye / Climate Change and Environment Portfolio / EU Partnership for Local Climate Action in Türkiye Project

Title

Grant Implementation Expert

Level

NPSA 9

Duty station (City and Country)

Ankara - Türkiye

Type (Regular or Short term)

Short-Term - Retainer

Office- or Home-based

Home-based

Expected starting date

01/11/2026

Expected Duration

Up to 130 days in 12 months

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN's global development network. It is an organization advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build better lives.

The Climate Change and Environment Portfolio’s strategy is focusing on promoting change at scale through investing in national capacity to respond in addition to piloting and prototyping development solutions that have the potential to lead to transformational change. Also, a key element of the strategy is to apply the integrated ecosystem approach, to help establish mechanisms to value ecosystem services with a view to address the market failures to fully reflect the true value of ecosystem services.

The portfolio strategy requires the establishment of programmatic partnerships, as a cross-cutting area, ‘with different ministries, international organizations (inter alia UNEP, EU, UNIDO, WB, EBRD and FAO), universities and CSOs, collaboratively adding value to the ongoing work of these stakeholders. The Climate Change and Environment (CCE) Portfolio focuses on three programmatic areas that complement each other: 1-Natural Resource Management contributing to sustainable environment management and conservation of natural resources in production landscapes, within the general framework of the ecosystems approach; 2- Climate Change and Disaster Resilience (including chemicals and waste) strengthening institutional capacities for analysis and risk management for resilience with a specific emphasis on climate change, and 3- Cooperation with relevant stakeholders to promote energy efficiency and renewable energy.

The overall objective of the EU Partnership for Local Climate Change Action in Türkiye (LCA) Project is to support Türkiye in its efforts to combat climate change through increased implementation capacity at the local level, which will ultimately contribute to sustainable, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development.

The overall outcome of the Project is the improvement of Türkiye’s local climate change mitigation and adaptation capacity, achieved through activities spanning five distinct components (Components A to E).

Component E focuses on providing Technical Assistance to the EU–Türkiye Climate Change Grant Programme (EU-TR CCGP). The Grant Programme is implemented directly by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change (MoEUCC), while UNDP provides technical assistance in support of its implementation.

Projects under the the Climate Change Grant Programme address at least one of these priority areas:

- In line with the priorities of the existing national adaptation and mitigation action plans between 2024-2030,

- Promoting resilient and low-carbon cities and sectors,

- Implementing adaptation and/or mitigation actions in line with existing local or national climate strategies.

As an additional element, all projects include a component (set of activities) on strengthening the communication between stakeholders and “raising awareness within the society”.

The approximate total amount allocated to the grant programme under Grant Component is EUR 15,114,913.23.

Minimum Grant Support* (EUR)

Maximum Grant Support* (EUR)

250,000

750,000

Any grant requested under this call for proposals fall between the following minimum and maximum percentages of total eligible costs of the action:

Minimum percentage: 50 % of the total eligible costs of the action

Maximum percentage: 90 % of the total eligible costs of the action A total of 25 grant projects has been contracted within the framework of the EU – Türkiye Climate Change Grant Programme. The projects are implemented across 15 cities in Türkiye, including Mersin, Çankırı, İzmir, Sinop, Konya, Ankara, Bursa, Çanakkale, Bolu, Malatya, İstanbul, Muğla, Isparta, Kahramanmaraş, and Diyarbakır, as well as in Warka (Poland).

Technical assistance under Component E supports the effective implementation and monitoring of the Grant Programme, including the operation of the Grant Management Information System (MIS), monitoring and evaluation arrangements, monitoring activities, reporting processes, capacity-building and consultative activities, follow-up of grant implementation processes, institutional learning, and the documentation and dissemination of programme results.

In this context, UNDP intends to engage a Grant Implementation Expert on a retainer basis to provide technical, analytical and operational support to the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team in relation to the implementation, monitoring, reporting and other related processes of the EU-TR CCGP, based on needs arising throughout the implementation period.

Beyond the LCA project, the Expert may also be requested to provide contributions to other projects as deemed relevant to his/her expertise.

3. Objective and Scope of Work

UNDP will engage a Grant Implementation - Expert to provide professional, technical, analytical and operational support to the implementation, monitoring, reporting and overall technical assistance provided to the EU–Türkiye Climate Change Grant Programme under Component E of the EU Partnership for Local Climate Action in Türkiye Project.

The Expert will work in support of the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team and will contribute to grant-related processes through review, analysis, preparation and consolidation of documentation and information, monitoring and reporting support, operational follow-up and other related activities. The Expert's functions will not include managerial, supervisory and/or representative functions.

The assignment will be implemented on a retainer basis. The Expert will be engaged on an as-needed basis through individual Service Requests issued by UNDP during the contract period. Each Service Request will define, as applicable, the specific assignment, scope of services, expected output(s), estimated level of effort, timeframe, reporting requirements, place of performance and any travel requirements.

The generic functions described below establish the overall areas within which services may be requested. They are indicative and not exhaustive and do not constitute a predetermined set of assignments or deliverables. Depending on the implementation needs of the Grant Programme, an individual Service Request may cover one or more of these functions.

Within the scope of the assignment, the Grant Implementation Expert may be requested to perform the following generic functions:

- Provide technical, analytical and operational support to the implementation, monitoring, reporting and follow-up of grant projects under the EU-TR CCGP.

- Support the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team in the preparation, review, consolidation and follow-up of grant-related documentation, information and implementation processes.

- Support the review and assessment of narrative, financial, progress, interim and final reports submitted by Grant Beneficiaries, together with relevant supporting documentation, through the MIS and/or other applicable reporting arrangements.

- Prepare and/or contribute to monitoring reports, programme progress reports, review notes, assessment notes, checklists, management summaries, briefing notes, presentations, trackers, analytical documents and other grant-related reporting and management outputs.

- Support the operation and use of the Grant MIS, including the review, recording, follow-up and consolidation of information and documentation submitted or generated during grant implementation.

- Support the operation of the Grant Programme's monitoring and evaluation arrangements, including the collection, review, consolidation and analysis of information relating to implementation progress, outputs, results, indicators, risks and other programme performance information.

- Support the tracking and consolidation of indicators and other quantitative and qualitative information reported by Grant Beneficiaries and contribute to programme-level analysis and reporting.

- Support desk-based and field-based monitoring of grant projects, including review of project documentation, preparation for monitoring visits, participation in site visits and meetings, documentation of findings, and preparation of monitoring reports, notes and follow-up recommendations.

- Support the review and follow-up of notifications, modification and amendment requests, implementation changes and other contractual or implementation-related matters submitted by Grant Beneficiaries, including preparation of technical observations, analyses and recommendations for consideration by the responsible parties.

- Identify gaps, inconsistencies, implementation risks, compliance issues and matters requiring clarification or follow-up in grant-related information and documentation and provide relevant inputs and recommendations to the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team.

- Support quality assurance of reports, documents, information and other materials produced or submitted in connection with Grant Programme implementation.

- Support communication, information exchange and coordination among UNDP, Grant Beneficiaries, the End Recipient, Contracting Authority and other relevant stakeholders concerning grant implementation, reporting, monitoring and related processes.

- Support the organization and delivery of meetings, consultations, trainings, workshops, guidance sessions and other capacity-building or information-exchange activities related to Grant Programme implementation.

- Prepare or contribute to guidance notes, presentations, training materials, templates, checklists and other tools intended to facilitate grant implementation, monitoring, reporting and compliance.

- Support the preparation, revision and application of grant implementation procedures, guidelines, reporting arrangements, monitoring tools, templates and other programme documentation, as required.

- Contribute to project- and programme-level reporting relating to Component E, including preparation and consolidation of inputs for progress reports, monitoring reports, donor reporting and other reporting requirements.

- Support the preparation and consolidation of information concerning Grant Programme achievements, results, challenges, risks and implementation progress for management, reporting and communication purposes.

- Support the identification, analysis and documentation of lessons learned, good practices, implementation experiences and programme achievements and contribute to the preparation of compendia, case studies, lessons learned reports, dissemination materials and other knowledge products.

- Support grant closure processes, including review and consolidation of relevant implementation, monitoring and reporting information and preparation of related documentation and programme-level inputs.

- Support the organization and implementation of Grant Programme events and related activities where technical or grant implementation input is required.

- Undertake other grant implementation support assignments falling within the overall scope and purpose of this ToR, as specified through individual Service Requests issued by UNDP.

The Expert may be requested to revise or further develop outputs prepared under individual Service Requests on the basis of comments provided by UNDP and/or relevant Grant Programme stakeholders.

Final approvals, formal contractual decisions, certifications and other functions vested in UNDP, the Contracting Authority, End Recipient or other authorized parties shall remain with the respective authorized entity and shall not be exercised by the Grant Implementation Expert.

If required by UNDP, the Grant Implementation Expert may be requested to provide additional consultancy services on topics related to her/his consultancies area.

5. Institutional Arrangement

UNDP will provide the Grant Implementation Expert with all relevant background documents and information required for the completion of assignments. UNDP is not required to provide any physical facility for the work of the Expert. However, depending on the availability of physical facilities and operational requirements, such facilities may be provided at the discretion of UNDP and/or in cooperation with MoEUCC. UNDP will facilitate meetings between the Expert and relevant stakeholders, when needed.

All documents, information and data provided to the Grant Implementation Expert are confidential and cannot be used for any other purposes or shared with a third party without prior written approval from UNDP.

The language of outputs will be specified in the relevant Service Request. Depending on the nature of the assignment, outputs may be required in English and/or Turkish.

The Grant Implementation Expert shall be responsible for the accuracy, consistency and reliability of the information and analysis provided under the assignment and for appropriately identifying the sources of information used.

The Grant Implementation Expert shall report to the Grant Manager of the EU Partnership for Local Climate Action in Türkiye Project under the overall supervision of the Project Manager and will work in close collaboration with the Grant Manager, Grant Expert, Project Team and other relevant stakeholders.

The specific technical focal point, expected outputs and reporting arrangements for each assignment may be further specified in the relevant Service Request.

Outputs prepared under a Service Request shall be submitted to UNDP for review and acceptance in accordance with the requirements and timeframe specified in the respective Service Request. Where revisions are requested, the Expert shall address the comments within the timeframe agreed for the respective assignment.

Place of work for the assignment is home-based and Ankara. Grant Implementation Expert will be expected to be present in MoEUCC (Grant Component Contracting Authority and Directorate of Climate Change) or UNDP premises at certain times when necessary. All travel, accommodation and living costs in duty station (home based and Ankara) will be covered by the Grant Implementation Expert. In case travels to other cities specified in the Projects DoA and/or other unforeseen travel out of the duty station is needed, the travel and accommodation costs of these missions will be borne by UNDP. The cost and terms of reimbursement of any travel authorized by UNDP for Expert must be negotiated prior to travel.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks, and opportunities, linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions.

Business Development

Human-centered Design

Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process.

Business Development

Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

Working with Evidence and Data

Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions, and supporting decision-making.

Ability to communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

Business management

Ability to identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks.

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Economics/ Business Administration / Management/ Social Sciences/ Engineering, Environmental Sciences/ Natural Sciences/ Statistics/ Political sciences/ Law or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in providing management advisory services, and/or hands-on experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development projects.

Required skills

- Excellent command of office software, such as word processors, spreadsheets, databases.

- Professional experience with government institutions in Türkiye.

- Specific professional experience in the design, implementation, and/or monitoring and evaluation of grant or similar programmes and/or contracts.

- Hands-on experience in EU grants or similar project implementation and/or its audit /verification.

- Specific professional experience in monitoring and evaluation and/or auditing, risk management and/or implementation of at least three (3) EU grant projects or similar programme financed by International Donors.

- Specific professional experience in preparation of training documents and execution of training covering the life cycle of grant projects such as tendering, implementation, monitoring, and financing.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Professional Certification in audit and/or risk management and /or accounting and financial management such as CIA, CMA, CPA or similar.

- Specific professional experience with UNDP Contracts and/or knowledge of contract management principles and /or audit/verification modalities of UNDP.

- Specific professional experience in EU-financed projects and contracts. Knowledge of general EU PRAG procedures related to Grants.

jobs.title: Health Governance Specialist (Open to Internal & External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the World Health Organization (WHO) in Viet Nam have formed a strategic partnership to support the government in addressing complex and interconnected challenges related to access, quality, and governance of medical products among other areas. The partnership draws on the two Agencies’ complementary strengths - UNDP’s leadership in governance, digital transformation, and system-wide reform, and WHO’s deep expertise in health systems, regulation, and patient safety

Over the course of 2025 and 2026, the two organisations have developed and implemented a Joint Programme on Improving Access to Quality Medical Products in Viet Nam, an initiative that supports the Government of Viet Nam in strengthening its regulatory and procurement systems, ensuring that medicines, vaccines, and medical devices are safe, affordable, and consistently available. The programme focus is on key areas such as institutional governance, regulatory reform, digital innovation, accountability mechanisms, and capacity development. Building on these initial success, the two Agencies have continued to pursue joint fundraising efforts, leading to the mobilization of new resources for the implementation of a five-year initiative aiming to help Viet Nam build the regulatory, digital, care, and financing systems needed for its next phase of inclusive, investment-ready growth. From the Health Governance perspective, the programme focuses on three key areas: access to quality medical products, digital health transformation, older persons and disability-inclusive care.

The Health Governance Specialist plays a pivotal role in driving forward the UNDP-WHO joint agenda and implementing the joint program of work. Under the strategic guidance of the UNDP Deputy Resident Representative but with a dual reporting line to WHO, the role is uniquely positioned to bridge both agencies’ priorities. The contract holder supports joint programme implementation, and strengthens donor and private sector engagement, while also contributing technical inputs to other relevant WHO and UNDP programmes of work. In doing so, the position reinforces coherence, coordination, and shared impact across both agencies – ensuring that support to Viet Nam’s health system is technically robust, institutionally grounded, and strategically aligned with national development goals.

The contract holder will provide high quality strategic and technical leadership for the joint WHO-UNDP programme on improving access to quality medical products, ensuring alignment with national priorities and the shared goals of WHO and UNDP. Through their role, they will assure oversight of planning and design, promote information sharing and communication between the two agencies, and oversee implementation, following a risk-informed results-based management approach. Furthermore, they will engage as necessary in building and fostering partnerships and resource mobilization to foster sustainability and ongoing technical support.

Greater detail on specific functions for each agency is detailed below:

Duties and Responsibilities

This role has a dual reporting structure, via both UNDP and WHO. Administrative management is via UNDP. Technical oversight and management is via both UNDP and WHO.

At UNDP, the contract holder reports to the UNDP Deputy Resident Representative. The contract holder is responsible for the management of all UNDP staff working on the Health Governance Portfolio.

At WHO, the contract holder reports to the WHO Universal Health Coverage & Disease Control Team Coordinator. (matrix reporting)

Perform WHO Responsibilities

The Health Governance Specialist will provide technical expertise to the development and timely implementation of WHO Viet Nam’s health systems strengthening agenda, with a focus on regulatory reform, access to quality medical products, and rational use of medicines. This work will contribute to WHO’s broader efforts to strengthen integrated, people-centered health systems aligned with international standards and national priorities. Responsibilities include:

Lead WHO’s work on access to medical products including the following aspects:

- Support the Development and Implementation of Vaccine and Medicines Regulatory Institutional Development Plans (IDP): Identify strategic priorities within the IDP together with MOH and leverage WHO’s technical experts to support regulatory strengthening as benchmarking follow-up actions;

- Support the Development of Medical Devices Law: Provide technical assistance for the development and review of the Medical Devices Law and related sub-law documents, ensuring consistency with global best practices and WHO recommendations;

- Support the Development of the National Medicines Policy: Provide technical support to the drafting and consultation processes for Viet Nam’s National Medicines Policy, promoting alignment with WHO frameworks and principles of equitable access, quality assurance, and appropriate use;

- Support to Improve Access to Quality Medical Products: Contribute to WHO’s work on improving access to safe, effective, and affordable medical products, with an initial focus on technical inputs to reference pricing, medical product nomenclature, and product categorization;

- Technical Inputs to Other WHO Priorities: Provide technical inputs to other areas of WHO Viet Nam’s work that intersect with health systems governance, clinical governance, digital health innovation, and access to medical products, as needed and in line with evolving country needs and workplans.

Perform UNDP Responsibilities

The Health Governance Specialist will provide strategic leadership for the development, resourcing and implementation of a Health Governance Portfolio. The role will position UNDP’s contribution around its comparative advantages in governance, institutional strengthening, accountability, inclusion, digital transformation and development financing, complementing WHO’s specialized health mandate. Responsibilities include:

- Strategic Advisory and Portfolio Leadership: Define the strategic direction and priorities of UNDP Viet Nam’s Health Governance Portfolio, ensuring alignment with national priorities, the UNDP Country Programme and UNDP’s governance mandate, and advise senior management and government counterparts on emerging health-governance challenges and opportunities;

- Programme Development and Oversight: Lead the design and substantive oversight of health-governance programmes and projects, including results frameworks, implementation arrangements, risk-management measures and sustainability strategies, and ensure the quality of key programme deliverables, reports and policy products;

- Partnerships & Policy Engagement: Provide strategic leadership across UNDP’s work on health-sector governance and integrity, access to quality medical products, responsible digital transformation, healthy ageing, disability-inclusive care and the care economy, ensuring coherence across these areas;

- Promote Resource Mobilization: Identify and develop financing and partnership opportunities for the Health Governance Portfolio and lead the substantive preparation of concept notes, in coordination with relevant teams;

- Portfolio and Team Management: Manage personnel assigned to the Health Governance Portfolio and oversee portfolio-level planning, performance, budgeting, reporting and risk management, while promoting collaboration with other UNDP portfolios affecting public-health outcomes.

Facilitate knowledge management

Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the project and the Organization.

Competencies

Core

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site

Cross-functional & technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Digital

- Portfolio design & management: Ability to identify leverage points in systems and design interventions that address them. The value of the interventions is determined not in isolation, but as part of the overall portfolio and their coherence; Ability to design processes that extract learning on an ongoing basis from existing portfolios, so that learning accrues over time and new options for action are continuously generated; Build a learning ecosystem around a complex development challenge: being able to mobilize a variety of stakeholders and help them learn and work together; Understand key principles of systems and complexity theory.

- Innovation Management: Being able to create the, strategies, conditions, structures and systems to enable innovation at an organizational level; Ability to navigate uncertainty and ambiguity, is able manage projects based principles of adaptation and emergence; Ability to shape demand for innovation services, navigate political constraints and make the case for allocation of resources to innovation, connect the appropriate innovation approaches based on business needs and make the case for innovation to be integrated at the planning level within their context; Having in-depth theoretical and experiential knowledge of innovation processes, methods, capabilities.

2030 Agenda: Peace

- Governance: Anti-Corruption

- Health: Universal Health Coverage

- Health: Health Resilience and Sustainable Systems for Health

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Public Health, Governance, Health Innovation, or a related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in health governance, health-system strengthening, public-sector reform, health policy, regulatory systems or a closely related field is required.

Required skills & experience:

- Demonstrated experience in providing strategic or policy advisory support on health governance, health-system reform or institutional strengthening is required;

- Demonstrated experience in designing, managing or overseeing complex programmes involving government and development partners is required;

- Experience in partnership development, stakeholder coordination and resource mobilization is required;

- Experience in at least one of the following areas is required: governance of medical products, health-sector integrity and accountability, digital health governance, quality of care, or inclusive systems of care.

Desired skills:

- Experience of working in Viet Nam or in a comparable middle-income-country context is an asset;

- Experience of working within the UN system or other international development organizations is an asset;

- Experience in developing successful funding proposals or strategic partnerships is an asset;

- Experience in responsible digital transformation, data governance or regulation of digital health is an asset;

- Experience in managing multidisciplinary teams or cross-agency programmes is an asset;

- Experience and knowledge of health-sector procurement, pharmaceutical regulation or medical-device governance is an asset.

Required Languages:

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Professional Certificates

Project management certification is preferred (PMP, PRINCE2, or other similar).

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Background

UNDP provides integrated programmatic, policy and financing solutions to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this context, UNDP has created a Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) and the Crisis Bureau (CB) are the two anchor Bureaux of the GPN.

In this context, the newly established Governance, Rule of Law, and Peacebuilding (GRP) Hub, a joint endeavour with the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS), provides leadership and advisory services to enhance UNDP’s impact on governance and peacebuilding, ensuring the integration of democratic governance and human rights into crisis response and recovery. The Hub aims to build an integrated portfolio collaboratively between the CB and BPPS and establish partnerships with various stakeholders including the UN System, IFIs, civil society, and the private sector.

Local and regional governments are already responsible of over 65% of the SDG targets, most of them linked to basic service provision from water, sanitation, mobility, climate action, health or education. Cities and territories are playing a big part on the implementation of SDGs, that are becoming a new tool for strategic planning and budgeting in the mid to long-term. Since 2015, local governments and their associations have been increasingly active in promoting the SDGs through advocacy, working with their local population and partners in transposing the spirit of Agenda 2030 in cities and territories. Local Governments have also started to use SDGs as a strategic framework to deliver better and more innovative public services linked to SDG targets and indicators.

To deliver more effectively on the above, UNDP is seeking to recruit a Programme Management Analyst, to provide technical advisory support to the SDG Local Action project, by effectively managing the project. A big percentage of the work requires guiding local and regional government implementation of innovative solutions for public service delivery including procurement management, and how this local action contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals. The Programme Management Analyst works under the guidance of the Advisor, Cities and Local Governments and in close collaboration with beneficiary cities around the world, UNDP Country Offices and a global project team based in more than 20 countries. The role includes to support local government´s procurement operations, monitoring project results and ensuring project efficiency.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Coordinate effective project planning and implementation

- Ensure compliance with UNDP policies and procedures in the management of the project’s procurement, including sourcing strategy, supplier selection and evaluation, quality management, customer relationship management and performance measurement.

- Ensuring compliance of operations with UN/UNDP rules, regulations and policies, implementation of corporate operational strategies, establishment of management targets and monitoring achievement of results.

- Ensure strategic resource management including planning of available resources, etc.

- Facilitate constant monitoring and analysis of the project operating environment, quick readjustment of the operations, advice on legal considerations and risk assessment.

- Support recruitment of project personnel by liaising with the Human Service Analyst and the beneficiary cities.

2. Ensure efficient project operations and monitor and report on progress

- Assist the Advisor, Cities and Local Government, helping to deliver on project operations on time.

- Liaise with city beneficiaries to better understand their needs and to assure that the project is contributing to local public service delivery.

- Prepare and maintains the project procurement plan, including e-tendering processes and evaluation, supports local governments to manage their contracts and vendors.

- Maintain all the project monitoring and implementation databases. Identifies improved project management systems and new digital tools available for project management.

- Maintain all project filing system updated with the necessary information for future auditing processes, to have clarity on what operations happened during the project activities for future inspections.

- Liaise with the finance team to monitor project commitment and expenditure levels against available resources and ensure that utilization of funds fully comply with UNDP financial rules and regulations.

- Monitor implementation and progress in achieving goals and targets in accordance with the established quality criteria and UNDP rules, regulations, and standards. Identify, analyze, and take adequate measures to manage emerging issues, problems, and risks.

- Establish partnerships and open channels of communication.

- Develop and maintain strong relationships and strategic linkages with implementing and development partners, government officials, businesses, NGOs, other national stakeholders, and beneficiaries to support key objectives and ensure inclusive implementation and participation of key stakeholders in assigned portfolio.

- Develop and maintain stakeholder mapping and analysis to identify stakeholder needs and how best to leverage their participation and/or strengthen their engagement. Prepare substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation and opportunities for joint initiatives. Make recommendations to the management team on activities with potential for scale-up, replicability and synergies.

3. Elaborate Terms of Reference and project documents and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Elaborate Terms of Reference for different services, goods and equipment, consultancies, LTAs, construction works and the development of digital and mobile tools.

- Work together with beneficiary cities to understand their needs and provide them with the best UNDP contracting option, including Letters of Agreement, procurement processes and responsible party agreements.

- Provide guidance on substantive and technical matters related to innovative basic service provision in cities.

- Facilitate knowledge building and sharing of best practices with regards to operational business processes.

- Contribute to creating capacities in the beneficiary cities regarding programme management and public service delivery through PPPs.

- Facilitate the development of project documents, prepares procurement plans and liaises with the Operations team to quickly respond to the needs of the project beneficiaries.

- Prepare monitoring reports for the donor on programme delivery.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

This position reports to the Advisor, Cities and Local Governments, based in New York

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business direction and strategy - System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management - Results-based Management

- Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results.

- Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments and tools.

Business Management - Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Procurement - Procurement Management

- The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source.

Procurement - Strategic sourcing

- Knowledge of strategic sourcing concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situtions.

Procurement - Supplier/relationship management

- Knowledge of supplier management concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or pratical situations.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (Master´s Degree or equivalent) in Economics, Law, Public Administration, Political Science, Urban Planning, Engineering, International Development or related field is required . Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of Master´s degree.

- CIPS level 3 is highly desirable for this position and candidates holding this level at the time of application will have a distinct advantage. If the desired certification is not available at the time of recruitment, it should be obtained within one year of recruitment. Candidates holding a CIPS certification at any level below at the time of application will have a proportionate advantage.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 2 years (with Master´s degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor´s degree) of working experience in procurement or project operations support with at least one (1) year of experience working closely with public administrations, preferably in issues related to service provision, public management and finance or public policy is required.

- Experience with UNDP procurement procedures or experience in UN project management is required.

- Experience preparing Terms of Reference for procurement and contracting processes is required.

Desired skills

- Experience working on Agenda 2030 and other UN global agendas will be an asset.

- Proven experience in working with local governments and their associations is an asset.

- Proven professional experience on use of results monitoring and reporting tools will be an asset.

- Experience working on innovation in the public sector will be an asset.

Language(s)

- Fluency in English is required.

- Working knowledge of another UN language is desired.

- Working knowledge of Portuguese will be an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.
