jobs.title: Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Liberia faces a complex and evolving humanitarian and protection context shaped by a combination of socioeconomic fragility, climate-related shocks, and pockets of recovery from past crises. Persistent poverty, high unemployment, food insecurity in vulnerable communities, and weak service delivery systems continue to expose significant segments of the population to heightened risk. Seasonal flooding, particularly in low-lying and densely populated areas such as Monrovia and surrounding counties, frequently leads to displacement, destruction of housing, disruption of livelihoods, and increased public health risks, further compounding household vulnerability.

Against this backdrop, protection risks remain significant, with Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (SEAH) continuing to be a critical concern within humanitarian and development settings. Liberia is consistently identified in regional safeguarding analyses as a context where SEA risks remain present due to structural vulnerabilities, limited access to complaint mechanisms in remote areas, power imbalances, and constrained institutional capacity. While awareness of Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards has improved across sectors, gaps remain in survivor-centered reporting systems, community trust in complaint mechanisms, and consistent accountability enforcement. Underreporting remains a key challenge, driven by fear of retaliation, stigma, and limited confidence that complaints will lead to meaningful action.

The UN and partners in Liberia have progressively strengthened collective safeguarding mechanisms through an inter-agency PSEA network composed of UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs/CSOs, donors, and relevant government counterparts. This network provides a coordinated platform for prevention, risk mitigation, and response to SEAH. It is typically chaired by an Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist, supported by rotating co-chairs, and links over 100 partner organizations across the humanitarian and development landscape. The network also engages a growing cadre of trained PSEA focal points to strengthen community outreach, awareness-raising, and safe referral pathways, while promoting survivor-centered approaches.

The inter-agency PSEA structure in Liberia reports to the UN Country Team (UNCT) and Humanitarian Country Team (HCT), which provide strategic oversight, guidance, and support for implementation of the collective PSEAH strategy and action plan. The Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist will report administratively to the Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) UNDP, to the Resident Coordinator/Humanitarian Coordinator, who holds system-wide accountability for advancing PSEA commitments across the UN and partners.

Investing in dedicated PSEA capacity in Liberia is essential to ensure that humanitarian and development assistance is delivered safely, ethically, and in line with “Do No Harm” principles. It strengthens accountability to affected populations, reduces reputational and operational risks, and supports donor expectations on safeguarding, gender equality, and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse.

Duties and Responsibilities

Strengthening Leadership, Accountability, and Coordination

- The role provides strategic leadership support to senior UN leadership in Liberia, particularly the Resident Coordinator (RC), UN Country Team (UNCT), and Humanitarian Country Team (HCT), to ensure effective Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH) across all UN and partner operations in Liberia.

- Provide strategic advisory support to senior leadership to ensure strong accountability for system-wide PSEAH implementation in Liberia.

- Collaborate closely with UN senior leadership to coordinate the inter-agency PSEAH Network in Liberia, including UN agencies, INGOs, national NGOs, civil society organizations, IFIs, and relevant Government of Liberia institutions.

- Represent inter-agency PSEAH priorities in key coordination platforms such as UNCT, HCT, OMT, Protection Cluster, Gender Theme Group, and other national coordination mechanisms.

- Work closely with Protection, GBV sub-sector, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Gender Theme Group, and sector leads to ensure PSEAH is fully integrated into programmes, policies, and joint planning frameworks in Liberia.

- Identify emerging risks, gaps, and trends related to SEAH in Liberia and advise RC/HC, UNCT/HCT, and the PSEAH Network on strategic and practical mitigation measures.

- Support senior leadership in developing resource mobilization strategies, Government of Liberia engagement strategies, and crisis communication and messaging strategies on PSEAH.

Leading Development of Liberia-Wide PSEAH Strategic Action Framework

- This function ensures a coordinated, country-wide strategic approach to PSEAH prevention and response across the UN system and partners in Liberia.

- Ensure annual inter-agency SEAH risk assessments are conducted in Liberia and that findings are integrated into sector assessments, UN planning frameworks (UNSDCF), and humanitarian response plans.

- Lead the development of a multi-year Liberia PSEAH Strategy with clear priorities, objectives, roles, and stakeholder responsibilities, including Government of Liberia and civil society engagement.

- Ensure alignment of PSEAH priorities with UNCT/HCT strategic planning processes and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) for Liberia.

- Develop a sustainability and exit strategy to ensure long-term national ownership and continued coordination of PSEAH mechanisms in Liberia.

- Promote integration of PSEAH within localization efforts and the humanitarian-development-peace nexus to strengthen national systems and institutions.

Oversight of Implementation of the Liberia PSEAH Programme

- This function focuses on ensuring effective coordination, implementation, and monitoring of PSEAH activities across Liberia.

- Support and advise Co-Chairs of the PSEAH Network in implementing the Network’s Terms of Reference (ToR) and Action Plan.

- Facilitate development and updating of the PSEAH Action Plan and Monitoring & Evaluation framework for Liberia.

- Conduct consultations with network members and senior leadership to assess gaps, strengths, and areas for improvement in PSEAH implementation.

- Support development of a sustainable resourcing plan for the Liberia PSEAH Programme.

- Provide regular updates and briefings to the PSEAH Network on emerging risks and implementation challenges.

- Strengthen national and in-country capacity by identifying skilled partners within the Network to lead training, mentorship, and capacity-building initiatives, including training of trainers (ToT) for PSEAH Network members.

- Promote collaboration between PSEAH Network, AAP, and CwC platforms to integrate community feedback into prevention and response systems.

- Assign and coordinate technical responsibilities within the Network to support information management, capacity building, and stakeholder engagement.

- Strengthening data systems to ensure risk assessment findings and case trends inform decision-making and programme improvements.

Strengthening Victim/Survivor-Centred Approach (VSCA) in Liberia

- This area ensures that all PSEAH interventions in Liberia prioritize dignity, safety, and rights of victims and survivors.

- Ensure coordination between the PSEAH Network and Protection Cluster, GBV sub-sector, and Child Protection actors in Liberia for a harmonized survivor-centred response.

- Serve in a senior advisory role supporting system-wide victim/survivor rights approaches within UN and partner agencies in Liberia.

- Coordinate with GBV and Protection actors to ensure consistency in prevention and response mechanisms across the UN system.

- Facilitate integration of community feedback mechanisms through AAP and CwC platforms to improve reporting and response systems.

- Support strengthening of Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs) across agencies to ensure safe, accessible reporting channels.

- Develop and support rollout of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for inter-agency SEAH referral pathways in Liberia.

- Ensure SOPs align with GBV and Child Protection referral systems and adhere to victim/survivor-centred principles.

- Support training of focal points and staff in safe reporting, complaint handling, and referral systems.

- Coordinate capacity-building initiatives on survivor-centred approaches across UN and partner organizations.

Stakeholder Engagement and Knowledge Sharing

- This function ensures strong coordination, advocacy, and knowledge sharing across national, regional, and global levels.

- Engage Government of Liberia institutions, UN agencies, NGOs, and civil society to strengthen PSEAH coordination and capacity-building.

- Represent inter-agency PSEAH priorities in UNCT, HCT, OMT, and regional coordination platforms.

- Provide regular briefings to UN leadership on PSEAH risks, progress, and implementation challenges in Liberia.

- Strengthen linkages with sub-national structures, including county-level actors, to ensure PSEAH integration across Liberia’s decentralized system.

- Liaise with regional and global PSEAH networks to ensure Liberia aligns with international standards and best practices.

- Support resource mobilization efforts for sustainable PSEAH programming in Liberia.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Inter-Agency PSEAH Specialist will report administratively to the Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) UNDP, directly to the Resident Coordinator (RC) with a dotted-line reporting responsibility to the Chair of the UN PSEA Network. In carrying out their duties, the Specialist will work closely with the UN Country Team (UNCT) and relevant partners, including UNDP programme units, PSEA and safeguarding focal points, and other staff and consultants supporting the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) agenda.

The Specialist will collaborate across UN agencies, technical teams, and coordination structures to ensure effective coordination, strong alignment, and successful implementation of PSEAH-related activities within the UN system.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

- Act with Determination : LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

Cross Functional and Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system.

- Negotiation and Influence Ability to reach an understanding, persuade others, resolve points of difference, gain advantage in the outcome of dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions through compromise and create win-win situations.

Business Management

- Results-based Management Ability to manage Programme and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results.

- Partnerships Management Ability to build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Communications

- Creative direction and copywriting Ability to creatively communicate concepts in an engaging and simple way.

2030 Agenda:

- Peace Governance Electoral Cycle Support.

- People Gender Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Social Work, Public Health, Gender Studies, Law, Human Rights, Humanitarian Studies, International Relations, and/or another related social science discipline is required. OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of five (5) years of experience (with a Master’s degree), or seven (7) years of experience (with a Bachelor’s degree), in Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), protection, human rights, and/or gender-based violence or a related field is required.

Required skills:

- Experience in coordination and stakeholder engagement skills: Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-agency or multisectoral groups, evidenced by successfully facilitating at least 4–6 inter-agency coordination meetings per year and ensuring actionable follow-up on agreed recommendations, is required.

- Experience in data analysis and reporting skills: Ability to collect, analyze, and interpret PSEA-related data, with proven experience producing at least quarterly analytical reports that inform decision-making and risk mitigation strategies, is required.

- Experience in capacity-building and training skills/experience: Experience designing and delivering PSEA training sessions, demonstrated by conducting a minimum of 3–5 training or awareness sessions annually for staff, partners, or community stakeholders, is required.

- Experience in communication and advocacy skills: Strong ability to develop clear messaging and advocacy materials on PSEA, demonstrated through the production of regular communication products—such as briefings, awareness materials, or campaigns—at least 2–4 times per year and engagement with diverse audiences, is required.

- Experience in field experience in humanitarian and/or development settings in PSEAH is required.

Desired knowledges and skills:

- Experience in risk assessment and safeguarding skills: Ability to conduct PSEA risk assessments across programmes or operations, evidenced by completing at least 1–2 formal risk assessments per programme cycle, including mitigation recommendations, is desired.

- Experience working in Liberia, the Sahel, and West Africa is an advantage.

- Experience in an inter-agency coordination role is an advantage.

- Demonstrated experience in international development and humanitarian architecture is desired.

- Proven familiarity with the UN system and global coordination structures (e.g., IASC, UNSDCF) and coordination structures at response level (clusters, sectors) is desired.

- Proven ability to develop an Action Plan/Strategy is desired.

- Familiarity with data protection and confidentiality measures is desired.

- Demonstrated experience in leading strategic processes is desired.

- Previous work with UNDP, another United Nations entity, a development partner, a donor-funded programme, or an international/non-governmental organization is desired.

In December 1991, the General Assembly adopted Resolution 46/182 designed to strengthen the United Nation's response to both complex emergencies and natural disasters. In addition, it aimed at improving the overall effectiveness of the UN's humanitarian operations in the field.

Background and Organizational Context

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994. UNDP has a strong track record and comparative advantage to support the achievement of national priorities and United Nations Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNMSDCF). It is one of the leading United Nations agencies present in Suriname in terms of programmatic scope, partnerships and financial footprint. The advantage of UNDP is illustrated by the achievements during the program cycle 2022-2026, which supported the priorities around democratic governance, sustainable development and climate action. The Country Program 2027-2031 will focus on supporting Suriname around two strategic programme areas: (a) democratic governance for inclusive transformation; and (b) resilience and environmental protection.

UNDP’s support to the Democratic Governance for Inclusive Transformation will include four interlinked priorities: a) electoral support; b) decentralization and local governance; c) revenue governance and public financial management; and d) digitalization and innovation. In addition, UNDP Suriname will continue as the funding recipient of the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Suriname and facilitates the CCM Secretariat. Other programmatic priorities may be included in consultation with the development partners and stakeholders in Suriname. In its interventions, UNDP prioritizes participation of all, including women, youth, and ITPs as a way to increase institutional effectiveness and improve transparency, accountability, and inclusion in public decision-making.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative/Head of Office, the Programme Analyst (Effective Governance and Inclusive Transformation) is responsible for managing and further expanding the programme portfolio and creating synergies, complementarities and linkages with the resilience and environment protection work of UNDP, applying a portfolio approach.

Specifically, the role includes executing and expanding current projects, building a pipeline of new initiatives that are aligned with Suriname’s national priorities, and UNDP’s policies, programmatic and operational offer globally and in the region. Importantly, the incumbent will be responsible for maintaining and expanding UNDP’s partnerships with the Government, bilateral donors, UN agencies, vertical funds (GEF, GCF, others), the EU, IFIs and other partner organizations.

The incumbent will support the senior management of the UNDP Suriname in the design and execution of thematic and sectoral strategies, knowledge management, partnerships, and support the implementation of other strategic initiatives.

The Programme Programme Analyst (Effective Governance and Inclusive Transformation) will supervise the Programme Associate and be a part of a multidisciplinary team working closely with other thematic portfolio and the Operations team at UNDP Suriname, the Regional Bureau for LAC, the Regional Hub in Panama and the technical and operational teams across UNDP.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Resident Representative (RR), Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) the Programme Analyst is responsible for management of UNDP programme within the thematic/sectoral areas assigned. The Programme Analyst analyzes political, social and economic trends; leads formulation, management and evaluation of programme activities within his/her portfolio; and provides policy advice services.

The Programme Analyst supervises and leads the Programme Associate and coordinates activities of the project’s staff. The Programme Analyst works in close collaboration with the Programme and Operations teams in the CO, programme staff in other UN Agencies, UNDP staff in HQs and Regional Hubs, technical advisors/experts, external specialists, government officials and partners, donors, and civil society to ensure successful implementation of the UNDP programme.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

1. Contribute to formulation and Implementation of UNDP Programme Strategies and policies

- Analyze socio-political, governance, and social development trends and identify areas for UNDP support.

- Lead the development and execution of thematic strategies on governance, poverty reduction, social services, and SDG integration.

- Provide technical input to national planning processes (e.g., CCA, UNMSDCF, CPD).

- Promote inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches in programme design and delivery.

2. Ensure effective management of the CO programme within the assigned thematic/sector areas focusing on quality assurance and risk management from formulation to implementation of the country programme

- Design and formulate programme/project proposals, ensuring alignment with national development goals and UNDP priorities.

- Apply RBM tools and manage project implementation, financials, and reporting.

- Ensure programme results and indicators are met in a timely and efficient manner.

- Organize and support evaluations, audits, and strategic reviews.

3. Build strategic partnerships and resource mobilization

- Develop and strengthen partnerships with government, UN agencies, donors, NGOs, civil society, and the private sector.

- Identify funding opportunities and contribute to the office’s resource mobilization strategy.

- Contribute to joint programming and inter-agency collaboration, especially around social development and governance reform.

4. Policy Advisory Services and Knowledge Management

- Provide policy advice to government counterparts in governance, poverty alleviation, and inclusive development, with a particular focus on the Indigenous and Tribal communities, youth, women and other groups.

- Facilitate the development of evidence-based policies and institutional reforms related to governance and inclusive transformation.

- Document and disseminate best practices, lessons learned, and knowledge products.

- Foster internal and external knowledge sharing and innovation, including through UNDP Communities of Practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Education

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics, Public Administration, Business Administration, Law, Political, Social Sciences, Environmental or Development Studies, or any other related field is required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

- A minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in programme management, policy analysis, and stakeholder engagement is required.

- Experience working with government institutions, civil society, vulnerable groups, including Indigenous and Tribal Peoples (ITPs) and People with Disabilities (PWDs), and international development partners is required.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP is required.

- Experience of leading and supervising multidisciplinary teams is required.

- Experience in design, implementation and/or evaluation of development projects is desired.

- Familiarity with UN/UNDP systems, procedures, and programming frameworks is an asset.

- Experience in working with multidisciplinary issues such as Governance, Climate Change, Local Development, Social Inclusion, Economic Transformation, Gender, Youth, Digitalization (is desired) or other development related field is a strong asset.

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Republic of Moldova's EU accession process and decentralization reform require stronger inter-communal cooperation to improve the planning and delivery of essential public services that benefit equally men and women, including from marginalized/vulnerable groups. While Intercommunal Development Associations (IDAs) have significant potential to support integrated territorial development, they continue to face legal, institutional, and capacity constraints. The project will support the Government of the Republic of Moldova, through the State Chancellery and partner local authorities, to strengthen the inter-communal cooperation framework by improving the regulatory framework, developing and piloting an integrated strategic planning methodology for IDAs, and establishing a digital platform for coordination and knowledge sharing. The project will also facilitate peer exchange with French local authorities to strengthen capacities in territorial governance, essential and inclusive public service delivery, and access to EU funding, contributing to more effective people-centered local governance and enhanced readiness for EU integration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the PRIM Project Manager, the Public Services Improvement Analyst ensures the effective and efficient implementation of local public service improvement at local level. The incumbent applies and promotes the principles of results-based management (RBM), as well as a client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations.

Public Services Improvement Analyst works in close collaboration with the Programme Specialist/Cluster Lead and other Project Managers for effective achievement of results and resolving complex project- related issues and information delivery.

The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies, as well as implementation of the effective internal control systems.

The incumbent will ensure the provision of development services and products (commensurate with the scope of the project) of the highest quality and standards to national counterparts and clients through applying HRBA and GE approaches. More specifically:

1. Support to local public service improvement issues, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Advise and assist targeted local public authorities to develop and implement capacity building plans in the area of local public service improvement, through participatory community involvement processes.

- Promote a participatory, human rights and gender sensitive approach to service provision at local level in close coordination with other local and national partners.

- Support the implementation of jointly selected service improvement initiatives, with active participation of community members (using inter-municipal cooperation, PPPs and other tools) and through expansion of the services currently rendered in the urban centers towards the neighboring communities.

- Support in general project development, implementation and project-related strategic processes.

2. Ensure provision of top-quality advisory services and facilitation of knowledge building and management, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Provide policy options and high-quality advisory inputs to the project from local development perspective to ensure these are responsive to national policies, priorities and strategic plans, and advance UNDP's corporate goals.

- Provide training and capacity building support on local public service improvement.

- Make sound contributions to local development-related knowledge networks and communities of practice

- Provide solid inputs to project’s analytical products, work plans and progress reports, etc.

- Identify and synthesis of best practices and lessons learnt from the field.

- Conduct analytical work (e.g. institutional and risk analyses, capacity assessment, policy reviews) community development highlighting UNDP support and strategy. Play an active role in policy advice, strategic thinking, knowledge sharing.

3. Ensure creation of strategic partnerships, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Liaise, synergy and coordination with project partners on common service provision issues.

- Prepare substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation with development partners, contribute to the resource mobilization efforts.

- Ensure wide dissemination and visibility of project achievements. Participate in national and international fora, making substantive contributions as appropriate.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

The key results have a direct impact on the overall successful achievement of the Project. Accurate analysis and presentation of information enhances UNDP's position as a strong development partner. The information provided facilitates decision-making of UNDP management.

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Objetivo do Cargo e Contexto Organizacional

O projeto “Fortalecimento e monitoramento das ações de inovação e aperfeiçoamento dos sistemas penal e socioeducativo, em linha com princípios e diretrizes nacionais e internacionais de direitos humanos”, tem por objetivo atuar no desenvolvimento de metodologias e ações inovadoras com foco em restabelecer o regular e adequado funcionamento do sistema prisional e socioeducativo, além de produzir subsídios para fortalecer o monitoramento e a fiscalização das intervenções oficiais sobre esses sistemas, alinhado aos princípios e diretrizes nacionais e internacionais de direitos humanos. Em especial, o projeto atuará de forma a instrumentalizar o Conselho Nacional de Justiça – CNJ para: (i) o fomento ao desenvolvimento dos mandatos e das capacidades (constitucionais, convencionais e legais) do Poder Judiciário para a superação de gargalos e dos entraves que dificultam a performance individual e uma melhor atuação coletiva de magistrados diante dos sistemas penal e socioeducativo, notadamente para a proteção das posições de populações mais vulneráveis, e (ii) a atuação na viabilização do pleno e integral cumprimento da decisão (de mérito) proferida pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal na ADPF 347, que consolidou o entendimento acerca da existência de um estado de coisas inconstitucional das prisões brasileiras, determinando a pactuação e o monitoramento de um plano nacional e de planos estaduais e distrital voltados à superação de um quadro de desarranjos estruturais e de violação massiva e sistemática a direitos fundamentais – cenário que impede a realização da gramática e dos programas de princípios presentes na Constituição Federal, nos Tratados Internacionais de Direitos Humanos e na Legislação ordinária.

Para o alcance desses objetivos, o projeto se organiza em 6 linhas de atuação, que correspondem aos resultados intermediários esperados:

1 Implantação, fortalecimento e acompanhamento/avaliação de ações que garantam o regular funcionamento do sistema penal;

2 Implantação, fortalecimento e acompanhamento/avaliação de ações que garantam o regular funcionamento do sistema socioeducativo;

3 Aperfeiçoamento e incremento quantitativo e qualitativo da coleta e produção de dados oriundos dos sistemas penal e socioeducativo;

4 Aperfeiçoamento, fortalecimento e acompanhamento de estratégias de atenção a populações mais vulneráveis em contato com os sistemas penal e socioeducativo;

5 Assessoria técnica ao CNJ para incidência junto à magistratura de 1º e 2º graus, por meio de criação de canais de sensibilização e comunicação, disseminação de conteúdos, formação, treinamento, estratégias de interação, diálogo e outras ações que permitam melhor instrumentalizar o cabedal das opções de atuação dos juízes brasileiros, viabilizando-lhes práticas mais compreensivas quanto à população e suas desigualdades;

6 Gestão eficiente e gestão de conhecimento do projeto realizadas.

A presente contratação se insere na linha de atuação 3 acima descrita na área de Sistemas e Projetos para atendimento à Coordenação Estratégica de Tecnologia da Informação, considerando a necessidade de qualificação das informações dos sistemas da justiça criminal e penal, bem como de execução de medidas socioeducativas do CNJ, que impactam de forma transversal nas ações implementadas pelo Programa Fazendo Justiça, agregando-se às ações correlatas que já se encontram em curso para os dois sistemas desenvolvidos diretamente pelo programa (SEEU e Plataforma do Socioeducativo). Após quatro anos de implantação das iniciativas da primeira fase do Programa, verificou-se a necessidade de aprimoramento das rotinas de preenchimento, análise e sistematização dos dados dos sistemas informatizados geridos pelo CNJ em atuação no ciclo penal e socioeducativo, notadamente o sistema que registra as informações da audiência de custódia (SISTAC), o banco de dados que registra as ordens judiciais relativas a mandatos de prisão, alvarás de soltura e medidas penais (BNMP), do cadastro das inspeções prisionais (CNIEP) e de internação do socioeducativo (CNIUPS), entre outros. Esse esforço permitirá depurar e sistematizar melhores informações para implantação das políticas judiciárias nessas áreas, colaborando com iniciativas das linhas de atuação temáticas. Além de apoiar no uso de novas tecnologias que colaboram para o aprimoramento da qualidade das informações e do monitoramento das políticas públicas penais sob a responsabilidade do CNJ.

Os resultados-chave esperados para este posto visam garantir a qualidade, eficiência e efetividade na implementação do projeto, em linha com as metas acordadas e com as prioridades do CNJ.

O projeto tem vigência atualmente até 31/12/2027.

Deveres e responsabilidades

A/o Analista Técnico em Programação (DevOps) será responsável por, sob supervisão do coordenador estratégico de tecnologia da informação da área de Sistemas e Projetos, realizar a assessoria técnica ao planejamento, implementação e acompanhamento de ações de desenvolvimento de sistemas previstas nesta área, colaborando para o cumprimento do cronograma estabelecido e para a qualidade das entregas realizadas no que tange a área de Sistemas. Este/a profissional atuará ainda em estreita articulação com a equipe do CNJ e do PNUD. Para o alcance desse objetivo, estão previstas as seguintes atividades indicativas:

1. Preparação de ambientes tecnológicos e atuação em diagnósticos, monitoramento e documentação

a. Preparar ambientes de teste, homologação, webservices e ambiente tecnológico condizente com metas, entregas e ações previstas no âmbito da área de Sistemas.

b. Atuar no diagnóstico de erros, monitoramento e documentação técnica das soluções, contribuindo para a disseminação e reutilização do conhecimento

c. Realizar os alinhamentos necessários com a Coordenação da área de Sistemas e Projetos.

2. Criação de utilitários, produtos e scripts para entrega automatizada e suporte a integrações e equipes

a. Criar e suportar a criação de utilitários, produtos e scripts para entrega automatizada.

b. Suportar a integração e release das soluções.

c. Suportar a equipe de desenvolvimento com o deploy ou migração dos sistemas para cloud privada ou pública;

d. Suportar a equipe de desenvolvimento na implantação de soluções baseadas em microsserviços.

e. Apoiar na automatização dos fluxos de integração contínua e entrega contínua.

f. Apoiar as equipes de desenvolvimento de software a trabalhar com infraestrutura como código.

3. Elaboração e registros de documentação

a. Elaborar, tratar registros de documentação ativa dos trabalhos;

b. Seguir fluxos de uso de ferramentas de acompanhamento dos serviços pactuados e executados.

c. Realizar registros no JIRA destinados ao recebimento e acompanhamento das demandas permitindo maior rastreabilidade, transparência e controle sobre o ciclo de vida de solicitações de TI.

d. Realizar entregas previstas para o cumprimento das metas, dos cronogramas e dos resultados pactuados.

e. Assegurar o alinhamento das demandas e atividades às prioridades e às ações no âmbito da área de Sistemas e Projetos.

4. Análise e integração das soluções

a. Contribuir com análises e resoluções de problemas técnicos, monitorar desempenho, investigar falhas e aplicar correções sem interrupção dos serviços.

b. Facilitar a comunicação entre áreas de desenvolvimento, tecnologia e operações.

5. Fomento à Gestão do conhecimento

a. Subsidiar a Coordenação da área de Sistemas e Projetos com informações, dados e levantamentos relacionados ao desenvolvimento de sistemas informatizados.

b. Apoiar a elaboração e divulgação de relatórios, matérias e informativos, visando à transparência da execução do Projeto.

c. Facilitar a construção de capacidades institucionais nas áreas temáticas atribuídas.

d. Fomentar a promoção de partilha de conhecimento e ações relacionadas à Sistemas informatizados sob responsabilidade da área de Sistemas e Projetos.

O(a) titular desempenha outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que a coordenação considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do Projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

A/o Analista Técnico em Programação (DevOps) - Inovação e Tecnologia, integrará a equipe da área de Sistemas e Projetos, na linha de atuação 3, e estará submetido/a à supervisão direta do Coordenador Estratégico de Tecnologia da Informação da área de Sistemas e Projetos.

Competências

- Alcançar Resultados - NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora seu próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes e entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo.

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas e riscos conhecidos, é um solucionador de problemas prático e faz melhorias.

- Aprender Continuamente - NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curioso, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros e pede feedback.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se às mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidades e incertezas, e é flexível..

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra determinação e motivação, mantém a calma diante da adversidade e tem confiança.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão e compreensão em relação aos outros, formando relacionamentos positivos.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios / Pensamento Estratégico

- Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Gestão de Negócios / Gestão de Projetos

- Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

- Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

- Capacidade de monitorar tecnologias novas e emergentes, bem como compreender seu uso, potencial, limitações, impacto e valor agregado. Habilidade de adotar rapidamente novas tecnologias nas atividades profissionais e capacitar outras pessoas a fazer o mesmo.

- Diploma do Ensino Superior (Bacharelado) nas áreas mencionadas acima, combinado com 2 (dois) anos adicionais de experiência qualificada, será devidamente considerado em substituição ao Diploma Universitário avançado.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

- Candidatos com Diploma Universitário avançado (Mestrado ou equivalente) em área relevante não precisam de experiência profissional. Candidatos com Diploma de Ensino Superior (Bacharelado) devem possuir, no mínimo, 2 (dois) anos de experiência na área de Tecnologia da Informação, com atuação em desenvolvimento, implantação, integração, automação ou operação de sistemas e ambientes tecnológicos.

- Experiência de trabalho em desenvolvimento de sistemas automatizados no setor público.

- Experiência de uso da Maven, LLM, N8N, message brokers (Ex: RabbitMQ,Kafka)

jobs.title: Communications Analyst/EVRF, Short-Term
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous references and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet.

Amid a dynamic socio-economic context of Moldova, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP) is embarking on a deeply transformative process. The “Digital Transformation of Social Protection” Project, financed by the Government of Italy through the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), stands as testimony to this momentum forward. Moldovan social protection system faces substantial challenges caused by inefficiencies, limited digital integration, and an unmet demand for institutional framework and service delivery better addressing contemporary socio-economic uncertainties. The MLSP's endeavour is to reengineer this landscape, enhance its digital infrastructure and create a framework that is efficient, inclusive, resilient, and adaptable to changing contexts and conditions. The Ministry has launched three major reforms, namely that of social services (RESTART); that of the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI); and that of the National Council for Determination of Disability and Work Capacity (CNDDCM). These initiatives are not just a response to evolving needs but a visionary stride towards a future where social protection is seamlessly inclusive, empowering, and a realized right for every citizen, as defined by the 2030 Agenda.

The Project aims to address the fragmented digital infrastructure of the social protection system, which currently operates with multiple, disparate, and non-interoperable information systems. This fragmentation causes binding inefficiencies in data management and service delivery and undermines the ability to provide timely and appropriate support to beneficiaries. By developing a new, integrated Information System – eSocial, the Project aims to achieve delivery of social protection & employment services in a more coherent, accessible, and resilient way, enhancing the Ministry's ability to meet existing demands and adapt to future changes.

Complementing the processes above, the Project supports the enhancement and institutionalization of the Ministry’s capacities to lead ongoing efforts of digitalisation of social protection services via a dedicated Digital Center for Social Innovation (DCSI), which will ensure the intervention’s sustainability and advancements. DCSI experts engaged by the Project support the development of the eSocial digital platform and its adoption within MLSP and subordinated institutions: ATAS (regional agencies for social assistance), STAS (regional structures for social assistance), NEA, SLI, CNDDCM, AGSSSI (the Agency for the Management of Highly Specialized Social Services), etc.

Additionally, with UNDP support, the Government has established the Energy Vulnerability Reduction Fund (EVRF), an evidence‑based compensation scheme that has already supported hundreds of thousands of households during past heating seasons.

This support is closely coordinated with UNDP’s Digital Transformation of Social Protection project financed by the Government of Italy, ensuring coherence across reforms, alignment of digital architectures, and interoperability between employment and social protection systems within a unified government-wide digital ecosystem.

The Projects’ strategic approach is rooted in Moldova’s national priorities, as defined by the RESTART Reform of Social Assistance and the UNDP Country Programme Document for the Republic of Moldova (2023-2027). The Project is designed to leverage technology as a key driver of change, streamline processes, enhance user experience, and strengthen institutional resilience. It involves comprehensive mapping and optimization of current business processes, ensuring they are streamlined and designed for the best possible user experience.

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of key functions:

The Communications Analyst/EVRF in close cooperation with the project team, under the direct supervision of the “Digital Transformation of Social Protection” Project Manager, will provide dedicated support to the EVRF communication and visibility plan for the 2026‑2027 heating season, while also contributing to broader communication efforts of the project, contribute to the design, planning, execution, monitoring and reporting of the project activities related to communication and visibility, aimed at increasing public awareness, promoting transparency, and ensuring visibility of EVRF results, while supporting overall project visibility. More specifically:

I. EVRF focused communication:

- Develop and implement the EVRF Communication and Visibility Action Plan for the 2026 2027 heating season.

- Identify key audiences and effective communication channels to ensure inclusive and accessible outreach.

- Draft public facing materials (talking points, briefs, factsheets, presentations) aligned with EVRF milestones and legal updates.

- Draft and disseminate press releases, stories, and newsletters highlighting progress and showcasing the impact of the EVRF.

- Maintain and update public facing content on compensatii.gov.md, including FAQs, registration guidance, and automated notifications (SMS/email/pop ups) in Romanian, Russian, and English.

- Document and promote success stories and testimonials from EVRF beneficiaries and implementers (social workers, hotline staff, librarians).

- Support awareness campaigns, public events, and outreach activities, including the annual launch of the heating season.

- Produce and adapt communication materials and visual content (infographics, short videos, social media posts).

- Monitor outreach performance using analytics and feedback tools; adjust strategies accordingly.

II. Effective Project Communication:

- Contribute to the implementation of the Projects’ Communication Strategies and Visibility Plans in close collaboration with the Project Manager, DTSP Communication Analyst and UNDP Communications Analyst.

- Support the national partners in designing and implementation of joint civic education and information campaigns, as well as in developing and delivering the key messages.

- Draft talking points, briefs, factsheets, handout materials and dynamic presentations, considering the gender and human rights aspects.

- Provide advice and recommendations to mitigate potential public communication crisis and sensible issues. This shall include, but not be limited to, press monitoring (pre and post crisis), drafting of press releases and/or written reactions, and ad-hoc crisis reports.

- Contribute to the implementation of awareness campaigns, trainings, workshops, and public events, using various channels of communication and engaging with media representatives for a broader audience.

- Develop engaging digital content (infographics, illustrations, quote cards, videos, social media posts) to simplify complex topics related to energy vulnerability, social protection, digital services and project interventions and increase public understanding.

- Facilitate regular consultations and dialogue with national partners and stakeholders to ensure their perspectives are well reflected in the civic education and public awareness efforts.

- Develop news pieces, success stories, scripts for video reportages and coordinate with subcontracted photographers and videographers;

- Establish and manage stakeholder communication channels, including newsletters, working groups, and online platforms, to ensure continuous engagement.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

The Communications Analyst/EVRF will work under the supervision of the UNDP Project Manager in close coordination with the DTSP Communication Analyst and the UNDP Communications Analyst, in close cooperation with the UNDP Moldova Country Office and overall project team, for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery.

He/she also will collaborate with other UN projects, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Industry and other national stakeholders (the National Employment Agency; the National Office of Social Insurance; AIPA; etc.). The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP administrative rules, regulations, policies, and strategies.

Achieve results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional and Technical Competencies

Business Development - Knowledge facilitation:

- Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas.

- Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Management - Communication:

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Management - Digital Awareness and Literacy:

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value.

- Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed.

- Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

Communications - Campaign management:

- Ability to produce and implement communications and advocacy campaigns which lead to impactful change.

Communications - Creative direction and copywriting:

- Ability to creatively communicate concepts in an engaging and simple way.

Digital - Data storytelling and communications:

- Skilled in building a narrative around a set of data and its accompanying visualizations to help convey the meaning of that data in a powerful and compelling fashion

2030 Agenda: People - Gender:

- Communication and Advocacy for Gender Equality.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Journalism, Communication, Public Relations, Sociology, International Relations, or another relevant field, or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a Master’s degree are not required to have prior professional experience.

- At least two years (with Bachelor’s Degree) in communication, mass-media, public relations, and/or other substantive area is required.

Desired skills:

- Proven experience in similar positions in UNDP or other UN Agencies.

- Proven experience in working in the areas of social protection, energy vulnerability, energy efficiency or employment.

- Previous experience in development assistance or related work for a development organization, governmental institution, NGO or private sector / consulting firm.

- Experience in development and implementation of media/communications strategies and plans, visibility and awareness raising campaigns, drafting communication materials and products.

- Experience in conceptualizing and implementing national and local public outreach/communication campaigns.

Required languages:

- Fluency in Romanian and English is required;

- Knowledge of one or more minority languages relevant for Moldova, including Russian, Romani, Gagauzian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian and sign language, is an asset.

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.title: Anti-Corruption Analyst, Short-Term (multiple post)
jobs.description:
Background

Preventing and combating corruption is a priority for the Government of the Republic of Moldova and central to its European Union accession agenda. The authorities have adopted the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme 2024–2028 and are strengthening the institutions that deliver it. Moldova is also a State Party to the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), and these reforms support its implementation. The focus is now on putting these frameworks into practice, with sustained technical support.

UNDP implements one component of the EU-funded project ‘Support in combating and preventing corruption and organized crime in the Republic of Moldova’, together with Expertise France and Civipol. The consortium project seeks to reduce corruption and financial crime, including money laundering, by strengthening effective, efficient, independent, and accountable justice, prosecution, and investigation systems. The project will support the application of EU standards and relevant OECD and GRECO recommendations, strengthen institutional ownership, and promote preventive, risk-based, and evidence-driven approaches to integrity management.

The UNDP component is delivered as part of the REDACT project. REDACT (Resilient Democracy through Anti-Corruption) strengthens the capacities of anti-corruption, law enforcement and justice institutions, improves coordination among them, and supports oversight by civil society and the media. More information is available on the REDACT project page.

Under the UNDP-led project component, the intended outcome is to enhance institutional capacities across government to mainstream anti-corruption and integrity frameworks. A central intervention is focused on supporting the establishment and mentoring of a cross-institutional network of integrity, ethics, and corruption-prevention practitioners. Additionally technical assistance to enhance corruption risk identification and mitigation through a combination of strategic analysis, legislative review, sectoral analysis, and digital analytical enablement will be provided.

The Anti-Corruption Analyst will provide substantive and analytical leadership on the activities of the UNDP-led component that relate to the monitoring of the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme, support to the existing cross-institutional network of integrity and ethics tutors, the reinforcement and adaptation of national integrity and anti-corruption instruments, and the strengthening of institutional analytical capacities to identify and address integrity risks.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Anti-Corruption Analyst will have responsibility to deliver substantive technical outputs and effective engagement with partners. The incumbent will act as a technical lead and trusted adviser to national partners, and is expected to spend a large part of the working time with the partner institutions, at their premises, in their working groups and in consultations, delivering analysis, providing hands-on technical assistance and helping institutions align their work. Building relationships of trust and credibility with national actors is central to the role.

I. Lead Technical and Substantive Support on NIAP Monitoring, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Instruments, and Institutional Risk Analysis:

- Lead the technical implementation of the assigned activities (NIAP monitoring, support to the network of integrity and ethics tutors, integrity and anti-corruption instruments, and institutional analytical capacity), providing hands-on analysis and advice to the partner institutions and the Project Team.

- Lead the substantive support to the National Anti-Corruption Centre (NAC) in coordinating, monitoring and evaluating the implementation of the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme (NIAP) 2024–2028, including indicator frameworks, data collection and reporting protocols, and quarterly monitoring cycles with implementing institutions.

- Provide the substantive content for the digital monitoring dashboards (indicators, visualisation logic, reporting formats and analytical outputs) in close cooperation with the ICT Analyst, who leads their technical implementation, and, for the monitoring of integrity and work ethics guidelines, with the tutors and reporting institutions.

- Support the preparation of periodic, data-driven NIAP progress reports and of the quarterly progress-reporting meetings with responsible institutions, and facilitate peer exchange among the members of the NIAP Monitoring Group, reporting institutions and civil society.

- Provide advisory support to the midterm review and final evaluation of the NIAP, including the methodology, terms of reference and quality assurance of evaluation outputs, and coordinate the engagement of civil society organisations in independent shadow reporting.

- Guide the review of the legislative and regulatory framework for integrity and anti-corruption mainstreaming, including its alignment with EU standards and OECD and GRECO recommendations, and contribute to the preparation of regulatory proposals.

- Support the adaptation of existing national integrity and anti-corruption instruments, including integrity plans and early-warning and data-sharing mechanisms, in close cooperation with NAC, the National Integrity Authority (NIA) and other relevant institutions.

- Contribute to the review and update of integrity and ethics learning materials, including a training track for newly elected local officials, and to awareness-raising on integrity obligations and tools, in cooperation with NAC, NIA and the National Institute of Public Administration and Management (INAMP).

- Support the engagement of civil society organisations and the private sector in detecting, analysing and reporting integrity risks, including through the reLAWed platform and the interoperability of the e-Expertise system with Particip.gov.md.

- Lead the substantive work on strengthening NAC’s capacity to analyse integrity plans and to identify trends, recurring risks and sectoral vulnerabilities, including analytical training and mentoring of NAC officials.

- Guide targeted corruption risk assessments in the sectors identified as highest risk and the development of risk remediation plans, ensuring methodological soundness and the use of the evidence generated.

- Facilitate the co-creation of legislative and regulatory proposals between NAC and other institutions on the basis of the risk assessment findings.

- Support the National Integrity Authority in strengthening its analytical and oversight capacities on asset and personal interest declarations, including risk typologies, verification methods and the referral of cases to law enforcement.

- Conduct research, analytical reviews, assessments, mapping exercises, and other evidence-based analyses to inform project interventions, policy dialogue, and decision-making processes.

- Develop and contribute to technical papers, concept notes, guidance materials, analytical reports, recommendations, briefs, and other substantive knowledge products relevant to the project objectives.

- Support the identification of institutional needs, opportunities, risks, and challenges related to governance, integrity, accountability, and anti-corruption mainstreaming and reforms, and propose practical solutions and recommendations.

- Review and provide technical feedback on deliverables prepared by consultants, service providers, implementing partners, and other stakeholders to ensure quality and alignment with project objectives.

- Monitor developments, trends, good practices, and emerging issues relevant to the assigned thematic areas and provide technical advice to support adaptive project implementation.

- Document technical lessons learned and good practices from the assigned activities and feed them into the policy dialogue with partners.

II. Contribute to the network of integrity and ethics tutors:

- Contribute to the further development of the existing network of integrity and ethics tutors, the in-house focal points designated by state institutions, and of the related communities of practice, working with NAC and the participating institutions.

- Provide technical input to the competency model for the tutors and to their structured training, including on building trust in the tutoring mechanism within institutions, confidential peer advice, integrity plans, mitigation measures, corruption risk assessment and compliance.

- Contribute technical sessions and mentoring to the training of the tutors, and guide expert trainers where engaged, so that the tutors apply consistent methodologies and monitor implementation in their institutions.

- Support NAC in convening regular community-of-practice meetings, and contribute technical content to joint working groups, case-based learning, exchange visits and the online learning space on MLearn; logistics for meetings, visits and events are organised with the Project Analyst and Operations.

- Facilitate peer-to-peer exchanges, in which high-performing institutions share their experience with others, and structured dialogue among NAC, the tutors and civil society.

- Capture insights from the tutors on emerging risks, vulnerabilities and good practices, and feed them into NAC’s risk analysis and the adaptation of integrity instruments.

III. Lead the implementation of the assigned activities:

- Act as a subject matter expert for the assigned interventions, leading on the substance and guiding the work of other experts and service providers where engaged, and provide timely technical advice and support to the Project Team and stakeholders and ensure outputs are delivered on time and to high-quality standards.

- Ensure that the analyses, instruments and capacity building supported under the assigned activities integrate a gender equality and inclusion perspective, to the extent the local context allows.

- Draft the technical specifications and terms of reference for the studies, expertise and services required under the assigned activities, and assess the technical quality of offers where requested; procurement itself is managed by the Project Analyst and Operations.

- Keep the Project Manager regularly informed on the substance and status of the assigned activities and of the relationships with partners, flagging emerging risks and needed adjustments early.

IV. Build relationships of trust and provide hands-on support to national partners:

- Work side by side with NAC, NIA, INAMP, the integrity and ethics tutors and other public institutions, spending a large part of the working time at their premises and in their meetings, to understand their mandates, priorities and constraints and to provide timely, practical and candid technical advice.

- Act as the day-to-day technical interlocutor of the counterpart institutions for the assigned activities, building and sustaining relationships of trust with senior officials, technical staff, civil society organisations and academia on the basis of reliability, discretion and technical credibility.

- Align the project’s support with the institutions’ own plans and priorities, and help the institutions align with one another (including on methods, data-sharing and the division of responsibilities), so that results are owned and sustained by national actors.

- Represent UNDP at technical level in the NIAP Monitoring Group, working groups and coordination platforms, and coordinate with the other partners supporting Moldova’s anti-corruption reforms, including the consortium partners of the EU-funded project, to ensure complementarity.

V. Contribute substantive inputs to project monitoring and reporting:

- Provide accurate and timely substantive inputs (evidence, analysis, indicator data and progress narrative) on the assigned activities to the Project Analyst and the Project Manager for the project, donor and government reports, which they compile.

- Identify, analyze, and report emerging issues, problems, and risks to the Project Manager, and support in implementing mitigation measures.

VI. Build institutional capacity and share technical knowledge:

- Design the technical content of, and deliver or lead, capacity building for partner institutions (including analytical mentoring, peer learning and training), involving technical experts and service providers where needed; logistics are organised with the Project Analyst and Operations.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Anti-Corruption Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, without supervisory responsibilities, in close cooperation with Programme, Operations, Communications and other teams in the Country Office (CO) for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery. The incumbent is expected to spend a large part of the working time with partner institutions rather than in the UNDP office. The 130 working days are planned with the Project Manager and scheduled around the partner institutions’ calendars and the project milestones. Two Anti-Corruption Analysts will be engaged. The Project Manager allocates the assigned activities between them at the start of the contract, so that the work proceeds in parallel and each has a clear focus.

He/she also will collaborate with the Project Analyst and the ICT Analyst of the project, other UNDP projects, National Anticorruption Center (CNA), National Integrity Authority (ANI), the network of integrity and ethics tutors and other national stakeholders. The Project Analyst leads project planning and budgeting, operational and procurement management, the results framework and donor reporting, and the organisation of events and knowledge products; the Anti-Corruption Analyst leads the technical substance and the relationships with national partners on which these depend, and provides the substantive inputs they require. The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies, as well as implementation of the effective internal control systems.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management - Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Management - Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development - Knowledge Facilitation

- Ability to animate individuals and communities of contributors to participate and share, particularly externally

- Equal Justice

- Gender Equality Strategy

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Law, Public Policy, Public Administration, Governance, Economics, Political or Social Sciences, or a related field relevant to the position is required; OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional 2 (two) years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with Master’s degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in the development, implementation, analysis, monitoring, or support of reforms, policies, programmes, or institutional processes related to justice, rule of law, anti-corruption, integrity, accountability, or related governance fields.

Required skills:
